description:

Not included from `bd init`: Codex and Cursor integrations, `AGENTS.md`, the `.agents/` skill, the reformatted `.claude/settings.json`, and `core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks` (it hid the jbcontext `post-commit` hook in `.git/hooks`).

## Test plan

title: Lab CSS: :where(.fw) button, no .fw prefixes, --touch and --rule
description:
## What

Refactor 5 of `lab-review.md`, scoped to the cascade and two tokens (no spacing scale, no font-size token). The breakpoint part was already done on `main` (every `max-height` query is 699, pinned to `band.ts` by `design/breakpoints.test.ts`).

- **Cascade.** `.fw button` becomes `:where(.fw) button`, specificity (0,0,1), so a bare class outranks it. The `.fw ` prefix, which 120 selectors carried only to outrank the reset, is removed. Comments that explained the prefix are gone; three that name a changed selector are corrected. `design/prefix.test.ts` fails on a new `.fw .x` selector. Root-scoped rules that are not the prefix tax (`.fw *`, `.fw :focus-visible`, the scrollbars, `.fw > main`, `.fw.menu-open …`) stay.
- **Tokens.** `--touch: 44px` (37 declarations: touch targets and the handle tracks that are targets) and `--rule: 1px solid var(--border)` (27). `--val-u`, the knob grid's unit column, keeps `44px`: it is a width, not a target. `tokens.test.ts` pins twenty tokens.
- **Touch test.** `design/touch.browser.test.tsx` reads the heights that `@media (pointer: coarse)` rules declare, as text (the runner cannot emulate a coarse pointer), so `var(--touch)` parsed as 0. Its two helpers now resolve a bare `var(--x)` through `:root`. With `--touch: 40px` its 19 cases fail, so it still checks the height.

## Evidence that nothing on screen changed

A one-off probe (not committed) fingerprinted every element's full computed style, with `::before` and `::after`, in the real `App`: six sizes (xl, l, m, s, low window, xs) × seven states (lab, palette, report, menu, simple, /boards, /docs), 28 436 elements; and, with transitions off, a hover on every visible control plus 80 Tab presses at three sizes × six states, 1 957 measurements. Compared with two baselines taken on `main`, both sets are identical. Two custom properties every element inherits from `:root` (the new tokens) are left out of the fingerprint, and React `useId` ids are normalised in element paths.

The probe does not reach `pointer: coarse` or `:active`. The one `:active` rule was checked by hand, and a separate static pass over all 600 rules at base and head (media rules included) found no pair whose precedence flips on an element they can both match.

## Left out

- A spacing scale and a font-size token (scope decision).
- `--rule` resolves `var(--border)` on `:root`, so a subtree that overrode `--border` would not change `var(--rule)`; nothing overrides it today.

## Checks

- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: 4 projects, 21 tasks, green (lab: 1414 tests).
- `deno task verify`: 557 passed.

title: Lab: drop the palette's outside-press exception for the ⌘K button
description:
## What

Removes the outside-press exception for the ⌘K button in `CommandPalette` ("Not the trigger…") and rewrites the trigger's comment in `shell/TopBar.tsx`.

## Why

While the palette is open, `.fw-scrim` (`position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 40`) covers the top bar at every band, so a press on the trigger never reaches it: it lands on the scrim, which closes the palette, and the click that follows reaches the scrim too, so nothing reopens it. The exception could not be reached by a mouse, and after #135 no test covered it.

## What guards it

The `LabLayout` case "a press where the ⌘K button sits closes the palette, and it stays closed" checks that the scrim is what lies under the trigger. Raising the top bar above the scrim (`.fw-top { z-index: 50 }`), the one change that would make the exception needed again, makes that case fail at its scrim assertion; checked by hand and reverted.

`TRIGGER_ID` stays: closing the palette still hands the focus back to the trigger.

## Checks

- Focused: palette, shell and `LabLayout` browser tests, 141 passed.
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: 4 projects, 21 tasks, green (lab: 1412 tests).
- `deno task verify`: 557 passed.

title: Lab tests: one stylesheet barrel, one store reset, one router mount
description:
## What

Refactor 7 of `lab-review.md`: the lab's browser tests get one stylesheet barrel, one store reset and one router mount.

- **One reset.** `resetApp` replaces the whole store with `useStore.getInitialState()`, then sets the four fields whose first value reads the browser (`lang.lang`, `ui.mode`, `ui.report`, `ui.settings`). The view and recipe slices, which leaked between cases before, are now put back too; a new store field needs no line in the reset. `Workspace.browser.test.tsx` loses its private `mountApp`. `harness/resetApp.browser.test.tsx` pins it.
- **One router mount.** `harness/renderAt.tsx` mounts a node at an address inside `MemoryRouter` and the `.fw` root; seven test files' local helpers use it. Hook wrappers and mounts without `.fw` stay as they are.
- **One stylesheet barrel.** `design/index.css` imports the eight sheets in the order `main.tsx` did; `main.tsx` and 25 tests import only it. A node guard, `design/index.test.ts`, fails if a sheet is left out of the barrel, if `main.tsx` imports anything else, or if a test imports a single sheet.
- **Stale restores.** Console.jump, Workspace and LayoutInvariants dropped the view restores and comments ("the view slice has no reset") that the new reset made untrue. One Workspace case now turns the highlight on, so its `top: 0` assertion can fail.

## One test changed meaning

With the full cascade, the open palette's `.fw-scrim` (`position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 40`) covers the top bar at every band, so the ⌘K trigger cannot be clicked while the palette is open. The old case "the ⌘K button closes the palette it opened" exercised a path the app does not have. It now asserts what the app does: a press where the trigger sits lands on the scrim, closes the palette, and the palette stays closed. Two negative controls were run: without `palette.css` the scrim assertion fails, and with the trigger reopening on `mouseup` the case fails.

## Left for a decision

- `CommandPalette`'s outside-press exception for the trigger ("Not the trigger…") is not reachable by a mouse while the scrim covers the trigger, and after this branch no test covers it. Removing it is a product change.
- The ⌘K trigger's `onClick` comment in `shell/TopBar.tsx` describes that exception.

## Measured before planning

Giving every test all eight sheets: 992 of 993 browser tests passed (the one failure is the ⌘K case above). Resetting through `getInitialState`: 993 of 993.

## Checks

- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: 4 projects, 21 tasks, green (lab: 1412 tests).
- `deno task verify`: 557 passed (includes the comment guard over `apps/lab/src`).

title: Lab prose: say what to do about the start-share and late-skeleton rules
description:
## What

A second pass over the lab texts #133 left alone, both languages. Two rule messages change:

**`startPair`**
- before: *arrow start and tunnel share do not fit together: a mixed start needs random start and a share of 0.3 to 0.7; any other start needs the share off (-1)*
- after: *arrow start and tunnel share clash: arrow start must be layers, random or tunnels, and a tunnel share (0.3 to 0.7) needs random start; otherwise the share must be off (-1)*

It now names the three starts, which also covers a fractional start such as `0.5` from a link.

**`giantWander`**
- before: *skeletons added later need straighter skeletons: above a later chance of 0.05, skeleton straightness must be at least 0.6 plus that chance*
- after: *too many late skeletons for how straight skeletons are: with late chance above 0.05, raise skeleton straightness to at least 0.6 + late chance, or boards get stuck*

It uses the row's own name (late chance), says which knob to raise and what happens otherwise.

The collapsed-block headers (`needsSkeleton`, `needsProbe`) keep their wording.

## How they were chosen

Two variants of each of the four texts were scored with Jev, twice, against the current ones, with the same description of where each text sits in the lab. Every difference but one stayed within Jev's run-to-run noise (0.04): these texts describe how one knob depends on another, so every variant has to name other knobs. The choice was made by reading the variants side by side, not by the score.

## Checks

- `deno task verify`: 557 passed
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify`: 4 projects, 21 tasks, green (lab: 1405 tests)
- EN/PL number parity and the glossary guard pass; no other file pins the old sentences.

title: Lab prose: explain the skeleton, rescue and rule texts
description:
## What

Rewrites 23 lab texts, English and Polish, that a player could not read without knowing the generator: the skeleton knobs, the "No effect" reasons, three rule messages, the "when stuck" group and three of its knobs, tail rework and the mixed start.

The glossary words stay (skeleton, run, run gap, coil penalty, target share). The texts now say what those words mean, or what happens:

- a run is a straight stretch of a skeleton, and a run cut short stops after 3 to 14 cells (`growSerpentine`);
- an inactive reason says why the knob is idle, instead of `needs skeletons > 0 …`;
- `stepZero` no longer prints as "No effect: no effect while …";
- a rule message says what would go wrong (medium and long arrows the same length, a board that gets stuck);
- `restarts` says it starts again on an empty board with a seed made from yours (`new Carver` per attempt).

Keys, flags, links and board ids are unchanged. The run-gap label does not start with "run", so the command palette still ranks Generate first for that query (`commands.test.ts`).

## How the texts were picked

A one-off Jev pass (TypeSafe System One, jev-1.13.0) asked three yes/no questions of every dictionary text (does a player get it first time, does it lean on an unexplained term, is it vague), with a note on where the text is shown in the lab. The worst-ranked texts were rewritten; five rewrites Jev did not score better were dropped.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| mean score, EN (lower = clearer) | 0.71 | 0.64 |
| mean score, PL | 0.66 | 0.60 |

Jev is not deterministic: scores move by up to 0.04 between runs, so only larger differences count. The score ranks texts; it does not prove the new ones read well. That is for a human to judge in the lab.

## Constraints kept

- `MAX_HELP` (170 characters) and the EN/PL number parity in `lab-i18n.test.ts`.
- The glossary guard (`glossary.test.ts`): no retired words.
- Pinned strings in `lab-i18n.test.ts`, `engine.test.ts` and `carve.test.ts` updated; the engine tests now read `RULE_REASONS.lmaxHole` instead of repeating it.

## Checks

- `deno task verify`: 557 passed
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify`: 4 projects, 21 tasks, green (lab: 1405 tests)

title: Lab: refactors 6, 8 and 9 — command figure, openStoredBoard, roving focus
description:
Refactors 6, 8 and 9 from `lab-review.md`. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-lab-refactors-6-8-9-design.md`; plan next to it.

**6. One command figure.** `run/CommandFigure.tsx` renders the caption, the Copy button (through `useCopy`) and the command. `LiveCommand`, `BoardColumn` and `FileColumn` use it; `BoardColumn` drops its own copy of the clipboard logic. The rendered DOM is unchanged, except that a board opened from disk now has Copy too. The export half of this refactor landed in #129.

**8. `openStoredBoard`.** `useStoredBoard`'s effect body moves, statement for statement, into `library/openStoredBoard.ts`. It returns the cancel of a read in flight and takes `read` as a parameter. The hook becomes one `useEffect`. `openStoredBoard.test.ts` runs its five exits and the races in the fast `node` project, including a late success and a late failure after the cancel and the A→B→A walk. The browser tests stay as the integration guard.

**9. One roving-focus helper.** `shell/roving.ts` has two parts:
- `nextIndex(key, current, count, { axis, wrap })`, used by `TabRow`, `GroupRail`, `BoardsRail`, `Segmented` and `CommandPalette`.
- `useFocusFollowsSelection(selection)`, used by the four strips. It focuses the selected item only when the selection changes. The inline ref callbacks it replaces refocused on every render while a strip held the focus.

`PresetStrip`'s 2-D grid stays as it is.

**Behaviour changes**, each pinned by a test that was red before its change:
- `FileColumn` has Copy.
- `BoardsRail` with nothing selected: ↑ goes to Preview, the last entry. Before, it went to the one before it.
- `CommandPalette` with no hits leaves ↑ ↓ Home End to the input.

`TabRow` gets its first test that the focus follows the selection.

Gate: `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache` green in a clean worktree at the branch head.

title: Jev guards: advisory hooks for the comment, message and dictionary rules
description:
Advisory Claude Code hooks that ask Jev (TypeSafe's System One model) whether new text breaks a written rule of this repository, and report it through `additionalContext` without ever blocking. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-jev-guards-design.md`; setup and figures: `docs/jev-guards.md`.

- **Comment guard (on).** After an `Edit` or `Write` under `apps/` or `packages/`, each new comment block of at most six lines (and each trailing comment) is asked `violates`, `history` and `spec_ref` against the `## Comments` section of `CLAUDE.md`. On the comment sweep's before/after labels: precision 0.985, recall 0.525, false alarms 0.5 % (in-sample).
- **Message guard (on).** Before `git commit` and `gh pr create|edit`, attribution lines are caught by a regex and "is this English" is Jev's `not_english` at 0.8. A Polish-letter regex was tried and dropped: the repository may quote the Polish dictionary, and it flagged 14 of 360 real messages. Held out from the data that picked 0.8: 756 commits since the English-only rule (5e17f97) and 54 older PRs, false alarms 0.0 %, detection 100 %.
- **Dictionary guard (hook off).** Pairs every English source text (`EN`, `PARAM_SPEC`, the reasons) with its Polish translation and asks whether they say the same; runs by hand with `deno task jev i18n`.
- **Silence as the contract.** A missing key, a locked 1Password mount (the key file is a FIFO), an HTTP error or a slow answer ends as exit 0 with no output; the key is read only when a guard has a question, so an ordinary edit costs one `deno run` (about 60–110 ms). Nothing runs inside `deno task test` or CI: every test stubs the judge.
- **Measurement kept in the repo.** `deno task jev:eval comments|message|i18n` re-measures a guard; any change to a question, a threshold or the pinned model `jev-1.13.0` requires it. The message hold-out is anchored where its threshold was picked, so new commits and PRs never leak into it.
- **Shared extractor.** `commentLines`, `commentBlocks`, `MAX_BLOCK` and `MAX_HEADER` move from `comments.test.ts` to `packages/engine/comment-lines.ts` (Deno export only; not emitted to `dist`), so both comment guards agree on what a block is.

Needs the key mounted from 1Password at `~/.config/arrowz/typesafe.env` (see the docs); without it the hooks are silent.

Gates: `deno task verify` green (552 tests), `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` green (21 tasks).

title: Lab: leftovers after Stop-and-open and seed series
description:
Four leftovers from the Stop-and-open and seed-series work.

- **⌘K preset rows during a normal run.** The rows were off whenever anything ran, while `applyPreset` refuses only a series and `PresetStrip` keeps its buttons on during a normal run (a new run replaces it). The rows now follow the same rule; Generate, New seed and Check seeds still use `inFlight`. New case in `commands.test.ts` (red before the fix).
- **Polish series head.** It counts boards, so every word is plural: `Pełne: 3 z 5 · niepełne 1 · nierozwiązywalne 0 · przerwane 0`. English unchanged.
- **Import cycle.** `BOARD_COLUMN_ID` moves to `library/boardColumnId.ts`, so `FileColumn` no longer imports `BoardColumn`, which renders it.
- **SVG export in one place.** `run/drawSvg.ts` becomes `run/useSvgDrawing.ts`: a hook that owns the worker, `busy` and the teardown on unmount. `ExportButtons` uses it, and the library's two columns share `library/SavedExports.tsx` (the More menu's two buttons and the drawing's error), passing only the options, read at the click, and the names. Behaviour is unchanged; dropping `setBusy(false)` in the hook fails three `ExportButtons` tests.

Gate: `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` green (21 tasks).

title: Lab: check the knobs on N seeds
description:
Piece E of item 4 ("Parity gaps") in `lab-review.md`: Gap 3, the closing rate over N seeds — the last piece of item 4. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-lab-seed-series-design.md`; plan with its dry-run errata: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-29-lab-seed-series.md`.

## What it does

"Check seeds" runs the knobs on screen over seeds `seed … seed + N − 1` (N default 20, 2–200) and reports "Complete on X of N · incomplete · unsolvable · stopped", the means of the complete seeds (arrows, longest, time), and a button per seed that was not complete which reopens it as a normal run under the series' own knobs. The board on screen does not change and nothing is stored. Advanced view only.

## How

- Engine: `SeedRun`, `seedRunOf` (aborted → stopped, deadlock → unsolvable, ok → complete, else incomplete — a deadlock is `ok: false` in `generate()`), `summariseSeries` (means over complete seeds only, as `report.ts` does), and a `seed` → `seedDone` worker message with numbers only, no board file.
- Pool (`useSeries`): `min(N, cores − 1, 4)` workers (a 1000×1000 seed holds ~390 MB, measured), seeds handed out from a queue, one shared stop flag; first Stop keeps answered seeds and marks running ones stopped, second Stop terminates; the pool is terminated at the end.
- One gate in `useRun`: a normal run never starts during a series (auto-generate included); knob writers (`[`/`]`, presets, pasted command, Load into lab) refuse during a series; Abort stops whichever runs.
- UI: a "Check seeds" row with a count field and meter in the run column's "…" group, a ⌘K row, a "Seeds" section in the report drawer ("for other settings" after a knob edit, the failure shown when a series cannot run), the status line during a series. EN and PL.

## Verification

- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` 25/25, engine `deno task verify` 499 at the head; `worker-smoke` checks the built worker's `seed` answer.
- Dry run of the plan before execution (it caught the deadlock mapping), per-task reviews, a whole-branch review whose findings are fixed in the last five commits.
- Live pass in Chrome on a copy of the store: 200×200 × 20 seeds in 2.3 s; 1000×1000 with Stop mid-series; `]` refused during a series; a stopped seed reopened as a run; Polish strings; no store writes from a series. Incomplete seeds could not be provoked live (every board filled); that path is covered by tests.

Known leftovers: the ⌘K preset rows are now disabled during a normal run while the preset strip's chips are not; the Polish head line "Pełna na 3 z 5" could read "Pełne: 3 z 5".

title: Lab: Stop keeps the partial board, and a .board.json opens from disk
description:
Piece D of item 4 ("Parity gaps") in `lab-review.md`: Gap 6 (Stop that keeps the partial board) and Gap 8 (open a `.board.json` from disk). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-28-lab-stop-and-open-design.md`; plan with its dry-run errata: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-lab-stop-and-open.md`.

## Stop keeps the board

- The worker's `trace` reads a one-element `Int32Array` over a `SharedArrayBuffer` and throws `GenerateAbort` when it is 1; the engine's existing abort path hands back the board laid so far as a normal `done`, now carrying `aborted`.
- The lab is cross-origin isolated (COOP `same-origin`, COEP `require-corp` on Vite's server and preview, and on the Vitest browser project); `isolation.browser.test.ts` guards it. Without isolation Stop terminates as before.
- First Stop: "Stopping…", the button becomes "Discard"; the next `done` shows "Stopped — the arrows laid so far". A second Stop discards (the way out of the metrics step, which does not call `trace`).
- A stopped board is shown, never stored, never a delta baseline, and its report shows no deltas.
- `worker-smoke.mjs` checks the built worker stops on the flag at 400×400 with fewer arrows than a whole run.

## Open a board file

- `readBoardFiles` (pure): one `.board.json`, optionally with its meta; the meta is kept only when its id is the board's layout hash, so a renamed pair opens and a foreign meta is refused.
- `result.preview` is a union `origin: 'store' | 'file'`; the file preview lives at `/boards/file`, never reaches a store write or delete, and every reader (stage, column, report, Preview panel, status line) handles both.
- Three ways in, one hidden input: an "Open file…" button on the saved boards, a file drop on the stage, a ⌘K row.
- With its meta: the command, Load into lab, the view rows (local only). Without: facts (file name, layout hash), exports and a hint.
- Failures read on the library line in both languages ("it is not JSON", "the meta file belongs to another board", …).

## Verification

- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` 25/25, `deno task verify` 494 at the head.
- Dry run of the plan before execution; per-task reviews; a whole-branch review whose findings (a stored board left drawn at `/boards/file` after Back, weak tests, SVG voids for a meta-less file, label case, deltas on a stopped board) are fixed in the last five commits.
- Live pass in Chrome on a copy of the store: Stop at 1000×1000 (partial board, no store write), double Stop, file + meta, file alone by drop, bad files, Back from a stored board, Polish strings, ⌘K row. The real store was untouched.

Note: a lab tab loaded before this change may come from the HTTP cache without the new headers; one hard reload makes it isolated.

title: Lab: paste a carve command into ⌘K
description:
Part C of item 4 ("parity gaps") in `lab-review.md`, Gap 1: the lab prints the command that reproduces what is configured, and now reads one back.

## What changes

- **Paste into ⌘K.** A query that starts with `deno task carve` (a terminal prompt `$` and `NAME=value` environment words in front are fine), or with a flag that has a value or a second token, puts the palette in command mode: one row, "Load this command", showing the board (`30×40 · seed 5`, "drawn at random" under `--randomized`) and the mode flags the lab ignores (`--svg`, `--count`). A lone flag such as `--seed` is still a search for its knob.
- **Loading** sets the knobs (the same pinned draw the CLI does), the whole view with the look, and the simple view's recipe, all on the machine path; a line with pinned knobs switches to the advanced view; then exactly one run starts (`control.start()`, never `generate()`, which would redraw over the pins).
- **Problems in the page's language.** A line the parser refuses gives a disabled row and every problem listed under it, in Polish or English.
- **Engine.** `splitCommand` reads a pasted line the way a shell would: both quote kinds, a backslash before whitespace joins lines (the text input turns pasted newlines into spaces), and the prefix, prompt and environment words are dropped. The parser's refusals are typed `ArgProblem`s, and the CLI's English `errors` are built from them, byte for byte as before. `drawOf` is the pinned draw `carve.ts` did by hand, and the CLI now uses it.
- `viewFieldsOf` is shared by this loader and the library's "Load into lab"; `recipe.apply` writes a whole recipe without counting an edit.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-28-lab-paste-command-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-lab-paste-command.md`.

## Verification

- `deno task verify`: 494 passed (the CLI's refusal-text tests unchanged). `pnpm nx run-many -t verify`: 4 projects green.
- Browser tests paste through the real clipboard, including a multi-line command, and round-trip the lab's own command with quoted colours, with exactly one run.
- Live pass in Chrome, on a copy of the store: a terminal line (`$ ARROWZ_BOARDS_DIR=… deno task carve … --pstraight=0.9 --palette='…' --svg`) loads, switches the simple view to advanced and carves once; a broken line lists five Polish problems; a multi-line `--randomized` line reads "losowo"; `--seed` alone still finds the seed knob.

title: Lab: the report's missing rows, the delta as direction, and the colour fields in ⌘K
description:
Part B of item 4 ("parity gaps") in `lab-review.md`: the report shows what the engine already measures, its delta colour says only which way a number moved, and ⌘K reaches every colour and element field of the Preview panel.

## What changes

- **The delta is the direction.** `reportDelta(num, prev)` returns `up` / `down`; `StatRow.better` is gone. Green = up, red = down in the table and the summary, and a screen reader hears "up"/"down". What a rise means is the last sentence of each row's `?` help ("Higher = harder.", "Lower = faster."), audited for every row with a number and pinned by a test.
- **Nine new report rows.** `blocked from afar` (T2), `turns per cell`, `touching itself`, `neighbours of a long arrow`, and a sixth group "generator in detail": `tail reworks` (the `backbite` knob's effect; a dash with the knob off), `what stopped them`, `length when stuck`, `stuck on themselves`, `shortened`. The lengths row starts with the shortest–longest range. Every row is always present, so the index-keyed deltas never shift; the carver rows describe the last attempt.
- **The not-filled status line** names how many of the 2 × (W + H) edge places a new arrow could still start in.
- **⌘K rows** for the margin, dot colour, dot size, theme, background, arrow colour, highlight colour and palette. The palette's add button gets the id the jump needs; at the cap the jump lands on the first colour.
- `lab-review.md` statuses and the spec's two deliberate deviations (the unset-colour word, the short `shortened` label).

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-28-lab-report-parity-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-lab-report-parity.md`.

## Verification

- `deno task verify`: 477 passed. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify`: 4 projects green.
- Live pass in Chrome, Polish and English, on a copy of the store: two runs (`backbite` 0 → 3) show the new rows, green/red deltas and no overflow in the drawer; ⌘K jumps land on their controls (including an empty and a full palette, and the dot colour with the dots off). The not-filled line could not be reproduced live (900 seeds at the weakest knobs all filled); the engine formatter test and a browser status-bar test cover it.

title: View look parity: theme, colours, dot grid and margin through the command
description:
The first slice of item 4 in `lab-review.md` ("colour flags in the CLI and points and `pad` in the SVG", Gap 7). The lab's live command now reproduces the picture the lab exports. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-28-view-look-parity-design.md`; plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-view-look-parity.md`.

## Changes

- **The look moves into the engine.** A new neutral `packages/engine/look.ts` holds the themes, `resolveColours`, the default colours, `DEFAULT_PAD` (4), the point-grid defaults, `PAD_RANGE`, `POINT_RADIUS_RANGE`, `PALETTE_CAP` (8) and `isHexColour` (`#rrggbb`). `@arrowz/board-element` re-exports the same names, so its public API does not change. The theme tests moved with them.
- **`toSvg` draws a margin and the point grid.** `SvgOptions` gains `pad` (cells, absent = 1) and `points` (one `<pattern>` and one `<rect>` over the cells, a dot in each cell centre, as the element's shader places it). Called without them, `toSvg` draws the same bytes as before: `svg-golden.json` is unchanged.
- **`View` carries the look.** Nine fields: `theme`, `palette`, `paper`, `ink`, `highlight`, `pad`, `showPoints`, `pointColor`, `pointRadius`. `''` means "not stated", so the theme shows through. `svgOptions(view)` resolves them the way the element does (stated > theme > default).
- **CLI flags.** `--theme`, `--palette`, `--paper`, `--ink`, `--highlight-color`, `--pad`, `--points`, `--point-color`, `--point-radius`. A bad value is refused with the flag's name. `buildCommand` prints them after `--sharp`, and `parseArgs(buildCommand(p, v)).view` equals `v` (pinned over every theme and the range ends). Colour values are single-quoted, because in zsh with `extended_glob` a bare `#` is a glob operator and the pasted command failed with "no matches found".
- **The store** checks the look fields on POST, each optional, and stores colours lower-case. Metas saved before this change read with the default look through `fillView`; no file is rewritten.
- **The lab.** `viewOf` carries the look through a new `lookOf`, so the live command, the save after each run and both SVG exports carry it. `exportColours` is gone. In the library, colour stays a viewing preference: a stored board's preview and its SVG draw its saved shape in the lab's current look. "Load into lab" now restores the stored look along with the shape.
- **Visible change for everyone:** an SVG from the CLI now has a 4-cell margin by default, as the lab draws it on screen, instead of 1. The README pictures were rebuilt (margin only, checked by script), and both READMEs document the new flags.

## Verification

- `deno task verify`: 471 passed. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: 4 projects, 21 tasks, green. Both were run in a clean worktree at the head.
- Live pass in Chrome, with the lab on a copy of the store: a 30×20 board with `gruvbox-dark`, a custom ink, a palette, colours on, top 3, points and `pad` 6. I exported the SVG from the lab and ran the copied live command in `zsh -c "setopt extended_glob; …"` with `--svg=`. `cmp` says the two files are identical (16 069 bytes).
- The plan was dry-run before execution, and each task was reviewed on a different model from its author. The whole-branch review traced the lab and CLI SVG paths by execution. Each Review Focus item in the plan was checked with a mutation.
- One lab browser test failed once, unnamed, in 1 of 7 full runs. It did not reproduce in the other 6.

title: Engine: close the envelope leaks at 1000×1000
description:
Twelve legal settings never filled a board at 600 and 1000 a side (9 of 400 at 1000, 3 of 200 at 600, none at 100–300). The measurements are in `docs/superpowers/measurements/2026-09-27-envelope-leaks.md`, carried over from the unmerged `engine/loops` branch. This PR ships the two fixes they led to.

## `giantWander`: skeletons added mid-run need straighter skeleton arrows

- New rule: when `wGiant` > 0.05, `giantStraight` ≥ 0.6 + `wGiant`.
- Ten of the twelve failing sets had `wGiant` 0.2 with `giantStraight` 0.5. Setting either knob back to its default fixed every one of them.
- Measured clean edge at 1000×1000:

  | `wGiant` | clean from | one step below |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0.1 | 0.7 | failed |
  | 0.15 | 0.75 | failed |
  | 0.2 | 0.8 | failed |

  `envelope.test.ts` pins these edges.
- The rule refuses no golden board, no preset and no lab-simple draw, because randomize keeps `giantStraight` at 0.94.
- `giantStraightFloor` is exported beside `straightFloor`.
- The reason is written in EN/PL, and both READMEs gain a row in the rule table. The `wGiant` help no longer warns that 1000×1000 may not fill.
- The lab's skeleton straightness slider now shows the bound as a mark and as "Minimum for this board".

## `straightFloor`: the `anticoil` ≤ 4 discount goes from 0.8 to 0.9

- At 1000×1000 with `anticoil` 4, today's floor of 0.7 failed 5 of 60 runs. At 0.75, all 60 closed.
- The floor stays the same for every side up to 600. At 800 it rises from 0.65 to 0.7, and at 1000 from 0.7 to 0.75.

## Costs

- The round-14 cell `1000/0.72/5/4` closed three runs out of three and is now refused. It is listed in `CONSERVATIVE`.
- The simple view's 1000×1000 board at shape 0.75 moves from straightness 0.72 to 0.75. It is the only one of the 60 size and shape positions that changes.
- A stored board saved with `wGiant` > 0.05 and a lower `giantStraight` than the new bound will show a violation when loaded.
- Measured at 800×800, `anticoil` 4: 0/60 at the new floor 0.7 with no restarts; the old 0.65 also filled, with 6 restarts.

## Verification

- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify`: green.
- Checked with a mutation: relaxing the rule's base from 0.6 to 0.55 fails the edge test.

title: Lab follow-ups: Nx test inputs, slot docs, deferred review minors
description:
Follow-ups after #120 and the deferred minors of item 6 in `lab-review.md`.

## Changes

- **Nx `engine:test` inputs.** `lab-docs.test.ts`, `comments.test.ts` and `neutral.test.ts` read `packages/board-element/src`, `apps/lab/src` and `packages/cli/*.ts`, none of which was an input, so a change there left a stale cached result. Before: appending a line to `arrowz-board.ts` gave a 1/1 cache hit. After: it gives 0/1, and so does a change to a lab stylesheet.
- **Slots on `/docs/element`.** A fourth table lists the seven slots with EN/PL descriptions, under a lead about `slot` and `data-board-action`. The navigation gains the section. An engine guard compares the `<slot name>` elements of `arrowz-board.ts` with `ELEMENT_SLOTS` both ways; renaming the `fit` slot turns it red.
- **⌘K ranking.** A query found at the start of a word now outranks one found inside a word, so "top" lists "how many longest" above Abort (whose hidden text is "stop").
- **Form field ids.** The palette input (`cmd-input`) and the `DraftNumber` entry (`<row>-entry`, a required prop via `rowIds`) now have ids, since Chrome flags fields with neither an id nor a name. There is no `name`, so autofill has nothing to key suggestions on.
- **`willReadFrequently`** on the one-pixel colour probe in `gl-color.ts`.
- **Copy.** A blocker with no gap now reads "right in front" / "tuż przed grotem" instead of "at 0 cells". The traps help says what "normal" does, and gives "3 to 8 times fewer" as digits so the Polish text can carry the same numbers within the 170-character cap.
- **Short-window rules: no change, now pinned.** The two `max-height: 699px` rules have no `min-width: 768px`, and that is correct. With the floor added, 375×540 and 740×360 break frame-overlap, scroll and board-clip. A 375×540 case passes on the current rules and fails with the floor added.
- **Flaky test hardened.** "deleting cancels a view edit…" failed once under a loaded verify run: two Playwright clicks took longer than the 350 ms debounce, so the edit was saved before the delete. It now uses DOM clicks and asserts the invariant itself, no POST after DELETE. With `cancelPendingSave` commented out, it still fails.

The report drawer covering the board's right 45 px at 1440×877 stays open, deferred.

## Verification

- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify`: green (4 projects, 21 tasks).
- Each behaviour change has a case that fails without it. The guards were checked with mutations: the slot rename, the width floor, and removing `cancelPendingSave`.

title: Lab correctness 2: SVG colours, per-board view saves, worker, downloads, Load into lab runs
description:
Item 2 of `lab-review.md`'s "What is still open" (the smaller correctness items), plus a reported bug: "Load into lab" did not show the loaded board until a reload.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-28-lab-correctness-2-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-lab-correctness-2.md`

## What changes

- **The SVG export carries the lab's colours.** `SvgOptions` gains `paper`, `ink`, `highlight` and `palette`; absent fields keep today's bytes (golden SVGs and fingerprints unchanged). `assignPalette` moves into the engine (`packages/engine/palette.ts`), so the SVG and the board element colour each piece from one assignment. The element's colour precedence becomes `resolveColours(theme, stated)`, which the lab's exports reuse. The "theme not included" note is gone. Jam strips take the highlight, as on screen. A highlight equal to the ink (`ayu-light`) still draws the highlighted pieces.
- **A view save keeps `aborted`.** The store keeps a stored flag when a save carries none; a fresh lab run now states `aborted: false`.
- **Pending view saves are per board.** Editing or deleting board B no longer drops board A's pending write.
- **The generator worker.** A message from a replaced worker is ignored; a worker that fails (e.g. a chunk 404) is dropped, so the next run builds a new one instead of hanging in "running".
- **Downloads** revoke the object URL after 40 s (FileSaver.js's delay) instead of during the click.
- **"Load into lab" starts one run** on the loaded knobs (`control.start()`, not `generate()`, which would redraw the knobs in the simple view with randomising on).

## Verification

- `deno task verify` 437/0; `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache` 21/21 — on the branch and on the branch merged with current `main` (#120).
- Every fix has a test that is red without it and a named mutation that turns it red.
- SVG download from the drawing worker's callback fired in Playwright 1.63's WebKit and Firefox 155 (Chromium as control). Safari itself is unchecked.
- Live pass in Chrome on a store copy: gruvbox-dark SVG has the theme's paper and ink; a 3-colour palette with a dark paper splits 42/42/42 and matches the screen; Load into lab shows 25×25 · seed 657297 without a reload.

## Decisions worth a look

- Jam strips in the SVG now use the highlight (the spec first said "stay pink"; the element draws them in the highlight, so pink would have been the one mismatch).
- One view-save timer per layout hash, not per recipe: two recipes of one layout edited within 350 ms still share a timer (accepted in the spec).
- `BoardFrame` and `exportColours` each map `''` to "not set"; left as two sites because `BoardFrame` memoises the palette separately.

title: Board element: controls through slots, with the defaults as fallback content
description:
## What

`<arrowz-board>` takes its controls from the host through named slots; its own hint and buttons become slot fallback content, drawn only where the host supplies nothing (spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-28-board-controls-slots-design.md`, plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-board-controls-slots.md`).

- **Slots**: `controls` (the whole bar, position included) holds `hint`, `zoom-in`, `zoom-out`, `fit`, `colors` (with `enableColors`) and `gestures` (with `interactive` or `play`) in its fallback. A custom `controls` switches the per-control slots off. Under a coarse pointer the `hint` and `gestures` slots hide, projected content included.
- **One click path**: `data-board-action` (`zoom-in`, `zoom-out`, `fit`, `colors`, `gestures`) on any projected element, at any depth; the default buttons carry the same attribute and lose their own `@click`. A board nested in the host's content keeps its clicks to itself.
- **State on host controls**: `aria-pressed` and `hidden` on projected `colors`/`gestures` controls, kept in step from `updated()`, from a `MutationObserver` (nodes a framework adds deep inside a bar) and on connect.
- **Public API**: `toggleColors()`, `toggleGestures()` (availability checks moved into them, so code, default and host controls obey one rule), the `colored` getter, and a `gestures-change` event. Documented in the README and in `lab-docs.ts` (EN and PL).
- **Projected content next to the canvas**: a projected bar is `position: relative` so an unpositioned one paints above the canvas; the board keys `+ − 0` ignore text fields and nested boards in the projected content, and keep working from a focused host button.

## Behaviour

With no projected content the element is unchanged: every existing test passes with no assertion edited. The lab and the demo are not touched.

## Verification

- At `e4c558b`: `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache` (4 projects, 21 tasks) and `deno task verify` in `packages/engine` (421 passed) green.
- Four tasks, each reviewed; every new test (26 in `controls.browser.test.ts`) has a mutation check that turned it red; whole-branch review, its fixes re-reviewed. Keys and pointer tests use real input through `userEvent`; the coarse-pointer test uses CDP touch emulation.
- Not done: a live pass in Chrome with a real mouse.

## Follow-ups

- `engine:test` does not list `packages/board-element/src/arrowz-board.ts` among its Nx inputs although `lab-docs.test.ts` reads it, so a cached run can replay a stale verdict (Nx reports it as a flaky task).
- Slot rows on the lab's `/docs` page.

title: Lab hotkeys and dismiss: one key table, one useDismiss, side effects out of App
description:
## What

title: Lab row shell: one RowShell for every knob row, one id rule, rows out of ViewPanel
description:
## What

title: Lab view schema: one table for the view, view.apply(), links and metas without a version
description:
## What

PR 1 of three stacked structural refactors of the lab (spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-lab-structural-refactors-design.md`, plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-26-lab-view-schema.md`). Refactor 3 of `lab-review.md`.

- `apps/lab/src/state/viewSchema.ts`: `ViewFields` is the one list of the view's 18 fields; `VIEW_SCHEMA` (a mapped type over it) holds each field's default and reader, the only place a view value is validated. `readView`, `readPatch`, `pickView`, `VIEW_DEFAULTS` derive from it.
- `view.apply(patch)` writes a view patch in one store update; the setters read through the schema (`setNumber` stays on `viewNumberOf`, so an emptied "top" field still gives the CLI's 0).
- The link is a full view snapshot read by the schema; `applyPayload` is one `view.apply`.
- "Load into lab" applies the stored view in one update and leaves the page's colours, points, margin and voids alone.
- `console/viewFields.ts`: one `VIEW_ROWS` table for the view's numbers and flags replaces four; `fieldOf` is gone.
- `VIEW_VERSION` and `BoardMeta.viewVersion` leave the engine and the CLI store; `readMeta` still fills missing fields.

## Intended behaviour changes

There are no production links or boards, so backward compatibility was dropped on purpose:

1. A link field that is missing or unreadable opens on its default, not on the page's current value.
2. The old link keys `hilite`, `highlight` and `help` are ignored.
3. A head height of 0 is literal, in a link and in a stored meta.
4. A link always carries the palette and the colours.
5. A link and "Load into lab" notify store subscribers once for the view.

Accepted side effects: the setters normalise what they are given (never sent by the UI); the hash's key order changes, so Back onto an entry the old encoder wrote restarts a carve once.

## Verification

- Clean worktree at `4c79a92`: `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache` (4 projects, 21 tasks) and `deno task verify` (421 passed) green.
- Every browser test outside the link contract passed without assertion edits.
- Plan dry-run executed before implementation; six tasks each reviewed; whole-branch review, fixes re-reviewed.
- Live pass in Chrome on a copy of the store: a link opens every field; a link naming only `W` opens the view on its defaults; Back restores the previous entry byte for byte; Load into lab keeps the page's theme, palette, paper and margin; no console errors.

title: Own cells on the ray block unless the tail has left in time
description:
## What

A piece's own cell on its corridor used to be skipped unconditionally. Now it
blocks unless the tail has left it by the time the head arrives.

The body follows the head's track, so cell `k` of a piece of length `n` clears
after `n - k` steps. The head may enter it on that step at the earliest: the
snake move into the square the tail is leaving. Arriving earlier would run the
piece into itself.

- `ownCellClears` (`packages/engine/geometry.ts`) carries the rule; it lives
  there because `game.ts` imports `engine.ts` and both apply it.
- `play()` bounces a piece off itself (`blockerId` = its own id). `GameHost`
  handles that as any bounce: a life lost and a shake.
- `analyse()` records the self-loop, which Kahn never frees, so such a board
  reports unsolvable. The legacy rigid-translation branch is untouched: there
  the own cells move with the shape.

## Why no board changes

The generator picks the first uncarved cell of a line as the head, so a ray
only crosses cells carved before the piece and a body never lies on its own
ray. Every generated board passes under both rules; the fingerprints hold.
Teaching the generator to carve such hooks is a separate, larger change.

## Verification

- Three cases in `game.test.ts`: the snake move (equality) exits, a curl that
  meets its own body one step early bounces, and `analyse` agrees with `play`.
- Mutations, each red: `>=` to `>`, `n - 1 - k` instead of `n - k`, `analyse`
  skipping own cells, `play` skipping own cells.
- `deno task verify`: 409 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: 21 tasks green.

title: Lab glossary: one word per concept across knobs, view panel, statuses, presets, CLI help and READMEs
description:
The third PR of the lab's copy pass (A: report, #112; B: simple view, #113). Stacked on #113.

A player now reads one word per concept, in English and Polish, everywhere the lab, the board element, the CLI's help and the READMEs speak: **arrow** (not piece / line / element), **complete** and **stuck** (not closed / jammed), **skeleton** (not giants), **target length** (not probe), **run gap**, **coil penalty**, **background** and **arrow colour** (not paper and ink), **dot grid**, **cells**. Keys, flags, links, stored metas and board hashes do not change.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-lab-glossary-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-lab-glossary.md`.

## What changes

- **Knob texts** (`PARAM_TABLE`, `PL.params`, short labels, groups, the start control, inactive reasons, rules, violation messages). No help warns about a value its slider cannot reach any more; a new test in `lab-i18n.test.ts` refuses a threshold outside the knob's own range. The trap help states the measured factors (seek 25–60% more, avoid a third to an eighth as many).
- **View panel, statuses, saved boards' list** ("Board complete: every cell filled.", "120 arrows", "Arrow #3 · … · free").
- **Mechanisms:** `EN_CHOICES` lets English show a display word (`trapBias` off → "normal") while the command keeps `--trapbias=off`; special-value chips are translated ("losowo"); five non-inflecting units (`×`, `× side` / `× bok`, `strz.`); the head width and head length each get their own help (a length of 0 draws a flat end, checked against `pieceShape`).
- **Preset panel:** a caption says levels set the size only; each mode describes itself (`title` + `aria-describedby`); the trigger reads "Easy · tall".
- **Board element** strings: "⌘-click an arrow", "Arrow colours".
- **CLI help** (`--help` and `--help=knobs`) and **READMEs** (both word lists follow the lab's words).
- **Guard:** `packages/engine/glossary.test.ts` refuses the retired words in every dictionary leaf, the knob texts, the reasons and the CLI help, naming the key.

## Beyond copy: the annotation strip

The plan's dry run found that a shorter rule text made the frame taller and slid a 25×50 board 3 px under its annotation at 375×812: the board's margin is in cells, so no margin holds a fixed-height label at a small cell size. `.fw-board` now reserves a strip (`--fw-strip`, 30 px, 44 px on touch) painted `--void`, which the annotation and the solo toggle sit in. This also closes "What is still open" item 7 (pad 0). Solo-mode tests read the strip's height from the page.

## Verification

- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` green (4 projects, 21 tasks); engine and CLI `deno task verify` 423/423; lab 1211 tests.
- Live pass in Chrome, EN and PL, 1440×900 and 375×812 touch: every group's labels and units whole, choice words and chips, preset caption, trigger and descriptions, the strip at 30 and 44 px under a dark theme, the element's words, the status line and the saved list. Not exercised live: an incomplete board's status line.
