title: Simple view: the size rows show the size Generate carves
description:
Fixes the first item of "What is still open" in `lab-review.md` (MEDIUM: in the simple view the size rows show the recipe, while Generate carves the knobs).

## Decision

The width and height rows in the simple view now read the knobs (`params.values`), which is what Generate carves and what the top bar shows. A preset, a link or Load into lab moves the knobs past the recipe; before this change the rows kept showing the recipe (25×50 beside a 1000×1000 board). Switching views overwrites nothing. The two sliders and the skeleton switch still show the recipe, because they cannot be read back from the knobs.

A size edit writes **both** sides into the recipe through a new `recipe.setSize(W, H)` (one debounced edit), then applies the recipe. Without that, typing a width would move the other side to the recipe's value (1000 → 50).

## Tests

- The test from `5060154` that pinned the old behaviour is inverted: a knob moved behind the panel shows in the row.
- New: with the knobs at 1000×1000, typing width 900 leaves height 1000 in the row, the recipe and the knobs, as one edit, with no run started.
- New: `setSize` clamps both sides and counts one edit.

All three failed before the change.

## Verification

- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` green without the Nx cache (4 projects, 21 tasks).
- Live pass in Chrome on a scratch store: advanced view, the 1000×1000 preset, then Simple, shows 1000 / 1000; typing width 900 gives rows 900 / 1000, top bar `900×1000`, command `--width=900 --height=1000`.

title: Lab correctness: view version in links and stored metas, redirects keep the hash, palette keeps its keys, decimal comma, Polish strings
description:
Fixes item 1 of `lab-review.md` → "What is still open" (lab correctness). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-lab-correctness-design.md`; plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-lab-correctness.md`.

## What changes

- **View version.** `VIEW_VERSION = 2` in `@arrowz/engine/command`. It is written as `viewVersion` into the link's `__view` and into a stored `BoardMeta`. A view that carries any numeric version reads by the new rules: a missing colour means none, and a head height of 0 is literal. A view without the field (every link and meta written before) reads exactly as it did.
  - A link can now clear the page's theme, palette, paper, ink and highlight colour.
  - A head height of 0 survives the link, the store's `fillView` and a reload.
  - `voids` travels in the link.
  - An unknown theme name is dropped (`themeOf`).
- **Redirects keep the hash.** `KeepHashNavigate` replaces the three `<Navigate>` redirects, so a link under a wrong path (`/x#…`, `/docs#…`) opens on its knobs.
- **Command palette.** A press inside the frame no longer takes the focus from the search input, and a native frame `keydown` listener stops keys from reaching the page's hotkeys (Escape closes the palette, anything else refocuses the input). This way `g` does not carve and Escape does not close the drawer behind the palette.
- **Decimal comma.** `DraftNumber` gets a `decimal` prop. With it, a comma reads as the decimal point, and only in fractional fields: `1,000` in the width still commits nothing.
- **Polish UI.** The palette's flag values come from the dictionary (`wł.`/`wył.`). `BoardError.reason: string | null`, where `null` is worded at render time as `boardNotStored`, so a language switch rewords it.

## Tests

Each new case was run before its fix and failed on the assertion the plan names. Each production condition has a mutation that turns its case red. The legacy cases that pinned the old reading were kept and moved onto hand-written legacy links and metas, so they still test old links.

- `deno task verify`: green.
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: green in a clean worktree (4 projects, 21 tasks).
- Live pass in Chrome, PL, 1920 px:
  - an old link under `/no-such-page` opens a 44-wide board at `/`;
  - Back after a pasted themed link restores `theme: ''`, and the entry is not rewritten;
  - a head height of 0 survives a reload, a save (`viewVersion: 2` on disk) and "Load into lab";
  - `0,35` sets 0.35, and `1,000` in the width changes nothing;
  - ⌘K over the open report drawer: after a click on the disabled Abort row, `g` goes to the search box and starts no carve, Escape closes only the palette, and text selection in the input still works;
  - a missing board shows the Polish sentence, which rewords on a switch to EN.

## Notes for review

- "Versioned" means "has a numeric `viewVersion`", not `>= VIEW_VERSION`, so a later bump to 3 does not turn version-2 links and metas into legacy ones. This deliberately adds no second exported constant.
- Left as known minors: a bare 400 ms wait in the Back test (tied to `WRITE_DELAY_MS`); no test that the encoder writes `voids: true` explicitly (absent reads as true anyway); ⌘K pressed while the focus sits on a row by code is swallowed; the old `exhaustive-deps` warning in `CommandPalette`; a test name `… (Ruling 6)` in `url.test.ts` that predates this branch.

title: Lab: fix the deep review's headline findings, element parity, dead code and the comment rule
description:
Fixes from the deep lab review (`lab-review.md`, added in the first commit of this branch), stacked on #107.

## Headline findings
- **Focus lost on a palette jump into a closed block (HIGH):** `CollapsibleBlock` now latches a forced open, so the knob the palette asked for keeps its block open and its focus.
- **The board's ◑ button took `colored` away from the lab:** the element dispatches a cancelable `colored-change`. Cancelling it clears the element's own override. The lab cancels it and writes the flag to whoever owns the board on screen: the lab's view, or the stored view in the library.
- **"% of perimeter" was a share of W + H:** the report row now reads "of width + height", in the lab and in the CLI summary.
- **The difficulty group's help was false:** it now says what the group's knobs change.
- **The low-window breakpoint disagreed at 700 px:** every stylesheet now uses 699 px, and a node test pins the CSS queries to `band.ts`.

## Parity with `<arrowz-board>`
- New view rows for the highlight colour and the margin (`pad`). The margin is clamped to the element's new `PAD_RANGE` (0–16). Both rows are carried in the URL hash and change the screen only, not the command or the export.
- A View / Inspect / Play control in a strip under the board frame:
  - Inspect: a ⌘-click shows a card with the piece's id, length, direction, and whether it is free or which piece blocks it.
  - Play: counts pieces left and mistakes, and has a Restart button.
  - The strip never covers the board (new `board-cover` layout invariant). Outside View it keeps a fixed height, so the board does not move between clicks.
- The element now has its own Inspect hint, and the README drift the review listed is fixed.

## Dead code
- Deleted the knob layer that nothing rendered any more: `KnobSlider`, `FieldHelp`, `viewHelpEntries`, and the `.fw-k*`, `.fw-kdesc`, `.fw-grid`, `.fw-skeleton` and `.fw-ends` rules.
- Also removed the uncalled `result.show` and an overridden report colour rule.
- `twoFrames` was copied in three test files; it now lives once in the harness.

## Comments
- The comment rule is now in `CLAUDE.md`: say why, once, in the fewest lines; no history; cite symbols, not line numbers.
- `packages/engine/comments.test.ts` enforces it on every `deno task verify`:
  - it fails on PR, round, Ruling, task, handoff and harness-fact markers, and on `file.ts:NN` citations;
  - non-header blocks may be at most 6 lines, and module or API headers at most 24.
- Its scope is `apps/lab/src`, `packages/board-element/src` and `packages/engine/lab-*.ts`.
- The sweep cut 8,644 comment lines to 6,466 (22.3% → 17.7%) and changed no code. A comment-stripped TypeScript print is identical in every file except for CSS comments inside the element's `css` template.

## Verification
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache` passes in a clean worktree.
- The browser pass in Chrome passed seven scenarios, both languages. It covered the palette jump, ◑ in the lab and in the library, highlight and margin surviving a reload, Inspect and Play, the report copy, 1280×699 against 1280×700, and a phone in Polish with a ten-digit seed.
- ⌘-clicks were simulated in headless Chromium. A real-mouse pass is still worth doing.

## Still open
`lab-review.md` → "Status after the fixes" and "What is still open".


## Follow-ups from the live pass
- The longest-pieces highlight is **off by default**; a link without the key reads as off.
- Readable lab names: `hilite` → `highlightLongest`, the colour field → `highlightColor` (store, i18n keys, DOM ids, hash keys). Old links still open through a legacy fallback. The element's own `view.highlight` is unchanged (the component will be refined separately).
- The saved board's layout hash is shown in full and wraps instead of being cut.
- The saved board's "generated" fact wraps between its parts (duration, date and time) instead of being cut.
- Switching View / Inspect / Play **keeps the game**: the lab mirrors the element's session, so Inspect describes the board as it stands. A separate **Reset** in Inspect and Play starts the game over.
- Still open (deferred): D2 — at phone width the element's own control bar covers about one row of the board's bottom-right cells. It is recorded in `lab-review.md`.

title: Lab board: keep its 16px beside the open settings drawer (round 3, PR 5)
description:
Round 3 of the Claude Design handoff (`handoff/HANDOFF-3.md`, section 5): a fix from the review. Stacked on #106.

## What changes

From 1024px up the open settings drawer pushed the board aside with `padding-left: var(--ls-w)`, which *replaced* the board wrap's own 16px. The board's frame stood flush against the drawer (one pixel away: the stage's 1px column gap), while closed, and beside the run column, it had 16px.

`design/console.css`: `padding-left: calc(var(--ls-w) + 16px)` in the `@media (min-width: 1024px)` rule for `.ls-open > .fw-boardwrap`. The gap on the board's left is now the same in every state.

## Measured

Live lab (Vite on the branch, real Chromium, drawer open by default), EN and PL:

| viewport | `.fw-board` open | handoff checkpoint | gap to the drawer |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1920×1080 | 654.6 | 655 (was 671) | 17 |
| 1440×900 | 517 | 517 (was 533) | 17 |
| 1280×800 | 378.6 | 379 (was 395) | 17 |
| 1024×768 | 424.1 | 424 (was 440) | 17 |

No horizontal scroll at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024, 924, 768, 600 and 375, in either language.

**Note on 16 vs 17.** The handoff's checkpoint reads `boardwrap.left + paddingLeft − ldrawer.right = 16`; in the app that sum is 17 in both states, because the stage's grid has a 1px column gap between the drawer's track and the board's. Closed, the handle ends at 28, the wrap starts at 29 and the board at 45. So the gap is the wrap's 16px plus that 1px seam, open and closed alike, and the frame widths match the handoff to the pixel. The test pins exactly that: `16 + 1`, open and closed.

## Tests

- `routes/LabLayout.browser.test.tsx`: new case at the four sizes — the board frame's gap to the open drawer and to the closed drawer's handle is 17px, and the open frame is the handoff's width. Red on the old rule (`open: expected 1 to be close to 17`), green on the new.
- **Outside the handoff's test list:** `harness/invariants.ts`, the layout audit's `board-width` floor at 1024 moves 440 → 424. The floor is there to turn red when a push eats into the board, and this PR eats 16px by design; the new value is the handoff's own checkpoint. 1440's floor (501) holds with 517 and is unchanged.

`pnpm -F lab test`: 1072 passed (1068 on #106 + 4). `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: green, 4 projects, 21 tasks.

title: Lab run column: Generate as the meter, the run state under it (round 3, 3h)
description:
Round 3 of the Claude Design handoff, PR 4 of 5: **run state in the run column, Generate as the meter (3h)**. Stacked on #105 (`lab/round3-docs`).

## What changes

- **Generate as the meter.** While a carve runs Generate gets `busy`: filled with `--signal-fill` to `--p`, label `Generating 41.3%` / `Generuję 41,3%` (new key `generatingPct`), `opacity: 1`, still `disabled`. `--p` is the same share as the progress, `1 − remaining/total`, rounded to one decimal like the label.
- **Progressbar for assistive technology.** Beside Generate, `div role="progressbar"` named `Run progress` / `Postęp generowania` (new key `runProgress`), min 0, max 100, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuetext` in the page's number format, visually hidden (`.fw-vh`). Generate points at it with `aria-describedby`. `.fw-stage` is `aria-busy="true"` during a run on the lab tab.
- **State line under Generate** (`p.fw-runstate`, `aria-hidden`): while running, the rest of the progress without the percent (new key `progressRest`); otherwise the last outcome, or the refusal in `--error` (`bad`).
- **Board column line** under `Load into lab`, for the library's notices.
- **`.fw-bar` from 768 up** is clipped to 1×1 (`shell.css`), the `<output aria-live>` stays in it and in the DOM, and `.fw-view` has one row.
- **Bands:** XL/L the line wraps; M/S it is the bar's last row, one line with an ellipsis; XS keeps the bar over the presets, and Generate in the CLI sheet is the meter too.
- **One function for the words** (`stage/useRunState.ts`): `RunStatusBar`'s branches moved out whole and unchanged in order, returning the live sentence, the run line and the library line. `useRunLine()` is the run's half without a router: the run column and its tests mount with no router.

## Decisions to check

- **Before the worker's first report** Generate says `Generating…` (the existing `generating` key) and the progressbar has no value (indeterminate), instead of inventing `0.0%`.
- **Decimals follow the language** in the live sentence too: `41,3%` and `1,4 s` in Polish (was `41.3` / `1.4` via `toFixed`), so the live sentence, the label and the line agree.
- **The board column line carries more than the four notices the handoff lists:** also `saveFailed` and a board that failed to load (`boardFileError`), both `bad`. From 768 up the output that used to show them is out of sight, so without this line a failed load or save would be silent on screen. The line is also shown with no board open, which is where Delete lands.
- **A failed run** (`generationError`) is `bad` too, like the refusal.
- **`busy` on `Stage` is optional** (default `false`), so `Stage.browser.test.tsx`, which is not on the list, mounts unchanged.

## Tests

Rewritten or extended from the handoff list:
- `run/RunColumn.browser.test.tsx`: the meter (label, `busy`, `--p`, opacity 1, gradient), the progressbar and `aria-describedby`, the indeterminate state, Polish, back to Generate once the run ends, and the line (progress rest, last outcome, refusal in `--error`). The focus cases Generate → Abort are unchanged and green.
- `stage/RunStatusBar.browser.test.tsx`: the live sentence while a carve reports (EN, PL), and the three texts of `useRunState` against each other: where they agree, where they differ, and the library line on `/boards` only.
- `routes/LabLayout.browser.test.tsx`: the checkpoints below, in the full App.
- `routes/LayoutInvariants.browser.test.tsx` through `harness/invariants.ts`: `bar-row` measured the whole M/S bar against 104px ("one or two lines"). With the state line as a row of its own the bar is 113px at 1024. It now measures the controls without that row, and adds a check that the line is one line.
- `design/shell.test.ts`: the ≥768 rule clips `.fw-bar` and never uses `display: none` or `visibility: hidden` (either would silence the live region).

Nothing outside the list had to change. The run of `triggers.browser.test.tsx` failed only while the run column needed a router, which the `useRunLine` split fixed.

Mutations, each reddening the named test: `opacity: 1` dropped from `.busy` → *carries the share done*; `.fw-bar` not absolute → the four *out of sight* cases; `nowrap` dropped from the M/S line → *the bar's last row, one line*; `busy={false}` → *Generate is the meter*; library notices never `bad` → *own line on the saved boards*; `aria-describedby` dropped → *points at a progressbar*. The `nowrap` mutation first survived: no sentence in the dictionary wraps in the 432px bar, even in Polish. The test now also feeds a worker error message, which has no length bound.

- `pnpm -F lab test`: 81 files, **1068 passed**.
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: green.

## Checkpoints (full App, carve at 41.3%, EN and PL)

| width | Generate | line under it | `.fw-bar` | `aria-busy` | document scroll |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1920 | 394 | 30.5px (1 line + padding) | 1×1 | true | none |
| 1440 | **260** | **47.0px (2 lines, 6 + 8 padding)** | 1×1 | true | none |
| 1280 | 260 | 47.0px | 1×1 | true | none |
| 1024 | **149 (PL)** / 165 (EN) | **16.5px, own row, one line** | 1×1 | true | none |
| 924 | 149 / 165 | 16.5px | 1×1 | true | none |
| 768 | 149 / 165 | 16.5px | 1×1 | true | none |
| 600 | CLI sheet | in the sheet | **600×41** | true | none |
| 375 | CLI sheet | in the sheet | **375×62** | true | none |

`aria-valuenow` 41.3, and the output still in the DOM with its sentence at every width. The board at 1440×900 grows from 700.2 to 741.6px, which is the old bar's 41.4px. Compared by eye with `r3-after-08` (1440 PL): matching.

## Notes (not changed in code)

- `BoardColumn`'s Copy still has its own copy of the clipboard logic; `run/useCopy.ts` (PR 3) could replace it.
- `workerError` stays unreachable, as the existing comment says: the run slice does not tell the two failure paths apart.

title: Lab docs: one navigation column, Copy on every block, ruled and coloured tables (round 3, 3f)
description:
Round 3 of the Claude Design handoff, PR 3 of 5: **documentation (3f)**. Stacked on #104 (`lab/round3-simple`).

## What changes

- **One navigation column, two levels.** `nav.fw-docs-toc` ("Documentation pages") lists both pages and, under each, its sections (Element: 4, CLI: 2) under a 1px guide. The page on screen is `aria-current="page"`; the section in view is `aria-current="true"` with a 2px `--signal` bar. The old row of page links (`.fw-docs-nav`) and its rules are gone.
  - The section in view is tracked by an `IntersectionObserver` rooted on `#docs-panel` (`useSectionInView.ts`): the last section whose heading has passed a line a fifth of the way down the panel. A section you jump to stays marked while its heading is on screen, so jumping to *Events* (too short to reach the line) does not mark *Methods and getters*.
  - Clicking a section of either page switches the page if needed and scrolls **the panel** to the heading (8px gap). Every click scrolls, also a second click on the same section.
  - Sticky in the panel at ≥768; under 768 it stands over the page, not sticky, lists only the current page's sections, every link 44px.
- **Page layout** `.fw-docs-grid`: 200px column | page of at most 110ch, 32px gap.
- **Copy on every block** (`DocsBlock.tsx`), in a 34px strip over the first line. Accessible name `Copy: <section>` / `Kopiuj: <sekcja>` (`Copied: …` after a copy). The clipboard logic is the live command's, extracted into `run/useCopy.ts` (LiveCommand behaviour unchanged, its tests untouched and green).
- **Syntax colours (GitHub Dark)** for the element example and the machine columns of all three tables, by column role (`docs/codeTokens.ts`, ports of `highlight()` / `tsTokens()`). Tokens are spans; the text is unchanged, so Copy writes the code, not the markup. CLI blocks stay plain.
- **README pointer** is now `aside.fw-docs-info` ("Note" / "Uwaga", new key `infoLabel` in `lab-docs.ts`) under the lead, with an SVG info glyph hidden from assistive tech.
- **Headings and tables**: `h3` 13px `--ink` over a `--border-strong` rule, 40px above (24px after a paragraph or the note); each table on its own `--graphite` plane, 1px frame, header row on `--surface`. All `h3` have ids (`docs-example`, `docs-props`, `docs-members`, `docs-events`, `docs-short`, `docs-knobs`).

## Deviations from the reconstruction, and why

- **The section is not in the URL hash.** The reconstruction uses `href="#docs-props"`. In the lab the fragment is the knobs' address (`useUrlHash` writes it on every route), so a section id there is overwritten at once and would read as a broken lab link when pasted. The section rides in react-router's navigation state (`sectionOf`), and a section link keeps the current fragment so clicking a section of the page on screen does not drop the knobs from the address bar.
- **44px under a coarse pointer too.** The round's CSS raises the column's links only under 768. The old row had `@media (pointer: coarse), (max-width: 767px)`; I kept that condition for the 44px rule so a tablet at ≥768 does not lose its touch size. The layout changes (one column, sections of the current page only) stay under 768 only.
- **Object keys in the example**: `W: 50, H: 50` colour `W`/`H` as properties, not as types for being capitals (the reconstruction's `tsTokens` colours capitals as types).

## Tests

Rewritten from the handoff list: `ElementDocs`, `CliDocs`, `DocsNav`, `DocsLayout` browser tests. New: `docs/codeTokens.test.ts` (node; every example and table cell joins back to its text, and the colour of each role).

**Outside the list:** `design/touch.browser.test.tsx` — its two "a docs link" cases were built on `.fw-docs-nav` markup, which the handoff removes; they now test a page link and a section link of `.fw-docs-toc` (both conditions: coarse pointer and XS).

Mutations, each reddening the named test only: pin rule removed → *jumping to the last section marks it*; observer not observing → *scrolling the panel moves the section in view*; scroll effect not keyed on the navigation → *a second click … scrolls back*; section link drops the fragment → *keeps the fragment*; `sticky` removed → *stays at the top of the panel*; coarse condition removed → both coarse *docs … link* cases (the XS ones stay green); key-before-`:` rule and `{}` depth in the scanner → their node cases.

- `pnpm -F lab test`: 81 files, **1042 passed**.
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: green (4 projects, 21 tasks).

## Checkpoints (measured in the full App, vitest browser, EN and PL)

| width | nav | page | links shown | link height | document scroll |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1920 | 200 | 792 | 2 + 4 + 2 | 32 / 30 | none |
| 1440 | 200 | 792 | 2 + 4 + 2 | 32 / 30 | none |
| 1280 | 200 | 792 | 2 + 4 + 2 | 32 / 30 | none |
| 1024 | 200 | 752 | 2 + 4 + 2 | 32 / 30 | none |
| 924 | 200 | 652 | 2 + 4 + 2 | 32 / 30 | none |
| 768 | 200 | 496 | 2 + 4 + 2 | 32 / 30 | none |
| 600 | over page | 560 | 2 + current page's | 44 | none |
| 375 | over page | 335 | 2 + current page's | 44 | none |

Same numbers in both languages and on both pages. The handoff's 741 (1024) and 324 (375) are 11px less than mine: exactly a classic scrollbar in the reconstruction's browser; the headless runner's overlay scrollbars take none. Current page and section: `--ink` (rgb 237,238,242), section bar `inset 2px 0 0 --signal`. Compared by eye with `r3-after-05` (1440 PL) and at 375 PL: matching.

## Notes (not changed in code, per the round's rules)

- **Tables wider than the panel at 768 and below.** The machine columns are `nowrap`, so the property table is 595px and the member table 634px wide. Before the round the panel already scrolled sideways at 600 and 375 (632px of content); with the 232px navigation column it now also does at 768 (886px in a 768px panel). The document never scrolls. A fix would be a table in its own `overflow-x: auto` box, or letting the type column wrap.
- **Copy under a finger** is 2px + 11px text tall, like the live command's Copy; neither is raised for a coarse pointer.
- The section links are links to their page (the fragment is the lab's), so "open in new tab" opens the page at its top, not at the section.

title: Lab simple view on the knob rows' grid (round 3, PR 2)
description:
Round 3 of the Claude Design handoff, PR 2 of 5 (variant 3c): the simple view moves onto the advanced view's knob rows. Stacked on #103, whose `--ok` token the later PRs use.

## What changes

- **`SimplePanel`** is now the `.kv.kv-g` grid in two `Section`s, `board` / `plansza` and `Preview` / `Podgląd`, with 14 `.kv-row`s. The cards (`.fw-k`, `.fw-grid`) and the help list over the panel (`FieldHelp`) are gone.
- **Size and seed** are `ValueKnob` rows: short label, `?`, value with unit, min, track and max. `ValueKnob` takes two optional overrides, `value` and `onSet`:
  - a size shows the **recipe's** value and writes through `recipe.setSide` + `applyRecipe(false)`, as `SizeCard` did;
  - the seed writes through `params.setMany`, the machine path (Ruling 4), so it does not bump `edits` and cannot wake `auto`.
- **Recipe sliders** (`PositionSlider`) are rows with no `?` and no numeric ends. The value is text (there is nothing to type). The end words `p.kv-ends` describe the track (`aria-describedby`).
- **Skeleton** is `Segmented` in a `wide` control track.
- **Randomise** is a switch row like `FlagRow`: short label `randomise` / `losuj`, value `on`/`off`, the whole sentence in `title`, and `randomizeHelp` under its `?`.
- **Preview** reuses the preview tab's own rows: `ViewNumberRow` (stroke, head width with its `auto` chip, head height), `SwitchRow` (rounded, colored, hilite) and `ThemeRow`. These three are now exported from `ViewPanel.tsx`. `ViewNumberField` and `ViewFlagSwitch` had no other caller and are deleted.
- **`KnobLine`** gets an optional `under` slot, a line in the row's own grid. This is how the end words stand **under the track**, as HANDOFF-3's known differences recommend, rather than across the row as the reconstruction has them:
  - ≥ 768 in a full panel: column 4. The words wrap inside the track when both do not fit (Polish "line shape" at 1024–1440 takes two lines; user ruling).
  - A panel too narrow for the bound tracks (container query): column 3, same wrapping.
  - XS: the whole row, one line, as in `r3-after-12` (user ruling). The track there is about 97px, and the Polish words took five lines under it.

## Wording to confirm (proposal, EN / PL)

- The randomise row's short label: `randomise` / `losuj` (`simple.randomizeShort`)

## Checkpoints (Chromium, full `App` in simple mode; settings sheet at < 768)

| width | panel | `.kv-row`s | first track (`width`) | bounds shown | end words under track | horizontal document scroll (EN / PL) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1920 | 752 px | 14 | **407 px** | yes | yes | none / none |
| 1440 | 544 px | 14 | **199 px** | yes | yes | none / none |
| 1280 | 522 px | 14 | 177 px | yes | yes | none / none |
| 1024 | 510 px | 14 | **165 px** | yes | yes | none / none |
| 924 | 448 px | 14 | 103 px | yes | yes | none / none |
| 768 | 448 px | 14 | 103 px | yes | yes | none / none |
| 600 | sheet 600 px | 14 | — | no (XS) | whole row | none / none |
| 375 | sheet 375 px | 14 | 97 px | no (XS) | whole row | none / none |

Compared with `r3-after-03`/`04`/`12`: same rows, values, bounds, switches, segmented control and theme select. The only difference is the end words' position at ≥ 768 described above. At 375, "długość element…" is truncated in the 12ch label track, as in the reconstruction.

## Tests

- Rewritten `simple/SimplePanel.browser.test.tsx`:
  - two named sections (EN/PL) and 14 rows, with no card left;
  - a size typed and dragged into the recipe, and the size row showing the recipe, not a knob moved behind it;
  - a recipe slider's text value and end-word description;
  - the end words under the track at 1440, inside a narrow track in EN/PL, and across the row on one line at XS;
  - skeleton at the right edge;
  - seed through the machine path;
  - randomise's short label, title, `?` help and `on`/`off`;
  - the preview rows and their writes;
  - theme, no palette editor, head height's help in its own row.
- `design/touch.browser.test.tsx`: the two `.fw-k` card entries become simple-view rows (value, track, segmented choice, 44px each).
- **Outside the handoff's list:** `console/ViewPanel.browser.test.tsx` loses its two cases for the deleted `ViewNumberField` ("a field hands its owner an already-clamped number") and `ViewFlagSwitch` ("a flag switch reports a press without writing any store"). They tested the components the handoff says to delete. Nothing else in that file changed, and nothing failed.
- Every new assertion was mutated red: size writing the knob, size showing the knob, seed through `params.set`, each of the three end-word placements, `under` not rendered, no wrapping, slider not described, randomise without title, fixed `off`. `justify-self: end` on the segmented control is an equivalent mutation: `.kv-g .cc` is already `display: flex; justify-content: flex-end`, so the rule ported from the reconstruction is inert. It is kept as ported, and the test pins the outcome.
- `pnpm -F lab test`: 923 passed. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: green.

## Notes (not changed in code)

- Now without an element: `.fw-k`, `.fw-grid`, `.fw-ends`, `.fw-k .bar` in `console.css`, the `KnobSlider` component (its `boundOn`/`percent` helpers are still used), the `FieldHelp` component and `viewHelpEntries`. The handoff names only the two deleted components, so these are left for a clean-up.
- At XS, every switch row (`FlagRow`, and randomise, which copies it) is 4px wider than its row. The advanced preview tab measures the same (rounded, multicolour, longest, jammed cells, point grid: 344/340), so it predates this round. It is most likely the switch's 44px touch target. It is clipped by `.kv` and not visible.
- The simple view's size and seed rows now show violations and rule bounds under themselves, as the knob rows do. The cards did not.

title: Lab report: a summary over the statistics and named groups (round 3, PR 1)
description:
Round 3 of the Claude Design handoff, PR 1 of 5 (variant 3b): the report gets a summary over its statistics, named groups, and the rhythm of the Preview panel's rows.

## What changes

- **Summary** (`report/ReportSummary.tsx`): four figures over the table (pieces, longest, D, time), each its number, its term and its change, with the caption "change against the previous run" linked by `aria-describedby`. `dt` precedes `dd` in the markup; `dd { display: contents }` puts the number first on screen. The change is the table's own `reportDelta`, so its colour follows `trend`, never the sign. Time reports no change; a first run shows hidden placeholders.
- **The rows the summary repeats leave the table** (`tr.sum`). What they said beyond the number stays reachable: D's full name is the `title` of an `<abbr>`, and the whole values of longest and time are the `title` of their numbers.
- **Named groups**: every `tbody` opens with `tr.grp > th[scope=rowgroup][colspan=3]`.
- **Grid rows**: `.fw-stats` and `tbody` are blocks and every `tr` is a grid (label | value | change). Rows are 34px with a `--border` rule, and headings are caps at 11px as `.kv-sub`. Wide values (`tr.long`) stay on their label's line. A row with no change carries `nodelta` (a class, not `:has()`, because the change's cell also holds its hidden word).
- **`--ok`** (`#3fb27f`) is the colour of a better change, in the table and the summary. It is added to `tokens.css` and `tokens.test.ts`.
- **Longest pieces**: the column headings are right-aligned over their numbers.
- **Stored board report** (`StoredFacts`): the same grid, with no summary and no groups.
- **Engine**: `StatRow` gets `key: StatKey | null`, the suffix of the row's `stat_<key>` label. The lab picks the summary and wide rows by key rather than by index. This is report-only; no board or hash moves.

## Wording to confirm (proposals, EN / PL)

- Groups: `size` / `rozmiar`, `blocking` / `blokowanie`, `reach` / `zasięg`, `shape` / `kształt`, `run` / `przebieg` (`statGroupSize` … `statGroupRun`)
- Caption: `change against the previous run` / `zmiana wobec poprzedniego przebiegu` (`reportSummaryCap`)

## Checkpoints (measured in Chromium, full `App`, report open; sheet at < 768)

| width | drawer | summary columns | groups | rows/cells overflowing | board size on its label's line | horizontal document scroll (EN / PL) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1920 | 461 px | 4 × 107 px, one row | 5 | 0 | yes | none / none |
| 1440 | 352 px | 4 × 80 px, one row | 5 | 0 | yes | none / none |
| 1280 | 352 px | 4 × 80 px | 5 | 0 | yes | none / none |
| 1024 | 352 px | 4 × 80 px | 5 | 0 | yes | none / none |
| 924 | 352 px | 4 × 80 px | 5 | 0 | yes | none / none |
| 768 | 352 px | 4 × 80 px | 5 | 0 | yes | none / none |
| 600 | sheet 600 px | 4 × 142 px | 5 | 0 | yes | none / none |
| 375 | sheet 375 px | 4 × 86 px | 5 | 0 | yes (PL too) | none / none |

The time figure fits its column at every width. The load run's time was `0.03 s`; the handoff's `0.42 s` is the same length.

**Accessibility tree** (Chrome, `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, same markup with and without `report.css`): `display: block` on the table and its bodies keeps `table "Statistics"`, its rows, row headers and cells. Chrome drops `rowgroup` in both cases.

## Tests

- Rewritten `report/ReportPanel.browser.test.tsx`: rows counted without the group headings; five named groups in EN and PL; the Preview rhythm; `--ok` contrast; the summary's order, caption, titles and changes; which rows hide; `long`/`nodelta` by key; nothing past its row at 352px in EN and PL; right-aligned longest headings; the stored report's grid.
- `design/tokens.test.ts` asserted that `--ok` was *not* ported. That assertion is dropped and the token list is now eighteen. The handoff names this file under PR 1 but not under "Tests to rewrite".
- Engine: the pinned rows carry their keys, and a new case checks that keys are unique and match their labels.
- Every new assertion was mutated red: `tr.sum` shown, better back to `--ink`, `nodelta` dropped, `dd` not `contents`, longest headings left-aligned, `abbr` without title, a change coloured by sign, 12px group headings, a wide value that will not wrap (`text-wrap: nowrap`), and a label track of `1fr`. `white-space: nowrap` on a wide value is an equivalent mutation, because `text-wrap: balance` later in the same rule restores wrapping.
- `pnpm -F lab test`: 918 passed. `deno task test` (engine): 387 passed. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: green.

## Notes (not changed in code)

- Chrome reads the group headings in capitals ("SIZE"), because `text-transform` reaches the accessible name. `.kv-sub` in the Preview panel does the same today.
- The mock's `report.css` declared `.fw-rsum-wrap ~ .fw-stats tr.sum { display: none }` twice, and `small.better` first as `--ink`, then as `--ok`. Both were merged into one rule each. `.fw-rsum dt abbr { text-decoration: none }` is new: without it, the full-name `abbr` would underline "D".
- The summary's time uses a decimal point in Polish too (`0.02 s`), the same as the table's time row today.
- `StoredFacts` rows reuse `rowClass`, so its pieces, longest and time rows carry `sum`. That is harmless: the rule only applies after a summary, and a stored board has none.

title: Lab: responsive layout in five bands, a bar under the board and bottom sheets on a phone
description:
Handoff 2, PR 7 — the last of the round. The lab and the saved boards lay themselves out in five width bands and a low window, with no flag: the package's `.fw.rwd` is `.fw`.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-lab-responsive-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-23-lab-responsive.md`

## Bands

| Band | Width | Layout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| XL | ≥ 1600 | as PR 1 |
| L | 1280–1599 | run column 18rem, settings drawer capped at 34rem |
| M | 1024–1279 | the right column is a bar under the board (`CLI · Copy · command · Generate · alternatives · …`); the open drawer pushes board and bar |
| S | 768–1023 | as M, the drawer lies over the board and starts closed |
| XS | < 768 | one column; Settings / CLI / Report (saved boards: Boards / Board / Report) as bottom sheets over a 56px sheet bar; a menu chip in the top bar; the presets as a grouped list |
| low | < 700 tall, ≥ 768 wide | the preset strip stands in the top bar |

## Decisions

- **D1** one PR for all bands.
- **D2** in a low window `PresetStrip` renders inside `TopBar` — one instance, placed by a `matchMedia` hook (`state/band.ts`, `shell/useLayoutBand.ts`).
- **D3** below 1024 the settings drawer starts closed and closes on crossing into that range **without** writing the remembered preference; widening back restores it.
- **D4** the saved boards follow the lab's rules (the open board's column is the bar at M/S and a sheet at XS).
- CSS owns the layout: every new element (`SheetBar`, the menu chip, the `…` popover) is always in the DOM and shown by media queries, so nothing appears or vanishes beside `Stage` (the GL context survives).
- XS joins the existing `(pointer: coarse)` size blocks through a media query list instead of a second copy; the switch stays 36×18 with a 44×44 target (PR 4), not the package's 48×26.
- ⌘K's touch word is "command palette" / "paleta poleceń", inside its accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3), not the package's "commands".
- Keys: Escape closes one layer — the `…` popover and the menu consume their own, then an open sheet, then report, then settings. At XS `r`/`s` toggle the sheets, and Escape with no sheet open changes nothing (a remembered report is invisible there).
- A ⌘K jump to a knob or a view field opens the settings sheet at XS, or the drawer when it is closed elsewhere — found by the whole-branch review: with D3 the jump landed on nothing at S and XS.
- Picking a board in the phone's Boards sheet closes the sheet.
- PR 1's stopgaps are gone (the 1279/900 stage templates, the 600px preset panel); the pins that held their geometry in `LabLayout`/`Workspace` tests are retired.

## Tests

- 795 → 910 in `lab:test`. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` (21 tasks, no cache) and `deno task verify` (386/0) green at `874d315`. (At `c1386fc`, `lab:check` failed on a type error in `SheetBar.browser.test.tsx`; fixed in `874d315`.)
- `LayoutInvariants` runs the handoff's eight sizes (1920×1080 … 375×812) on both tabs, with new invariants: `board-width` (spec §2's floors: 1440 ≥ 501, 1024 ≥ 440, 768 ≥ 678, XS edge to edge), `bar-row`, `sheet-fit`, `sheet-bar`, `touch-target` (open sheets included), `top-scroll`, `hidden-box`. `KNOWN_RED` is `{}`, and a test checks every key it could hold names a real case.
- Every invariant and behaviour was shown to bite by a mutation that turned its named assertion red.
- Live pass: scripted Playwright at all eight sizes in English and Polish (sheets, menu, `…`, low-window presets, resize across 1024 and back, saved boards) — no horizontal scroll, no console errors.
- Manual pass in Chrome through DevTools MCP at all eight sizes, both languages, both tabs: drawers, sheets, menu, `…`, presets from the top bar, `f` / `r` / `s` / Escape at XS, D3 across 1024 and back (no storage write), D4. It found four defects, each fixed test-first:
  - **L 1280–1599:** the 34rem drawer leaves the knobs a 360–400px panel, while a row's five tracks need `30ch + 188px` (404px); the maximum's track and the slider's right end were cut off (at 1280 on every row). The container query now drops the bound tracks below that floor instead of at 359px, so **L shows no range ends** (XL keeps them). `knobgrid` expects them from 1600 and gained a 1920 case so the shown branch is still measured.
  - **XS with a ≥360px panel (e.g. 600×900):** the XS block hid `.mn`/`.mx` on the five-track grid, so the slider auto-placed into a 36px track (322px now); it takes the narrow panel's three tracks.
  - A new `knob-row` invariant reads both (`panel-overflow` is blind to them: `.kv` clips the row first). Mutations: the 359px threshold turns `board@1280×800` (en, pl) red, the XS tracks removed turn `sheet-settings@600×900` red; 1920 and 375 stay green as controls.
  - **React duplicate key `probe`** in the difficulty panel (the dependency block's id vs its parent knob's key, since #95): the block is keyed `block-<id>`.
- Left open, from before this PR: at XL the open report (489px overlay) covers 21px of the board's right edge.

## Stacked on

#99 (`lab/saved-boards`) ← … ← #94. Merge from the bottom.

title: Lab: saved boards in the lab's layout, with a size rail, a board column and the open board's report
description:
Handoff 2 (Claude Design, round 2), PR 6 of 7: the saved boards in the lab's layout. **Stacked on #98** (`lab/presets-centre`) → #97 → #96 → #95 → #94.

## What changes

The saved boards tab now uses the lab's stage: the settings drawer on the left, the board, a right column, and the report drawer.

- **Drawer.** The console is the settings drawer's content on both tabs. On the saved boards its rail is `SIZES` (one tab per size, with its board count in `--ash`) and `ELEMENT` · `Preview`, a vertical tablist with the lab rail's keys (`BoardsRail.tsx`, which replaces `SizeChips.tsx`). The panel shows one of two things:
  - **List** (`BoardList.tsx`): a header (`25×50 · 3 boards · Refresh`), then ruled 52px rows. A row shows eight and four digits of the hash (the whole id is in `title`), a short date, `pieces · longest`, and the source, or `not closed` in `--warn`. The open row sits on `--signal-fill`.
  - **Preview** (`BoardPreview.tsx`): the lab's knob rows, in two sections. "Arrows · saved with the board" has stroke, head width, head height, rounded and multicolour. They are read from the stored view, clamped, and saved back through `useViewSave` as before. "Colours" is the lab's own section, because `BoardFrame` lays the lab's theme, palette, paper and ink over a stored board.
  - With no store, or an empty one, the rail has no size tabs and the panel says why.
- **Right column** (`BoardColumn.tsx`, which was `BoardDetail.tsx`): `CLI · this board` with Copy and the command broken between flags, **Load into lab** as the primary action (`.fw-go`), Delete from disk (arming works as before, hover and armed in `--error`), Download SVG and Download board file for the stored board, and the facts: layout, seed, source, generated. With no board open it says "Open a board from the list." It is keyed by the open board, as the detail was, so an armed Delete never carries over to another board. The run column stays mounted and hidden on this tab, so a carve in flight keeps its node.
- **Report.** The drawer works as in the lab and reports the open board: the six figures the store keeps (`StoredFacts.tsx`), a note that the full report needs a run, and the longest pieces read from the board. The `.fw-lab.library .fw-drawer { display: none }` rule is gone.
- **Keys.** `r` and `s` are bound on both workspace tabs, and the ⌘K footer lists them there too.
- **CSS.** `library.css` is replaced by the handoff's `boards.css`, without its RWD rules, which belong to PR 7. The `:not(.library)` qualifiers on the stage rules in `console.css` are gone, along with `.fw-runs`, the chips and the empty-store one-column rule.
- **Shared pieces** (their own commit): `NumberRow` / `FlagRow` / `ColoursSection` out of `ViewPanel.tsx`, `drawSvg` out of `ExportButtons.tsx`, and `refreshLibrary()` out of `useLibraryList`, so that the list and the column can both refresh without a second fetch-on-mount.
- **Dictionary:** new EN/PL entries, with a Polish plural helper for "plansza / plansze / plansz". `sizeGroup` and `genShort` are removed because nothing reads them now.

## Decisions (please review)

1. **What the report shows for a stored board** (asked and settled before implementing): the stored figures and the longest pieces, with no engine change. The 23 run rows need `CarverStats` and metrics that a stored board does not carry, and `StoredBoard` deliberately has no `ReportInput` (spec §5.3). The longest-pieces table uses the lab's count even with the highlight off, because a stored board has no highlight of its own.
2. **Preview is not literally the lab's `ViewPanel`**, as the handoff says. That panel edits the lab's view, which does not draw a stored board's arrows. The rows are the same components, bound to the stored view, plus the lab's colour section, which does apply.
3. **The size tab keeps PR 5a's Ruling 7.** Choosing a size opens the board already open if it has that size, otherwise the first board of that size.
4. **Exports on the column** use the stored board's own view, and draw jammed cells when the board did not close, as the stage does.
5. **Touch targets.** The size tabs keep the old chips' 44px, the rows 52px, and Refresh 44px under `(pointer: coarse)`. The lab rail's own target is left to PR 7.

## Deviations from the handoff

- The fact list's term track is `max-content` on a subgrid, not `9ch`. The live run in Chrome caught the Polish "wygenerowano" (12 characters) overflowing into its value, and a test now checks both languages.
- `boards.css`'s `.fw-lab.boards:not(.library)` row rule became `.fw-lab.library { grid-template-rows: minmax(292px, 1fr) }`, because the repo names the face `library`.

## Tests

title: Lab: lighter square switches, with a 44px target for a finger
description:

title: Lab: the Preview panel as knob rows, with dependency blocks and descriptions
description:
Handoff 2 (Claude Design, round 2), PR 3 of 7: the Preview panel on the knob grid. **Stacked on #95** (`lab/knob-rows`), which is stacked on #94.

## What changes

- **Preview is made of knob rows** on the same five-track grid as the generator groups (the grid test now walks the preview too, at 1440 and 924, in EN and PL). There are five titled sections, each a named group: *arrows* (stroke, head width, head height, rounded, multicolour), *highlight* (longest → top count), *grid* (jammed cells, point grid → dot colour, dot radius), *colours* (theme with its swatch strip, background, ink, palette), *export* (export cell).
- **Numbers are drawn tracks** whose bounds come from `VIEW_RANGE` (`command.ts`), read at render and never copied, plus `POINT_RADIUS_RANGE` for the dot radius. A typed value goes through the existing slice readers, which clamp.
- **Head width 0 = auto**: an `auto` chip in the minimum's track. Releasing it lands on the width the automatic head draws at the current stroke (`autoHeadWidth`), so the head does not jump. `viewFields.test.ts` checks this width against the engine's own `pieceShape` at five strokes on both sides of the 0.5 rule change.
- **Two dependency blocks** (`CollapsibleBlock`, shared with the generator's): the top count sits under *longest*, and the dot colour and radius under *point grid*. Each block opens with its switch or on a palette jump to one of its rows.
- **Values without a number** (`on`/`off`, hex, the palette's `n / 8`) sit in the value track in the numbers' colour. The palette takes the minimum's and the control's tracks.
- **A `?` and a description on every row.** Every control's `aria-describedby` resolves.
- **Removed:** the colours card, the flags card and their CSS (`.fw-k.fw-flags`, `.fw-k.fw-colours`, `.fw-colour-cell`), `ColorField`, `ColoursCard`, `DRAWING_FLAGS`. `ViewNumberField`, `ViewFlagSwitch` and `ThemeSwatchStrip` stay for the simple view and the library detail.

## New texts, for review (EN / PL)

Where they existed, texts are reused: `cellHelp`, `headHelp` (both heads), `pointRadiusHelp`, `paletteHelp`. `pointColorHelp` and `showPointsHelp` come from the element docs (`lab-docs.ts`). The rest are written from the repository's facts:

| key | EN | PL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| strokeHelp | Line width in grid units. Below 0.2 the line thins into the paper; at 0.9 it fills its own square and leaves the tip no room. | Grubość linii w podziałkach. Poniżej 0,2 linia ginie w papierze; przy 0,9 wypełnia swoją kratkę i nie zostawia miejsca na grot. |
| topHelp | How many of the longest pieces the highlight marks. 0 marks none. | Ile najdłuższych elementów wyróżnia podświetlenie. 0 nie wyróżnia żadnego. |
| roundedHelp | Rounds the corners a piece turns through, and caps its tail with a disc. | Zaokrągla rogi, przez które skręca element, i zakańcza jego ogon kółkiem. |
| coloredHelp | Draws each piece in a colour of its own: from the custom palette, else the theme, else a hue per piece. | Rysuje każdy element własnym kolorem: z własnej palety, inaczej z motywu, inaczej odcieniem na element. |
| hiliteHelp | Draws the longest pieces in the highlight colour, on top of the rest. | Rysuje najdłuższe elementy kolorem wyróżnienia, na wierzchu pozostałych. |
| voidsHelp | Marks the cells the generator failed to carve, where the board jammed. | Zaznacza komórki, których generator nie zdołał wyciąć, tam gdzie plansza się zaklinowała. |
| themeHelp | A built-in theme: paper, ink, highlight and the colours of the pieces. What you set below wins over it. | Wbudowany motyw: papier, tusz, podświetlenie i kolory elementów. To, co ustawisz niżej, ma pierwszeństwo. |
| paperHelp | The board’s paper. Set, it wins over the theme; cleared, the theme supplies it again. | Papier planszy. Ustawiony wygrywa z motywem; wyczyszczony oddaje go motywowi. |
| inkHelp | The arrows’ colour while they are not multicoloured. Set, it wins over the theme; cleared, the theme supplies it again. | Kolor strzałek, gdy nie są wielobarwne. Ustawiony wygrywa z motywem; wyczyszczony oddaje go motywowi. |

The short labels (at most 12 characters, pinned by a Deno test), section headings, block headers, `on`/`off` (`wł.`/`wył.`) and the theme row's `none`/`brak` are all in `lab-i18n.ts`.

## Deviations from the handoff

- **Ranges come from the repository, not the reconstruction:** cell 1–200 (not 20–400/10), stroke 0.2–0.9 (not 0.05–1), head width 0–0.9 (not 0–2), head height 0–1.2 (not 0.2–3), top 0–1000 (not 1–50), dot radius 0–0.5 (not 0.02–0.5).
- **The reconstruction's descriptions are not used.** Its stroke text ("1 fills the cell") contradicts the 0.9 ceiling. The texts above replace them (decided with the maintainer).
- **The theme row's empty option is `none`**, as the handoff names it. The longer `none (default colours)` did not fit a select the length of a slider's track. The simple view keeps the longer one.
- **The palette's add button is a chip** in its row, with its old text `add colour`.
- **A disabled chip** gets its own colour (`--border-strong`), so the add button at the cap still reads as refused.

## Tests

Every case keeps its intent (bounds against `VIEW_RANGE`, clamp on commit, following the store, typed value not written early, palette and theme behaviour, disabled look), now through the rows. The four-sections, cards and help-list cases became five sections, rows and descriptions on demand. Also `Workspace` (switch names) and `SimplePanel` (palette absence).

One mutation first stayed green and exposed an unpinned palette position, now fixed in its own commit.

title: Lab: knob rows on one five-track grid, dependency blocks, descriptions on demand
description:
Handoff 2 (Claude Design, round 2), PR 2 of 7: the knob rows. **Stacked on #94** (`lab/settings-drawer`); merge #94 first.

## What changes

- **One row per control, one grid for the whole console.** Every row in every generator group uses the same five tracks: `label (+?) | value | min | control | max`. The label track is fixed at 12ch + the `?` (+ the dependency indent), and only the control track flexes. Values, tracks, selects and bounds therefore sit on one x across rows and groups (measured at 1440 and 924, EN and PL). Below a 360px panel (`@container`) the bound tracks drop.
- **Short labels** (the engine's terms, at most 12 characters in both languages, pinned by a Deno test) and **units** are in the dictionary. The full sentence stays in the row's `title` together with the range, and in the description.
- **Drawn track:** rail, fill, a 2×12 thumb and the rule floor, with the native range input laid over them transparently, so keyboard and touch come from the platform. The simple view keeps `KnobSlider` unchanged.
- **Special values** (`Lmax` 0 = `auto`, `giantStep` 0 = `random`): the value track shows the word, and a chip in the min track is pressed while the knob holds the value. Releasing the chip returns the knob to its last value, then to its default, then to the smallest legal value (`Lmax` 17, which is checked against `lmaxHole`).
- **Descriptions on demand:** a `?` per row (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`) opens the row's own description. A closed description stays in the tree (`.fw-vh`), so every `aria-describedby` still resolves.
- **Dependency blocks** replace per-knob "No effect" lines. The skeleton block (6 knobs, sub-sections *layout* / *growth*) sits under `giants` and `later share`; the probe block sits under `probe share`. A block is collapsed while its parents are 0, with a header saying what it needs. It opens when a parent turns on, when the palette jumps to one of its knobs, or when one of its knobs is refused. The block's own reason is said once, in the header; a row's other reason (`stepZero`, `anticoilWins`) is still that row's line. `knobLayout.test.ts` checks the blocks against the engine's `inactive` functions.
- **Lengths mix bar:** short, medium and long shares with a percent legend. The `short + medium ≤ 0.9` rule is a `--warn` mark at 90%, and the long share turns `--error` past it.
- **The descriptions switch is removed**, together with `ui.help` and the link's `help` field. Old links that carry the field still load. The simple view, the preview and the library detail show their descriptions until they get rows too.
- **Touch:** under `pointer: coarse` the handoff's touch sizes apply now (52px row, 44px value and track, 40px select, 32px `?`/chip, 48px block header), so rows do not regress below the old 44px targets before PR 7.
- **Dead rules removed:** the generator-only `.fw-k.off` / `.fw-k.bad` / `.num em` rules. The rest of `.fw-k`/`.fw-grid`/`.fw-kdesc` still serves the simple view, the preview (until PR 3) and the library detail (until PR 6).

## Deviations from the handoff (all decided with the maintainer)

- **`later share` is a parent, not a dependent.** The engine turns the skeleton on with `giants > 0` **or** `wGiant > 0`. The reconstruction hid `later share` inside a block headed "needs giants > 0", which is false. The header reads "needs giants or later share > 0".
- **Reasons other than the block's are kept** under their rows, dimmed in `--ash`. The reconstruction showed none.
- **"show help" is removed** rather than kept as "expand all".
- **The 0.9 cap is a marker at 90% of the bar.** The reconstruction draws nothing for it.
- **Ranges come from `PARAM_SPEC`**, not from the reconstruction's invented ones (e.g. `giantSpan` 1–200, not 0.5–8).
- **The chip's accessible name is `auto (max length)`**, not `max length: auto`. That second name is the value button's name while the knob is `auto`, and two buttons with one name are indistinguishable.
- **The `.sp-4` variant is folded into `.kv-g`.** It is the only variant in use.

## Tests

- Rewritten: `KnobPanel`, `ValueKnob`, `ChoiceKnob`, `StartKnob`, `KnobSlider` (plus the drawn track), `knobgrid` (five tracks, one x across groups and languages at 1440 and 924, no label cut), `design/console.browser` (contrast of an inactive row), `touch` (knob row sizes), `useFocusRequest` (flash on the row), `LayoutInvariants` (`lengths-help-off` → `lengths-help-open`), plus the help-switch cases in `RunColumn`, `SimplePanel`, `ViewPanel`, `Workspace`, `url` and `ui.slice`.
- New: `knobLayout.test.ts` (blocks against the engine; release values against the rules) and the dictionary short-label test.
- Mutation check: seven mutations (later share not a parent, block reason repeated, no indent compensation, closed description `display: none`, chip named like the value, cap at 80%, palette jump ignored) each turned the named cases red.
- `pnpm -F lab test`: 74 files, 778 tests passed. Deno: 384 passed. eslint, prettier, deno fmt/lint and tsc are clean; the one eslint warning (`CommandPalette.tsx:76`) predates this branch.

## Out of scope, noticed

- The value button shows the raw JS number (`0.08`, not `0,08` in Polish); the bounds already use the language's format.
- `maxBack`'s CLI word `auto` (= 200) is no longer shown beside the number; the slider still announces it via `aria-valuetext`.

title: Lab: settings drawer on the stage's left, run column beside the board
description:
Handoff 2 (Claude Design, round 2), PR 1 of 7: the settings drawer on the stage's left edge and the run column beside the board.

## What changes

- The lab's stage has four tracks: the settings drawer's handle (28px, 44 on a coarse pointer), the board, the run column (`clamp(16rem, 22vw, 28rem)`, 16rem below 1280, 14rem at 900 and under) and the report's handle. Nothing sits under the stage but the clamp notice and the violations.
- **Settings drawer** (`.fw-ldrawer`): the report's drawer mirrored. It holds the console (rail 126px, 112px at ≤900, plus the panel). It is open by default and remembered under `labSettings`, the same way `ui.report` is remembered. From 1024px up it does not cover the board: `ls-open` pads the board's track by `--ls-w`. The drawer is toggled by its class and never remounted. When it closes with the focus inside, the focus moves to its handle.
- **Keys:** `s`/`S` toggles the settings under the same guard as `r`, and only on the lab tab. Escape closes one layer per press: the report first, then the settings. The palette's footer adds `s settings`.
- **Run column:** it now belongs to `Stage` on both tabs and is hidden by class on the saved boards, so its node and refs survive the trip. The CLI figure and the command are `flex: none`: the whole command shows and the column scrolls instead of the box. This reverses spec §5.2's growing figure, so Generate now moves down with a longer command.
- **Saved boards:** unchanged until PR 6. They keep the `.fw-runs` column and the console under the stage.
- The `.fw-runs` track leaves the lab, and with it the last filmstrip reservation (the filmstrip is dropped).

## Deviations from the handoff

- **Below 1024px the open drawer lies over the board instead of pushing it.** Pushing would leave the board 44px wide at 768 and about 0 at 414. This is a stopgap until PR 7's responsive layout. Under roughly 700px the open drawer also covers the run column, so it has to be closed to reach Generate there.
- **The push-aside padding is `:not(.solo)` inside `min-width: 1024px`, not `padding-left: 0` in solo.** The handoff's solo override also zeroed the board's own 16px padding, and turning solo on animated the board's size for 180ms. Both were caught by the solo geometry test. This is the pattern `rwd.css` uses in PR 7.
- **The settings handle's `aria-controls` names the console (`settings-panel`), not the drawer that contains the handle.** The report's handle does the same with `lab-report`.
- **The console's hide waits out the 180ms slide**, as the report's does, rather than hiding at once.
- **`run.css`'s growing-figure rule is replaced in place** rather than overridden from `console.css`: the run column lives only in the stage now.

## Tests

- Rewritten: `LabLayout` (the closed report handle, the command box contract, solo, run column widths), `RunColumn` (the command box), `Workspace` (eight Generate cases pinned to 1400×900, the console now sits in the drawer), `Stage` (new props), `CommandPalette` (footer counts).
- New: `ui.slice`/`preferences` (the settings state and its storage), `Stage` (handle attributes, focus return), `LabLayout` (`s` with its refusals, the Escape order, no `s` on docs or saved boards, push-aside at 1024/1400/1920, the 414 overlay), a `settings-fit` invariant and a `settings-closed` state in `LayoutInvariants`.
- Mutation check: six mutations (no push-aside, padding in solo, no second Escape, no focus return, no stopgap, growing figure) each turned the named cases red.
- `pnpm -F lab test`: 73 files, 748 tests passed. eslint, prettier, and deno fmt/lint on the dictionary are clean. The single eslint warning (`CommandPalette.tsx:76`) predates this branch.

title: Lab: preset picker, report drawer and a wider run column from the design handoff
description:
Carries the Claude Design handoff ("Arrowz workshop" project, `HANDOFF.md` + `lab-app.html`) into `apps/lab`. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-22-lab-presets-drawer-design.md`; plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-22-lab-presets-drawer.md`.

## What changes

- **Preset picker.** The scrolling strip of 26 chips becomes one trigger in the 38px row (`preset · Easy portrait · 25×50 ▾`, or `custom settings` with "edited since the last preset" beside it) and a panel with one column per level; each row shows its mode and size. Disclosure pattern (`aria-expanded` + `aria-controls`), arrow keys / Home / End inside the panel, Escape / outside press / choice close it. The panel's keys act only inside the strip.
- **Top bar** shows `Arrowz / W×H` only; the preset's name and "edited" moved to the picker (`presetsDirty` removed).
- **Report as a drawer** over the board on the stage's right edge: a 28px handle (44px on touch), slide 180ms (none under reduced motion), the report hidden only after the slide. Remembered in localStorage (`labReport`), hidden in solo, and not shown on the saved-boards tab, where the report is empty by design. **R** toggles it and **Escape** closes it on the lab tab; the ⌘K footer lists `r` there.
- **Run column** widened to `clamp(20rem, 22vw, 28rem)`; the command box grows with the column. One `CommandText` renderer (lab and saved-board detail) wraps the command only between flags, with names in `--ash` and values in `--ink`; a selection reads back as the one-line command.
- **Generate** in JetBrains Mono, 500, 13px, 44px, with its own focus ring.
- **Top-bar hover** is a fill (`--signal-fill-hover`) instead of an underline, for the segmented buttons and ⌘K. **Scrollbars** are thin, in `--border-strong`.

## Where this departs from the handoff (verified against the code)

- `.fw-cmd` is shared with the saved-board detail, so both render through `CommandText`. Wrapping uses inline layout instead of the handoff's flex-wrap, because white space between flex items is not rendered and a selection glued the flags together.
- The handoff's 12% `--ink` hover fill measures about 4.2:1 on `--signal-fill` (under AA); `--signal-fill-hover` is 4.61:1.
- `aria-haspopup="menu"` + `role="group"` contradicted each other; the picker is a disclosure.
- The preset panel got a `max-height` (pinned at 420×700); dead `.size` rules were dropped.

## Tests

- New layout invariants `popover-fit` and `drawer-fit`, matrix states `presets-open` and `report-open`, a dedicated `presets-open @ 420×700` case, a Polish trigger case at 420.
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache`: 21/21 tasks passed (run in a clean worktree). `deno task verify` (engine): 383 passed, 0 failed.
- Live pass in Chrome (EN and PL, 1440 and narrow): picker by mouse and keyboard, drawer by handle / R / Escape, reload, solo.

## Known and left for later

- Chrome derives accessible names with `text-transform` ("PRESET …", "REPORT"); the tests compute them without it.
- At 1440×900 the command box shows about 2.5 lines and scrolls inside itself.
- The open report scrolls sideways below about 380px (below the supported 420px).
- The `--ash` scrollbar-thumb hover applies in Safari only; Chromium ignores `::-webkit-scrollbar*` once `scrollbar-width` is set.

title: Fix the lab's visual defects and guard them with layout invariants
description:
Fixes the ten visual defects of the 2026-09-22 implementation review, adopts its knob-panel layout,
decides the Signal-plane contrast, and puts a layout-invariant browser test in front of all of it.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-22-lab-visual-fixes-design.md`.
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-22-lab-visual-fixes.md` (14 tasks, executed task by task with a
review after each, a whole-branch review, and a live pass in Chrome).

## What changed

**The test that guards it.** `LayoutInvariants.browser.test.tsx` mounts the whole app over a matrix of
states × viewports and asserts eight invariants: the document scrolls on neither axis, the board lies
inside its wrap, siblings of `.fw-lab` and `.fw-lib-detail` do not overlap, no button keeps the UA
border, every `aria-describedby` resolves, every visible text run clears 4.5:1, every control in the
top bar lies inside the bar, and no panel scrolls sideways. It started with today's failures listed by
defect id; each fix deleted its own entries first, watched the case go red, then fixed the defect.
`KNOWN_RED` is empty.

**The defects (P1–P10).** Visually hidden text no longer grows the document (`position: relative` on the
scrolling panels). The clamp notice and the violations get their own rows, so the board is whole. The
report column grows with the window and keeps deltas beside their values. The `edited` marker moved from
the preset strip to the top bar, where it no longer covers the last chips. The board detail is laid out in
rows instead of sticky buttons over scrolled content, and an empty or unreachable store drops the library
to one column. Four plain buttons got a class (`.fw .fw-btn`). The top bar gives way at 420px, in both
languages, instead of scrolling the document sideways. One dead background declaration is gone.

**Signal.** No text sits in or on `--signal`: three new `--signal-fill*` tokens carry `--ink` at AA, and
the top bar's opacity dimming is gone.

**Layout.** Knob cards have one rhythm (12/18/28px) and one control axis. Descriptions moved out of the
cards into a `dl.fw-kdesc` under each panel heading — hidden from the eye by the help switch, never from
the accessibility tree. The preview is four sections: geometry, drawing, points, colours. Touch targets
are 44px under `(pointer: coarse)`.

## Gates

`pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache` green (21 tasks). Engine `deno task test` 382/382. Lab suite
692 tests. A live pass in Chrome at 1280×800, 1024×768 and 420×900 checked every item the plan lists; it
found the two defects the tests could not see (a 22px description column and a dangling separator), and
both are fixed here.

title: Record the lab visual review and the waves it proposes
description: A read-only review against the Arrowz workshop reference: the chaos is structural (no spacing scale, two column grids, a 1fr/1fr height split, a flat type scale, seven renderings of selection), not a matter of colour. Findings carry measured evidence and file:line sources; the proposals group into a CSS-only wave, a component wave, and a design-first wave for features the reference never covered.

title: The command palette, and the two hotkeys its footer advertises
description:
Row 7 of the lab spec's §10 named three v2 additions — a run filmstrip, a parameter diff and a ⌘K palette. This branch delivers **the palette alone**, together with the two hotkeys its footer advertised but the application never had. The filmstrip and the diff keep their row; `Stage.tsx`'s empty rail and its guard stay reserved for them.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-21-lab-command-palette-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-lab-command-palette.md`.

## What it does

- **⌘K opens from every route**, the documentation included, because navigation is half of what it is for. It refuses nothing but a missing modifier, so it opens while a knob is being typed into.
- **The repertoire is what the lab already does**: run actions, the three tabs and both docs pages, the view and language switches, all 28 generator knobs (the `--start` pair as one row), the preview's five numbers and five flags, and 26 presets — about 74 rows, uncapped, scrolling in its own box.
- **A knob row jumps to that knob**: the rail switches, the focus lands on the control itself, and the knob's box carries a 1.2 s outline. From the saved boards or the docs the application returns to the lab first.
- **A row that cannot run stays listed and says why** — an idle Abort, a blocked Generate, the run rows during a carve.
- **`g` generates; `[` and `]` step the seed and carve it.** They live where `f` lives — the workspace, not the docs — and fall silent while the palette is open, because its search box is a field.

## What is deliberately absent

- **The two exports.** Each is a closure inside `ExportButtons` holding a worker or a per-board hash; a palette row could only reach them by clicking their button through the DOM. They stay one click away in the run column. Recorded in §4.
- **The mock's 40-row cap**, which would have hidden half this repertoire.

## Verification

- `deno task verify` 381 passed / 0 failed; `pnpm nx run-many -t verify --skip-nx-cache` 25/25.
- A manual pass in Chrome at 1280×800, 10 checks of 10: the trigger's appearance, the ranking of `seed`, the active row staying visible through 35 ArrowDown presses, jumps from both other tabs, the trigger toggling, five footer hints on the lab face against three on the docs, the hotkeys working outside the palette and inert inside its field, and Escape. Console clean.
- Every task was implemented test-first and reviewed on its own diff; a whole-branch review found four Important issues, all fixed and re-reviewed.

## Known and left

Three small things were judged non-blocking and are left on purpose: the palette's "skip the push when the route is already on screen" ships without a test of its own; the negative regex in `design/palette.test.ts` is whitespace-literal; and two older documentation drifts survive — §8 still names the field `focusKnob: RailTarget | null` where the code has `focusTarget: string | null`, and the plan still lists the `cmdSecPreset` key this work deleted.

title: Let the lab set the board's colours and its point grid, and start the store beside it
description:
Four reports from the same afternoon, after living with the palette work: the lab had no controls for the point grid while the element's own demo had three; a theme painted the board's paper but the frame around it stayed light; a custom palette offered no way to say what the background should be; and `pnpm nx serve lab` did not start the board store.

Three of them are one sentence said three times — **a colour the user chose does not reach every surface that should show it.** The fourth rides along because it is four lines of JSON.

## What changed

**The element** publishes the point-radius bounds it already clamped to (`POINT_RADIUS_RANGE`), and announces the paper it actually painted as the CSS custom property `--arrowz-paper`, written from the one place where precedence and sanitising have both run. Its `:host` background follows that property, so the letterbox around a board that does not fill its frame is the board's own colour.

**The lab** gains controls for the point grid — visibility, colour, radius — and for the board's paper and ink, built from the console's existing row shapes. The radius reads its bounds from the element rather than the engine's `VIEW_RANGE`, because the point grid is none of the engine's business: adding it to that table would have required a CLI flag and invalidated every board already in the store.

**A theme and custom colours now coexist.** The old rule cleared one when you set the other; it existed because a stated field beats a named theme, so holding both would have shown a theme the board was not drawing. Overriding field by field removes the premise — a chosen theme really is still supplying everything you did not override, so the picker tells the truth. Seven test cases that pinned the old rule were inverted rather than deleted, and every comment and help string that stated it was rewritten, in both languages.

**The link carries all five settings**, so a lab you paste into a fresh tab opens on the same board.

**`pnpm nx serve lab` starts the store** as a continuous Nx target. `verify` lists its dependencies explicitly, so the server cannot creep into the gate.

## The invariant worth knowing

The lab never states a colour field the user did not set. The element sanitises *after* precedence, so a stated empty string would beat a chosen theme and then fall back to the element's own default — silently turning a dark theme light. `''` means "not set" and is never handed over; the conditional spread is what enforces it, on both the live branch and the library preview.

## Verification

Both gates green at the final commit, run uncached: `deno task verify` 380 passed, `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` across 4 projects and 21 dependent tasks.

A live run in Chrome at 1400×900 checked what no test does: a dark theme with the surround matching the paper, a custom paper overriding a theme while the theme survives, the unset ink absent from the element's view rather than empty, the point grid visible once cells clear the element's 6px veto, and the whole state surviving a paste into a fresh tab.

That run also corrected a design assumption worth recording. `.fw-board` reads `--arrowz-paper`, but the element sets it on its own host — a child — and custom properties inherit downward, so the frame always resolves to its fallback. It makes no visible difference, because the element covers the frame and paints the paper itself; the comments and one test name that claimed otherwise were corrected rather than left to mislead.

## Notes

Three snippets the plan dictated verbatim could not work as written: a comment whose backticks closed a `css` tagged template, a test line that failed `tsc` because `Element` has no `.style`, and a DOM assignment that never reached React's `onChange` because of its value tracker. Each was fixed the way the surrounding code already documents.

title: Give the board a palette: twelve themes, a custom palette, and a repaint that skips the geometry
description:
`<arrowz-board>` can now be told which colours to draw its pieces in — either an array on the view, or the name of a theme that ships with the element — and it re-colours **without rebuilding its geometry**.

**Stacked on #86.** The base of this PR is `engine/one-palette`, not `main`: `packages/engine/colors.ts` comes from that PR. Merge this one into `engine/one-palette` first, then #86 into `main`.

## What it does

- **`palette.ts`** — assigns a colour index to every piece over the board's adjacency graph. Neighbours differ (0.2% of touching pairs share a colour at five colours, against ~20% for `id % n`), and every colour carries an even share. Computed over *all* pieces, never the drawn subset, so removing a piece never repaints the board.
- **`themes.ts`** — twelve themes ported from open-source editor themes, six light and six dark, each pair from one upstream project. Every arrow colour clears 3:1 against its own paper, every ink 4.5:1. `everforest-light` and `ayu-light` ship a single arrow colour by design: their accents are built for thin glyphs on near-white paper and only one of each clears the floor.
- **`BoardView.palette`** — validated colour by colour; a non-array container degrades to empty rather than throwing, like every other view field.
- **`GlLayer.setColors`** — re-uploads the colour buffers over the existing scene and reuses the assignment when the board and palette length are unchanged. Measured on the 1000×1000 board: **23.3 ms against 184.5 ms** for the full re-tesselation. This also repairs a cost that predates palettes — changing `ink` alone used to pay a full tesselation.
- **`theme` attribute** on the element, with precedence: an explicit field in `view` beats the named theme beats the element's own defaults.
- **The lab** — a theme picker with a swatch strip in both panels, an editable custom palette in the console (native colour inputs, capped at 8), both travelling in the URL hash, and a caveat where the SVG export lives.

## Out of scope, deliberately

The engine's export path is untouched: `toSvg`, `SvgOptions`, `View`, the board file and the golden hashes do not change, and the golden-hash tests pass unmoved. An exported SVG therefore keeps the golden angle and will not match a themed screen — the lab says so next to the download.

## Notes worth a reviewer's time

- `view.colored` turns out to be a **geometry** field, not a colour one: `strokeOf` widens a highlighted piece's stroke by 1.5× against 1.15×, which moves vertices. It is in the geometry key for that reason.
- A custom palette and a named theme are mutually exclusive, enforced in the lab's store slice. The first colour added turns arrow colouring on — that lives in the editor's own action, so restoring a link that states `colored: false` is not overridden.
- The design doc records what shipped, and its §2 inventory is explicitly the before-picture with refreshed line numbers.

## Verification

Both gates green on the final commit: `deno task verify` 380 passed / 0 failed, `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` across 4 projects and 25 tasks, lab suite 533 tests.

Executed as nine TDD tasks plus a three-task addendum, each reviewed; three whole-branch reviews produced one Critical and eight Important findings, all fixed and re-reviewed. A live run in Chrome confirmed the themes, the strip, the auto-enable, the mutual exclusion and a link reproducing a custom palette in a fresh tab.

title: Give the engine one palette, and colour an SVG by piece id
description:
The diagnostic hue lived twice. The board element computed it from a piece's
id (`view.ts`); `toSvg` computed it from the piece's position in
`board.pieces` (`engine.ts`). A board file keeps the ids it was written with,
and `decodeBoard` accepts gaps in them — it checks an id for being
non-negative, unique and below the cell count, and for nothing else — so one
board could be drawn in one set of colours on screen and exported in another.

Measured on a board of the ids 5 and 7, the shape `decodeBoard` admits:

| source | colours |
|---|---|
| `toSvg`, from the index | `hsl(0 …)`, `hsl(137.508 …)` |
| the element, from the id | `hsl(327.54 …)`, `hsl(242.556 …)` |

## What changed

`packages/engine/colors.ts` owns the formula now, the way `geometry.ts` owns
the shapes: it imports nothing, so `engine.ts`, `command.ts` and the board
element can all reach it. `toSvg` calls `hueOf(pc.id)`; `view.ts` re-exports
the three functions from `@arrowz/engine`, so the element's public surface and
its consumers (`gl-color.ts`, `tesselate.ts`) are unchanged. The new module
reports where a new engine file must: the `NEUTRAL` list of `neutral.test.ts`,
the `include` of `tsconfig.build.json` and `mod.ts`.

## Why no golden moves

Measured **before** the change, not argued: the generator numbers a piece by
the length of the array (`engine.ts:1358`) and backtracking only pops the last
one, so every generated board has `id === index`. The golden `colored-stick`
case and all seventeen coloured recipes of `docs/images/manifest.json` showed
no divergence. No hash in `svg-golden.json` and no README image moves —
`svg-golden` confirms it after the change.

The divergence itself was deliberate, not accidental: the board-game spec of
2026-09-10 moved the element's hue to the id and recorded that "the CLI's
`toSvg` is a separate code path and stays byte-identical". This closes it.

## Tests

- `colors.test.ts` — four checks the element's `view.test.ts` used to carry for
  its own copy; `view.test.ts` stays, and now proves the re-export is this code.
- `engine.test.ts` — `toSvg` colours a piece by its id, on a hand-built board
  whose ids are 5 and 7, with a negative control for the colours an
