  index-based hue would print.

Both new assertions were proved by mutation: putting the index back reddens the
toSvg test, and moving `HUE_STEP` to 137.5 reddens `colors.test.ts` and the
`colored-stick` golden.

Gates: `deno task verify` 379/0, `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` 25 tasks.

title: Narrow the head bounds to what stays readable
description:
Reported from the lab: the view fields still accept values nobody can read. A
head two squares wide and two tall sits in a cell that is one.

| field | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `stroke` | 0.2..0.9 | unchanged — narrowed in #82 |
| `headWidth` | 0..**2** | 0..**0.9** |
| `headHeight` | 0..**2** | 0..**1.2** |

Both floors stay at 0: `--arrow-width=0` means automatic, and `--arrow-height=0`
is the tip of no height the prose documents on purpose.

## Why they were too wide, and why that was my mistake

#82 set these ceilings to the biggest head the READMEs draw
(`--arrow-width=2 --arrow-height=2`), so that a documented picture would keep
working. That inverted what a documented extreme is for: the page prints an
exaggerated head to show what exaggeration looks like — it is not evidence that
the value is sensible.

The bound now comes from where a tip stops reading as a tip. `0.9` is the
element demo's own slider bound, where the effect is watched rather than argued
about; `1.2` is a little past one whole square, room for a deliberately tall
head and short of a spike reaching over the piece behind it.

**So the picture moved instead of the bound.** `head-big` is rebuilt at
`--arrow-width=0.9 --arrow-height=1.2` — the ceiling of both fields — and both
READMEs caption it accordingly. It was rebuilt through `deno task docs head-big`,
so the SVG, the PNG and the manifest agree.

## What followed, including one I did not expect

The knob table, the CLI help and the lab's fields all read the range from
`VIEW_RANGE`, so they follow by themselves. Three places did not:

- the store's refusal message (`0..2` → `0..1.2`), pinned as a literal on
  purpose because that case is about the exact wording;
- **`carve.test.ts`**, which drew the documented big head with `--arrow-width=2`
  as a value that must pass — found by grepping every occurrence rather than
  only the documentation. It now exercises both ends of the bounds instead of
  one: the ceiling pair `0.9 / 1.2` and the floor `--arrow-height=0`;
- the manifest the picture is rebuilt from.

The engine's own tests needed no change: the largest values they use are
`--arrow-width=0.8` and `--arrow-height=1.2`, and the latter is exactly the new
ceiling.

## Gates

`deno task verify` 374 passed, 0 failed. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` 25 tasks.
The lab cases that read `VIEW_RANGE` pass too (17 of 17).

title: Record the seeds that turned four refusals into ordinary jams
description:
Last item of the engine hardening area, and it turned out to be a measurement
question rather than a code one. **No rule changed here** — only the campaign
data did, and the comments that quoted it.

## What the list claimed

`CONSERVATIVE` named nine settings the straightness floor refuses although round
14 saw them close every board it gave them. Six of the nine stood on **three**
runs and three on **four**. A setting that really closes eight boards in ten
shows a clean sweep of three about half the time, so "always closed" was a claim
the sample could not carry.

## What fifteen seeds each said

| setting | campaign | now | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `500/0.65/3/10` | 4/4 | **6/7** | jams (seed 7, 21 258 cells left) |
| `500/0.7/2/10` | 4/4 | **4/5** | jams (seed 5, 8 952) |
| `600/0.75/2/10` | 4/4 | **13/14** | jams (seed 14, 15 899) |
| `700/0.65/4/6` | 3/3 | **6/7** | jams (seed 7, 4 606) |
| `1000/0.7/8/6` | 3/3 | **15/15** | holds |
| `1000/0.8/4/8` | 3/3 | **15/15** | holds |
| `1000/0.8/4/10` | 3/3 | **15/15** | holds |
| `1000/0.85/2/6` | 3/3 | **15/15** | holds |
| `1000/0.85/3/8` | 3/3 | **15/15** | holds |

Four were never excessive refusals — the rule was right about them. They now
carry the runs that found the jams, which moves them under the test demanding
that **every** jam be refused, so that test gets wider rather than narrower.

The five that survived are all 1000 a side. That is the opposite of where the
thin grid was suspected: the backlog pointed at "the corners 500 and 1000", and
1000 did not move under five times the sample.

Seeds start at 1, so the first three or four runs of each setting reproduced the
recorded campaign result before anything new was read — if they had disagreed,
the harness would have been wrong and none of the rest worth having.

## Can a different shape buy the five back? No

Measured separately, with no boards carved: the model first reproduced today's
rule exactly (zero leaks, exactly those five refusals), then searched the
step-shaped family the backlog suggested — the winding knobs moving the step
count instead of multiplying the side.

19 260 shapes leak nothing, and the cheapest of them costs **12** excess
refusals against today's **5**. None of them buys back a single one of the five;
each adds seven more at 300–600. The multiplicative form is not "multiplicative
for no reason" — it is simply better here.

So the five are a confirmed price, not a debt waiting to be paid, and closing
that backlog item is the honest outcome.

## Gates

`deno task verify` 374 passed, 0 failed. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` 25 tasks.
Both spike scripts were throwaway and are deleted; the raw measurement is in
`/tmp/arrowz-straight-floor/nine-deepened.jsonl` (108 rows).

title: Narrow the view bounds to what stays readable
description:
Second item of the engine hardening area. `VIEW_RANGE` described what the
drawing code can survive, not what a reader can see: `stroke` went to 2 — a line
twice as wide as its own cell, which swallows the tip it is meant to carry — and
the head fields to 3.

**Base is `engine/seed-range` (PR #81)**, not `main`: same area, and that PR is
still open.

| field | was | now | where the bound comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stroke` | 0.05..2 | **0.2..0.9** | the element demo, where a person watches the effect while dragging |
| `headWidth` | 0..3 | **0..2** | the biggest head the READMEs draw; 0 stays, it means automatic |
| `headHeight` | 0..3 | **0..2** | the same picture; 0 stays, the prose documents it on purpose |
| `cell`, `top` | — | unchanged | the demo has no control for either, so there is no second opinion |

## Why not the demo's head bounds

`0..0.9` and `0.1..1` were the obvious candidate — the demo's own numbers — and
are deliberately **not** used. They would:

- refuse `head-big.png`, which `docs/images/manifest.json` rebuilds and a test
  re-runs through the parser;
- delete a documented case, `--arrow-height=0`;
- break two values the engine's own tests exercise (`--arrow-height=1.2`,
  `--arrow-height=0`).

A bound that refuses the pictures its own repository ships is not a readability
bound. The table's comments carried that anchoring all along — *"README's
biggest head is 2"*, *"which README shows on purpose"* — while the numbers
beside them said 3. They agree now.

## Proof

Both ends are held by a picture the docs rebuild, not by a literal someone chose:

| mutation | reddens |
|---|---|
| ceiling to 1 | four cases, naming `head-big: --arrow-height=2 is outside 0..1`, the store's refusal message, and two engine cases built on `1.2` |
| floor to 0.3 | one case, naming `weight-thin: --line=0.2 is outside 0.3..0.9` |

Both mutations were reverted before committing, checked by a condition in the
commit script.

## Two echoes, and why one keeps its literal

`store-server.test.ts` pins the refusal message (`0..2`) as a literal on
purpose: that case is about the exact wording the server returns, so reading the
number back from the table would make it agree with itself.

`ViewPanel.browser.test.tsx` went the other way — it asserted `toBe(2)` under a
comment reading "2 is `VIEW_RANGE.stroke.max`". The case is about the field
clamping before its owner sees the value, whatever the bound is, so it now reads
the bound from the table.

## Gates

`deno task verify` 374 passed, 0 failed. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` 25 tasks.

title: Widen the seed to the ceiling the generator actually has
description:
First item of the engine hardening area. `max: 999999` was the first lab
field's arbitrary limit, justified by no commit and no spec. The generator's
real ceiling is `mulberry32`, which keeps 32 bits of state (`seed >>> 0`), so
2**32 wraps back to 0.

A million is thin for randomly drawn seeds: a repeat becomes likelier than not
after roughly 1200 draws, against roughly 77 000 now.

**Boards are untouched.** The same seed still runs through the same
`mulberry32`, so every recorded fingerprint reproduces and 0..999999 keeps
meaning exactly what it meant.

## What followed by itself, and what did not

The knob table, the CLI help and the lab's own docs page all read the range from
`PARAM_SPEC` through `rangeText`, so they needed no edit. What did:

- the boundary case in `carve.test.ts`
- the knob table row in **both** READMEs
- the prose in both READMEs — a third copy of the range, two screens above the
  table, that **nothing read**. Widening the ceiling left both pages saying
  "0 to 999999" while the table two screens down said otherwise.

That paragraph now has a guard of its own. It is found by an anchor rather than
by its heading, for the same reason the tables are: the headings are translated,
the machine numbers are not.

## The lab draws differently now

`Math.floor(Math.random() * 999999)` could not reach the top even of the range it
was written for. `getRandomValues` fills exactly the 32 bits the knob now allows.

This splits a stub that used to do two jobs: one pinned `Math.random` fed both
the drawn seed and the recipe's draw. The seed pinned in that case sits past the
old 999999 ceiling on purpose, so the case also says the widening reached the
lab rather than stopping at the engine.

Two comments made false by the change are rewritten rather than left: the seed
no longer "came from Math.random", and the draw's range is no longer a subset of
the knob's — it is now exactly the knob's.

## Proof

| mutation | reddens |
|---|---|
| ceiling back to `999999` | five cases: the boundary, both knob tables, **both paragraphs** |
| one digit wrong in the English paragraph | that paragraph alone — the Polish one stays green |
| the old `Math.random` expression | case 14, `expected 499999 to be 3000000000` |

The first says no one of those five places is a dead literal; the second says the
new guard reads the paragraph of its own file. All mutations were reverted before
committing, checked by a condition in the commit script.

## Out of scope

The restart spacing (`seed + attempt * 999983`) is deliberately untouched. It
mixes seeds after a restart, so changing it would move boards that already have
recorded fingerprints — a different decision from widening an input range.

## Gates

`deno task verify` 374 passed, 0 failed. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` 25 tasks.

title: Guard the four documentation columns that were blind
description:
§3.3 of the PR 6 spec names four columns of the element reference that no guard
read: `type`, `def`, `signature` and `detail`. `DEFAULT_PAD` could change to 6,
an event could gain a field, a signature could describe a method that no longer
exists — all with both gates green. This closes all four.

**Base is `lab/debt-and-details` (PR #78)**, not `main`: that PR touches
`docs-api.browser.test.ts` too. Rebase onto `main` once #78 merges.

## Three columns from the text (engine, Deno)

- **`type`** from the `declare` lines of the class.
- **`signature`** from the parser that already read those lines and threw the
  tail away — a method's whole head, a getter's return type, which is what the
  rows carry for each.
- **`detail`** from the event types, compared as field names.

**`lang` is excused from `type` by key, not by rule.** It is `noAccessor`, so
the native `HTMLElement.lang` stays in force and there is nothing for the class
to declare. "A property with no declare line" as a *class* would wave through
the next property that simply forgets one. The exception carries a negative
control: a key excused there that has since gained a declare line fails the
test, so the excuse cannot outlive its reason.

**Both comparisons resolve one-line type aliases first.** A reference table may
spell what an alias stands for rather than its name — `gestureMode` is exactly
that (`get gestureMode(): GestureMode` against a row reading `'drag' | 'click'`),
and measured, the only such row of eleven. Resolving rather than hard-coding
keeps the alias itself under guard.

## The fourth column from a real element (board-element, browser)

`def` is the one column whose truth is a **value**, not a declaration, which is
why it is read off a fresh `<arrowz-board>` rather than parsed in the engine's
text test. A parser would confirm that the constructor says
`this.pad = DEFAULT_PAD` and that the constant reads 4 — and would walk past the
day a default starts being computed. A fresh element cannot: it holds whatever
it really holds.

## Proof

Each guard was measured against the assertion named for it, with the rest of the
file green:

| mutation | reddens |
|---|---|
| `GestureMode` widened to `'drag' \| 'click' \| 'pen'` | `signature of gestureMode` |
| `declare enableColors: boolean \| null` | `type of enableColors` |
| a field added to `FinishedEvent` | `detail of finished` |
| `DEFAULT_PAD = 6` | `default of pad` |

The first also proves the alias is guarded rather than merely substituted. All
four mutations were reverted before committing, checked by a condition in the
commit script; the tree is clean.

## Out of scope

The element README is a second, unguarded copy of the same information, and it
has already drifted: it says `board` is `Board | null` where the table says
`BoardData | null`. That divergence is recorded in `lab-docs.ts` and stays a
known debt rather than a silent one.

## Gates

`deno task verify` 372 passed, 0 failed. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` 25 tasks.

title: Close the lab debt and details left by PR 6
description:
Six items, each named and located by the backlog note after PR 6, and none of
them a design question. The first is the only defect a user of the lab could
meet; the rest are guards that claimed more than they checked.

## The hotkey (`App.tsx`)

`useSoloKey` sifted out modifiers, key repeat and editable targets, but not two
cases that reach a document listener anyway:

- **`isComposing`** — an IME sends the keystrokes of the character being
  composed, so `f` on its way into a character toggled the view instead of
  becoming text. The same reason a field is refused, arriving through a
  different door.
- **`defaultPrevented`** — a listener on the document sees an event whatever
  anyone closer to the keystroke already did with it, so a key someone else had
  consumed toggled solo as well.

Each refusal is proven separately: with only `isComposing` added, the
`defaultPrevented` assertion still failed, so neither is written green. The test
produces `defaultPrevented` from a capture listener one step earlier, the way a
real handler would, because it is not a field of `KeyboardEventInit`.

## Four guards that did less than their names

- **`ReportPanel`** read a computed style off `head instanceof HTMLElement ?
  head : document.body`. `<body>` has a computed style too, so a heading that
  stopped rendering would have left the case measuring the document instead of
  going red. Now a throwing helper, like `stats` and `row` beside it. Measured
  by dropping the heading's id: "the longest-pieces heading is not on the page".
- **`ElementDocs`** is named for the machine columns staying put across a
  language switch and sampled one column of one row. `mono` is the class those
  columns wear and the description column does not, so both directions now
  cover every row of all three tables. Measured: translating the `def` column
  leaves the old assertion green — it read the type column — and turns the new
  one red over 70 cells.
- **`docs-api`** held two independent checks in one test: the per-key loop that
  catches a lying attribute mapping, and the `observedAttributes` comparison
  that catches an attribute the page never mentions. A loop stops at the first
  row it dislikes, so one wrong mapping left the second check unreached.
  Measured by swapping `show-points` and `point-color` between two rows: the
  loop goes red and, split apart, the set comparison runs and stays green.
- **`node-smoke.mjs`** had two idioms for one counter and a third that exited on
  the spot, so a failing documentation check reported "golden board(s) differ
  under Node" and sent the reader to the wrong file.

## The shared `pre` box (`docs.css`)

`.fw-docs-term` repeated all eight declarations of `.fw-docs-code` bar the
bottom margin. A shared `.fw-docs-pre` carries the box and each block keeps its
own name, rather than the two collapsing into one: the docs route tests tell the
element page and the CLI page apart by `pre.fw-docs-code` against
`pre.fw-docs-term`, so a single merged name would have cost the routes their
marker to save eight declarations. `white-space: pre` stays with the terminal
block alone, where the measured sideways scrolling leans on it.

## Gates

`deno task verify` 369 passed, 0 failed. `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` 25 tasks,
lab 491 of 491. Every mutation above was reverted before committing; the tree is
clean.

title: Fill the docs tab with the element's API and the CLI's help
description:
Fills the lab's Docs tab with the element's API and the CLI's help, and guards both against the code they describe.

Stacked on `lab/retire-old-lab` (#75), so this PR's base is that branch, not `main`.

## What it adds

**One home for the documentation text.** `packages/engine/lab-docs.ts` is a new runtime-neutral engine module reachable as `@arrowz/engine/docs`. The machine columns — key, type, attribute, default, signature, detail — exist once and are not translated; only the descriptions have two languages, which is the rule `readme.test.ts` already states for the knob tables. The row tables are `as const satisfies` rather than annotated: an annotation collapses the key type to `string` and takes the compiler's parity guarantee with it.

**Two guards, each in the environment that can see what it checks.** TypeScript erases `private`, so at runtime a private method is an ordinary prototype property; Lit rewrites `static properties` in place when it finalises a class, adding `attribute: false` to every `state` entry, so the runtime shape is not what the author wrote. Neither question can be asked honestly in the other's environment:

- `packages/engine/lab-docs.test.ts` parses the element's **source declarations** and answers "is anything public undocumented?" — set equality in both directions, not containment.
- `packages/board-element/src/docs-api.browser.test.ts` asks the **runtime class** "does everything documented exist, and does each documented attribute match what its property declares?" — the guard lives in that package because it has `lit`, so the declaration type needs no cast.

Attributes are compared **per key**, never as sets: a table that swaps `show-points` and `point-color` between two rows leaves the set unchanged while the mapping lies.

**The route.** `/docs/element` and `/docs/cli`, with a `<nav>` of two `NavLink`s between them. Links rather than a radio group, because a documentation page has an address worth copying, middle-clicking and opening in a new tab; `NavLink` rather than a plain anchor, because an anchor reloads the document and takes the run in flight and the board's WebGL context with it. The bare `/docs` used to fall to the wildcard and land the reader in the lab; it now redirects, as does an unknown page name, which the wildcard cannot catch once `/docs/:what` has matched.

**The two pages.** The element's API as three reference tables plus a runnable example; the CLI's help **called** from `helpText()` at render rather than generated at build time. A prebuild would add the first generated source file in the repository, and four of `apps/lab`'s six targets would fail without it — while `lint` and `fmt` would inspect it only in some of its shapes (a generated `.ts` is caught by both, a `.json` by Prettier alone, a `.txt` by neither).

**Two accessibility debts**, unrelated to the feature but paid here because this is the PR that touches the lab's document structure: `aria-keyshortcuts="f"` on the board's solo toggle, whose name already says "key F" in prose, and the lab's first `h1`, so the report's heading can drop from `h3` to `h2` and the levels stop skipping.

## Departures from the lab spec, amended in it

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-13-lab-react-app-design.md` said the help would be generated and that a test would parse the event map. Both sentences are now amended: the help is called, and the guard reaches past the event map to the properties and members, split across two packages by what each environment can see.

## What the guards do not cover

Names and attributes only. `type`, `def`, `signature` and `detail` are unguarded — `DEFAULT_PAD` could become 6, or an event gain a field, with both guards green. This is recorded in the design spec's blind-spot list rather than left for a reader to discover. `kind` is compared, since the member parser already captures the `get`.

## Verification

- `deno task verify`: 369 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify`: 4 projects, 25 tasks.
- Every guard direction was proven by mutation and each mutation restored: a documented private member, documented internal state, a swapped attribute column, a deleted event, a getter documented as a method, and an explicitly `public` method the parser used to drop silently.

One defect is worth naming because no per-task review could have seen it: the docs panel did not scroll inside itself, and `/docs/cli` stretched the whole shell to 2018px at a 1280px viewport. It was the composition of three individually correct commits — the markup, an `overflow-y: auto` with no height, and a `white-space: pre` block 1978px wide. The test meant to catch it asserted the computed `overflow-x` declaration, which was true the whole time. The assertions now measure the effect: `scrollWidth > clientWidth` on the block, and the document not scrolling at all.

title: Retire the old Deno lab page
description:
Retires the old Deno lab page now that the React lab in `apps/lab` has reached parity with it, and leaves behind a store server that says what it is, a build-output proof that the React lab still carves the engine's boards, and documentation that describes one lab rather than two.

## What changed

**Added** — `apps/lab/scripts/worker-smoke.mjs` and the Nx target `lab:smoke`: it runs the worker chunk `vite build` emits and compares its board with the engine's own, in plain Node. It comes **first** in the branch on purpose: it is the successor to `packages/cli/lab-bundle.test.ts`, and from the moment that test is deleted nothing else proves a bundler kept the engine intact. `lab:verify` depends on it and `ci.yml` names it, so it runs by default.

**Deleted** — `packages/cli/lab.html`, `lab-page.ts`, `lab-worker.ts`, `lab-bundle.test.ts`; the `bundle` task in both `deno.json` files and its place in the root `verify`; the `bundle` target in `packages/cli/project.json` and in `ci.yml`; `lab.html` from `fmt.exclude`; the `board-element` implicit dependency of `packages/cli`, which existed only because the deleted bundle imported it; and `carve.test.ts`'s "every picture field of the lab stays inside the CLI range", which parsed `min`/`max` out of HTML with a regular expression. That last deletion costs no coverage: `ViewNumberField` reads each bound from `VIEW_RANGE` where it renders the field, and `ViewPanel.browser.test.tsx` holds the rendered attributes against the table.

**Narrowed and renamed** — `lab-server.ts` → `store-server.ts` (`createLabServer` → `createStoreServer`), `lab.sh` → `store.sh`, `deno task lab` → `deno task store`. The router now serves one area, `/store/`, plus the store's API; the page and `/dist/` areas are gone, `LAB_CSP` became the far stricter `API_CSP`, and `MIME` holds only what a stored file can be. The script's read permission narrowed from the package directory to the store, and the store's path is absolutised and exported so the grant and the directory the server opens are one string.

**Guarded** — the rule "the DOM belongs to no file here" used to carry an exception for the deleted page; `neutral.test.ts` now applies a DOM-only pattern set to `packages/cli` instead (`Deno.` deliberately excluded — that package is a Deno program).

**Documented** — both READMEs and `CLAUDE.md` describe one lab, with the two commands it takes to run it.

## Two things the diff does not say

1. **The comment sweep (the last six commits) is not in the spec.** §10 row 8 covers everything else; removing stale pointers to the deleted files from ~147 comment sites across 73 files was a decision taken during planning, not a requirement. A reviewer is entitled to know it was chosen rather than owed.
2. **Those commits are behaviour-free by construction** and can be read last, or skipped. Their rule was narrow: remove the pointer, keep the reason. Test titles changed (nine of them named the retired page) and one setup-failure string; no assertion, selector, constant or condition moved. The proof is the count of passing tests, identical before and after: 468 in 58 files for the lab, 362 for the Deno suite, 272 for the engine.

## Evidence

Both gates pass on the tip: `deno task verify` (362 tests, and visibly without a bundle step) and `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` (4 projects, including `lab:smoke`). The smoke was shown to bite: mutating the worker's seed reddens exactly three of its five checks.

Run by hand as well, against a copy of the store in a temporary directory: the store answers on 8777 and 404s at its root, `http://localhost:8779/api/boards` reaches it through the proxy — the check that the rename did not break the lab — and generating a board took the store from five files to six, with the freshly drawn seed on disk and listed in the library after a refresh.

## Known follow-ups, deliberately not in this PR

- `neutral.test.ts`'s walk is not recursive, so `packages/cli/scripts/` sits outside the new guard while `CLAUDE.md` states the rule for the whole package.
- `apps/lab/vite.proxy.ts` still exports `LAB_SERVER`; its doc comment already says "where `deno task store` listens". Renaming an identifier inside a behaviour-free sweep would have cost the property that made a 73-file diff reviewable.
- `store.sh` itself is covered by no gate: its permission narrowing and its port pin rest on measurement, not on a test.
- `store.ts`'s `exists()` swallows every `Deno.stat` error, including a permission denial, so an empty listing is not proof that a read succeeded.
- `packages/engine/HISTORY.md` still names `deno task bundle`. It is the engineering log and describes the repository as it was, deliberately left alone.

One correction worth naming: the spec's row 8 originally justified the deleted CLI test by pointing at `viewFields.ts`, which holds no bounds by design. The spec is fixed in this branch. The plan's Ruling 7 repeats the original error and was left as written — it is the record of what was decided, and the defect is worth remembering.

title: The board library, part two: the detail under the list
description:
The saved-boards tab gets the detail of the open board: the command the store
holds for it, its three view numbers and two view flags, *Load into lab*, and a
two-click delete. **Parity with the old lab is reached here**, which is what
spec §10's row 5b means by it — not at PR 4, as the first draft of the spec had
it.

Fourth in the stack: `#71` → `#72` → this. Base is `lab/library-debt`.

## What it adds

The panel's track becomes a two-row grid — the list scrolls, the detail stays
beneath it — because the detail's two actions have to stay reachable while forty
rows scroll past. The edited view lives in `result.preview.meta`, which is what
`BoardFrame` already draws a stored board from, so the redraw costs nothing and
there is no second copy of a stored board's view. `ViewNumberField` and
`ViewFlagSwitch` stop reading the store and take a value and a callback, which is
how the library's three fields keep the `VIEW_RANGE` bounds after `carve.test.ts`
dies with `lab.html` in PR 8 — the commitment recorded in PR #65.

It also pays three debts PR 5a recorded against itself: one answer about a size
the store has not got (the chips and the list could disagree), the third status
state (`loadingBoard` had been in the dictionary, unused, since 5a), and three
regions that all answered to the name "Saved boards".

## How it was built

Spec amended first (§5.1, §5.3, §5.6, §7.2, §10), then a plan of eleven tasks,
then **three rounds of adversarial plan review** — the third mutating every
repair from the second — and only then execution, one fresh implementer per task
with a scoped review after each.

That process is the reason this description can be specific about what nearly
went wrong. Ten defects were found and fixed, and **every one of them was in the
plan rather than in an implementation**. The three worth naming:

- **A pending view save wrote one board's view onto another board's file.** One
  click on another row both blurs the field — which commits the edit and arms the
  350 ms timer — and changes the address, and a local store answers well inside
  that pause. The write took the view from the closure but the board from the
  stage. It now captures the edited board at commit time.
- **A delete could report success while doing nothing.** It addressed the board by
  rebuilding `WxH` from the meta, while every read path uses the directory the
  store listed; for a board in a folder named `08x08` the request went to the
  wrong path, came back 404, and a 404 counts as "gone" — so the line said
  "Deleted", the listing refreshed, and the board was still on disk. It uses the
  address now.
- **A test could not see the regression it guarded.** The accessibility case
  asserted the three new region names but never the absence of the old one, so it
  passed just as well with four regions, three of them correct.

Two pieces of module-level state are deliberate and documented where they live:
the debounce timer in `useViewSave.ts` and the fade timer in `notices.ts`. Both
replaced a React effect whose cleanup ran on every render — measured, not
suspected: the debounce never fired at all, one edit posted twice, and after a
delete the flush re-POSTed the board, which the store wrote back to disk.

## Gates

Both green on the final commit, run on this branch rather than reported from a
task:

- `deno task verify` — 365 passed, 0 failed, CLI bundle intact (the old lab still
  builds; retiring it is PR 8's job, and nothing here touches it)
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` — 4 projects, 21 tasks; lab 468 tests across 58
  files, `check`, `lint` and `fmt` clean

## Still to do by hand

The nine-item browser pass from the plan's "Before the pull request" — two of its
items are things no test covers: that the list really scrolls under the pinned
detail at 860×900, and that the old lab still saves and reads a board.

title: Clear six recorded debts from the board library
description:
Six debts recorded during PR 5a's reviews, cleared one commit per item. **Stacked on `lab/board-library`** (#71), because every item touches files that exist only there; GitHub will retarget this to `main` when #71 merges.

| Commit | Item |
|---|---|
| `625dd21` | `boardError` becomes `BoardError { name; reason }` — the `split(': ')`/`rejoin` seam between two modules is gone |
| `2269539` | `vite.config.ts` names `./vite.proxy.ts` with its extension, which Vite's coming native config loader requires |
| `c0a7087` | `BoardList` hangs its rows off `entry` itself, dropping a fallback that would have built `/boards//<id>` |
| `30dc25d` | A cancelled listing ends its own wait: new `listDropped()` clears only `loading` |
| `7ba6b5c` | **No change** to `packages/board-element/vitest.config.ts` — a comment recording the measurement that says why it needs none |
| `6a50273` | The plan's "known flake" paragraph corrected: it was wrong, and it cost this branch two red CI runs |

## Why the first one goes now

`boardError` joined an address and a reason with `: `, and `RunStatusBar` tore the string apart again — a contract between two modules about a separator that also occurs inside a reason. PR 5b adds a detail panel that would be a **third** reader. Fixing it after that costs three call sites instead of two.

The case built around a reason containing `': '` (`HTTP 500: gateway down`) is kept: with the split gone it asserts the same property directly rather than through the seam.

## Two items worth reading rather than skimming

**`7ba6b5c` changes no configuration on purpose.** `packages/board-element/vitest.config.ts` was flagged as carrying the same optimizer trap that made CI fail twice on 5a. It cannot: that trap needs a dependency no source names, and every bare module those tests reach — `lit`, and the engine as a workspace link — is named by source the first-pass scan sees. Measured twice from cold (`rm -rf node_modules/.vite`, 17 files / 270 tests, nothing discovered late). The commit is the measurement, so the question is not reopened.

**`6a50273` corrects documentation that actively misled.** The paragraph said the iframe failure was a flake and told the reader not to debug it. It is deterministic on a cold optimizer cache, re-running never cleared it, and the 2026-09-14 run it leaned on (`34891181090`) was a different failure — a `LabRoute` assertion, no iframe timeout. The paragraph is corrected in place rather than deleted, so anyone meeting the failure in an older checkout finds the explanation.

## Verification

- **Cold run** (`rm -rf apps/lab/node_modules/.vite` first): **55 files, 417 tests**, no iframe timeout, no optimizer reload.
- `deno task verify` — exit 0, 365 passed, bundle emitted.
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` — exit 0, 4 projects, 21 tasks.

Items 2, 4 and 5 were each measured both ways: the warning present without the extension and absent with it; the new guard test red with `listDropped()` stubbed out and green restored; two cold board-element runs before concluding no change was needed.

title: The board library, part one: the workspace and the list
description:
Closes spec §10 row 5a.

The saved boards get a tab that shows them: size chips, a list, refresh, and the chosen board drawn on the lab's own stage — without a second `<arrowz-board>`.

## The shape of it

`LabRoute` becomes `Workspace`: **one panel serving two tabs**, mounted under `/` and `/boards` alike and hidden only under `/docs`, so the stage is the same DOM node on both. That matters because the stage holds `<arrowz-board>` and its WebGL2 context, which a remount would dispose. `Console` gains a third face — chips in the rail, the list in the panel — while the run column stays mounted and is **hidden by a class rather than replaced**: it holds a keyboard focus on Generate and its own transition ref, and a carve started in the lab can still be running when the library is opened.

The chosen board **is the address**: `/boards/:size/:id`, read with `useMatch`. To free that path, the Deno lab server's static area moved from `/boards/` to `/store/`; the directory on disk and the `/api/boards` JSON API are unchanged. A stored board lands in `result.preview`, beside and never instead of the run's `shown`, because a stored board has no run behind it and cannot fill a report. It is drawn under its own saved view, named in the status line, and the report column is empty while it is on screen.

The stage asks **the route** (`useInLibrary`), not "is there a preview", for what to draw, what view to draw it under, and what the status line says.

## Gates

- `deno task verify` — 365 passed, 0 failed, plus bundle
- `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` — 25/25
- `pnpm nx test lab` — 54 files, 416 tests

Both gate logs were grepped for warnings: the only notice is Deno's unconditional `deno bundle is experimental`, which pre-dates this branch.

## By-hand browser pass

Run at 1400×900 against a live store, per the plan's pre-PR checklist. **13 items passed**, including the three the automated suite could not reach on its own:

- a size chip keeps the board already open when it belongs to that size, and jumps to the first board of another size;
- returning to the Lab tab restores the lab's own board, annotation and report with nothing of the stored board left behind;
- the old lab (`/lab.html`) both saves to and reads from the moved `/store/` path.

**Three items are not verified** and are left for a human:

- everything at 860×900 — the automation could not shrink the page viewport below 1262px, so the `≤900px` media query never engaged. This includes the simple view on the library tab and the narrow-width rail.
- "the progress line resumes after returning to the Lab tab" — the 600×600 carve finished while the library was on screen, so the completed line was observed instead.

## Known follow-ups, deliberately not in this PR

- `useLibraryList` leaves `loading: true` after a cancelled fetch — latent today, since nothing renders it.
- `boardError` is a stringly-typed contract: `useStoredBoard` writes `<size>/<id>: <reason>` and `RunStatusBar` splits at the first `: `. Worth a typed field before PR 5b adds a third reader.
- Three regions share the accessible name "Saved boards" (chips group, list section, tab). Fixing it needs dictionary entries this plan forbade.
- `BoardList`'s `entry?.size ?? ''` is an unreachable fallback that would build `/boards//<id>` if it were reached.

## One note on the last commit

A by-hand observation appeared to show the list emptying after a failed refresh. It did not: instrumented measurement showed the real path keeps the rows, and the recorded DOM belonged to a page whose lifetime began with the store already down. No defect, no fix.

The investigation did surface a real gap, and the last commit closes it: nothing covered the requirement that the fetch path must not turn a dead store into a *successful empty listing*. A slice case driving `listFailed` by hand cannot see which outcome `listBoards` hands over. Verified by mutation — `if (!response.ok) return { ok: true, sizes: [] }` turns the new browser case red while all four slice cases stay green.

title: Name a board's layout by a canonical SHA-256, and key the store by it
description:
A board's arrangement of arrows now has one name, whatever seed and parameters produced it: `sha256-<64 lowercase hex>`, the layout hash. "Has this layout been generated before?" becomes "does this file exist?", with no database.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-15-layout-hash-design.md` (revision 3). Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-15-layout-hash.md`, executed task by task, each task reviewed.

## What changed

- **Engine** — `layoutHash(board): Promise<string>` beside the board-file codec, over a canonical form that leaves out piece ids and carving order: the ASCII tag `arrowz-layout/1`, varints W, H and the piece count, pieces ascending by head cell (head index, `length * 4 + dir`, 2-bit step codes zero-padded per piece), then the void count and absolute void indices. `fingerprint` and the board file format are untouched. Every golden board now records its layout hash beside its fingerprint, checked in Deno and under Node.
- **Store** — `saveBoard` is asynchronous and returns `{ meta, layoutExisted, recipeExisted }`. Files are named by the layout, and `BoardMeta.sources` lists every recipe (seed + parameters) that produced it. A recipe's key is `boardId(params)`, so re-saving with the same parameters replaces that recipe instead of appending one — the old lab's view edits re-post, and would otherwise multiply recipes. The board file is written only when the layout is new, so a stored name keeps one byte sequence and one fingerprint: `loadSession` refuses a saved game whose snapshot fingerprint moved.
- **CLI** — `--count=N` counts only new layouts; a seed whose layout is already stored still has its recipe saved, is named on stderr, and the batch moves on within the existing seed limit. Single runs report `layout already stored, recipe added|updated`; `--dry-run` reports the layout hash as `id`.
- **Lab** — the board-file download is named `sha256-<hex>.board.json`. The hash is asynchronous and a download must start inside its click, so it is computed when the board arrives and the button waits for it; a hash for a board that has since been replaced is dropped, and a hash that cannot be computed (no secure context) says so under its own dictionary key rather than in the SVG export's error line.
- **Docs** — both READMEs describe the new rule, and `readme.test.ts` now carves the documented boards and asserts that the names they print really are those boards' layout hashes.

## Evidence

- `deno task verify` and `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` pass on the head commit.
- The 15 golden boards' recorded hashes match, string for string, values computed independently from the spec's text by two reviewers, in Deno and in Node.
- Checked live: a second batch over the same seeds prints `batch: 3/3 boards written, 6 seeds tried, already stored: 1 2 3`; a 6x6 board carved with `restarts` 3 and then 0 lands in one file with two recipes; a view edit from the library keeps the recipe count and leaves the board file's fingerprint alone; the lab's downloaded board file is byte-for-byte the store's file, and its name equals the layout hash recomputed from its own contents.

## Notes for review

- A meta that is missing or unreadable beside a present board file makes the next save rewrite that file with its own numbering. The spec defines newness by the meta, and `listBoards` never lists a file without its meta, so such a file is not "stored" by the store's own definition. Called out because it is the one place where a stored name's byte sequence can move.
- No migration: boards under the old `seed<N>-<hash>` names stay on disk, unlisted and untouched.
- A known race is left open, as the spec accepts: the CLI and the lab server saving the same layout at the same moment keep one of the two recipes.

title: The generator lab as a React application: the report, the exports and solo
description:
## What this adds

PR 4b of the React lab (`apps/lab`), stacked on `lab/simple-view` (merge base
`1ffb0d6`). Both gates pass at the head of the branch: `deno task verify` (352
tests) and `pnpm nx run-many -t verify` (4 projects, 21 tasks).

- **A `result` slice and a store-level `completeRun`.** The run slice keeps only
  the process; the board, its report and its file live in `result`, written
  together with the run's end in one update. A run in flight keeps the last
  result on screen.
- **The report column.** Statistics with the change against the last result
  that had metrics (`reportDelta`, moved into the engine's `lab-report.ts`,
  which the old lab now uses too) and the longest pieces. It is the stage's
  third column above 900px and a row under the board at 900px and below.
- **Both exports** in the run column, in both views: Download SVG, drawn in a
  throw-away worker, and Download board file, the same bytes the store writes.
- **The annotation** `W×H · seed N` in the frame's top-left corner, naming the
  board on screen (during a run, the previous one).
- **Solo:** the `⛶` toggle in the frame's top-right corner and the `f` key
  give the board the whole lab panel, remounting nothing.
- **The command box's floor** (`min-height: calc(1lh + 6px + 58px)` on
  `.fw-cmdfig`), so the box never paints behind Generate.

This closes spec §10 row 4b. Parity with today's lab is still PR 5.

## Rulings

1. **The command box's floor applies at every width, not only at ≤900px.**
   With the exports in the column, 1400×900 in the advanced view overlapped
   Generate by 66.9px (by 16.9px at 1400×1000); the floor gives the figure
   84.4px, no overlap at 1400×900, 1400×1000 or 860×900 in either view, and
   Generate moves 0px as the command grows. `flex: none` at ≤900px fixed 860
   but not 1400 and moved Generate 4.8px; `min-height: auto` moved it 81.5px.
   Spec §10 is amended.
2. **The report row at ≤900px is sized by the stage's rows, not by a
   `max-height`.** Measured at 860 wide from 650 to 1100 high: a fixed 73px cap
   kept the board whole at 860×900 and clipped it at every lower height; a bare
   `minmax(292px, 2fr)` pushed the wrap up to 25.4px into the console.
   `minmax(min(292px, 100%), 2fr) minmax(0, 1fr)` (and `minmax(0, 2fr)
   minmax(0, 1fr)` below 700px of height) keeps the board at 260px inside its
   wrap with a 73/92px report at 860×900, gives the report 80/86px under a
   128/141px board at 860×650, and falls back to today's board exactly where
   today's layout already clips, the report shrinking to its padding under the
   console. Spec §5.2 is amended.
3. The solo toggle is `⛶`, not `⤢` (the element's own fit button); it is named
   `fullView` ("Full view (key F)") and carries `aria-pressed`.
4. The delta cell always prints its sign, and a hidden word only for better or
   worse (`deltaBetter`, `deltaWorse`); a neutral row says nothing more.
5. A result without metrics shows no statistics table but still shows the
   longest pieces, as the old lab ends up showing (`lab-page.ts:814-816`).
6. `completeRun` throws for a run that was never started, rather than invent
   parameters to show the board under.
7. One SVG export at a time: only the SVG button is disabled while its worker
   draws; an export error sits under the two buttons in a `role="alert"`
   paragraph and is cleared by the next SVG export, or when another board
   replaces the one it was about. It is the result slice's (`exportError`),
   behind the same identity guard as the store's answer, so a failure that
   lands after its board was replaced is dropped and no replaced board is kept.
8. The download anchor is attached to the document for the length of its
   click, so the click is an ordinary document event a test can observe.
9. The `f` listener lives in `App`, is attached only on the lab route, toggles
   from a focused button, and skips `input`, `textarea`, `select`,
   `contenteditable`, modifiers and key repeat.
10. The annotation is not in caps and takes no pointer events, so a drag that
    starts on it still pans the board.
11. Whole-app test helpers live in `src/harness/mountApp.tsx` for this PR's new
    files; the older route tests keep their own resets.
12. The statistics labels are row headers (`<th scope="row">`).

## Parity deltas a reviewer must judge

- A run in flight keeps the last result on screen; the skeleton cleared it.
- The board file download is new; the old lab downloads only the SVG.
- The export error sits under the export buttons, not in the run status.
- `f` ignores modifiers, key repeat, `select` and `contenteditable`, where the
  old lab toggled on ⌘F as well.
- The statistics labels are row headers.

## What this changes for test authors

- `run.board`, `run.file`, `run.report`, `run.saved`, `run.finished` and
  `run.stored` are gone.
- A test that finishes a run calls `completeRun` after `run.started`, and
  resets `result` beside `run`.
- A test that waits for a save waits for a file other than the one before
  (`savedAfter` in `LabRoute.browser.test.tsx`), because a run in flight no
  longer clears the answer.
- Layout cases set their own viewport: `page.viewport` outlives the case that
  set it.

## Browser pass

Chrome through the DevTools protocol against `pnpm nx serve lab` and
`sh packages/cli/lab.sh`, sized with device emulation at a device scale factor
of 1. The page restored a 25×50 seed 7 board from its address, so the runs
below are seed 7.

1. **A run in flight keeps the last result.** From 25×50 to 600×600, sampled
   every 40ms through the whole run (about 2.3s, ~60 samples each) at
   1400×900 and 860×900 in both views: every sample showed the same
   `<arrowz-board>`, the annotation `25×50 · seed 7`, the 25×50 report and both
   export buttons enabled; when the run finished, all four described 600×600.
   The advanced view was started with Generate (`auto` off); the simple view
   runs a committed size at once, so there the run was started by the address.
2. **Deltas.** The 600×600 report shows 19 signed deltas, coloured by
   direction: better `rgb(237, 238, 242)` (`--ink`), worse
   `rgb(222, 92, 78)` (`--error`), neutral `rgb(138, 143, 153)` (`--ash`).
   Switching to Polish kept all 23 delta cells (text and class) row for row
   and translated all 24 row labels, the heading and the hidden words
   (`lepiej`).
3. **Exports**, observed by intercepting the anchor's click and its Blob:
   Download SVG gave `arrowz-600x600-seed7.svg`, `image/svg+xml`, 8,876,976
   bytes, an `<svg>` root that parses and decodes as an image (1806×1806).
   Download board file gave `seed7-e672d126.board.json`, 292,900 bytes, and
   `cmp` against `packages/cli/boards/600x600/seed7-e672d126.board.json` found
   it identical. The SVG export took 436ms at 600×600; for that time only the
   SVG button was disabled, never the board-file button.
4. **The report row at 860 wide** (report box / content shown; board height):
   - advanced: 900 → 73.1px, 22.4px of the first row, board 260px inside;
     850 → 48.1px, 22.4px; 800 → 24px padding only; 760 → 24px padding only,
     overflowing 20.9px under the console, where `elementFromPoint` hits the
     console; 650 → 80px, 22.4px, under a 128.1px board.
   - simple: 900 → 92.1px, 22.4px; 850 → 67.1px, 22.4px; 800 → 42.1px, a
     clipped 18.1px of the first row; 760 → 24px padding only (1.9px under the
     console, which paints there); 650 → 86.4px, 22.4px, under a 140.7px board.
   At every height the board lies inside its wrap, the report scrolls inside
   itself (e.g. 73 of 822px), and from 900 to 760 the board keeps 260px and a
   knob row stays whole.
5. **The command box** ends 12px above Generate at 860×900 in both views and at
   1400×900 in both views. With a 386-character command it scrolls inside
   itself (56 of 387px at 1400×900 advanced; 56 of 102px at 860×900) and
   Generate's offset in the run column does not move (110.4px in the advanced
   view at 1400×900, and in both views at 860×900). In the simple view at
   1400×900 it moves 23.2px, the follow-up below.
6. **Solo.** From the corner button and from `f`, at 1400×900 and 860×900 in
   both views, `.fw-boardwrap` equals `.fw-lab` (1400×770.2, 860×770.2) and the
   element is 34px narrower and shorter; the element, its canvas and the run
   column are the same nodes. ⌘F (a trusted `Meta+f` and a synthetic one),
   Escape and a repeated `f` leave solo on; a focus on Generate lands on the
   toggle after `f`. In solo the element's zoom in and a drag change its view,
   and its fit restores the fitted view. Fit refits on the way in (cell
   5.726px → 12.693px at 1400 advanced, 4.448 → 12.693 at 860) and back on the
   way out. The browser's own find bar cannot be observed through the protocol.
7. **Console** after a fresh load: one warning, the `willReadFrequently`
   readback warning from the board element's colour sampling, and one error,
   the browser's 404 for `/favicon.ico` (`apps/lab` has no icon, unchanged by
   this branch). No React DevTools, Vite debug or "Lit is in dev mode" lines
   were captured by the protocol's console listing; no application errors.

## Follow-ups

- In the simple view above 900px Generate still moves as the command grows
  (24.5px at 1400×900 measured before this branch's change; 23.2px in this
  pass), untouched by this PR.
- `workerError` is still unreachable from the status line.
- The §7.1 `--signal` pair is still open.

## Not here

- The library (PR 5).
- The docs route (PR 6).
- The filmstrip, the diff strip and ⌘K (PR 7).

title: The generator lab as a React application: the simple view and the language switch
description:
## What this adds The React lab gains the top bar's right group: a **View** radio group (Simple / Advanced) and a **Language** radio group (PL / EN). The simple view is the old lab's recipe — width, height, two 0–100 sliders with their end words, the skeleton choice, the seed, and "randomise the settings on every generate" — drawn over the six preview fields the old lab keeps visible in simple mode. The language switch renames every visible string, sets `` and the board element's `lang`, and travels in the hash. Under the hood: `lang` and `recipe` slices and `ui.mode`, remembered under the old lab's own keys (`labLang`, `labSimple`, `labView`) through one guarded storage helper; one debounce for a typed knob and for a recipe edit; the knob's draft entry lifted into `DraftNumber`; `Segmented` as the one radio-group primitive; `SimplePanel` inside the one `Console`, with the run column kept as the same node in both views; the simple halves of every §2.2 trigger, and the whole 18-case trigger table as one test file. This closes spec §10 row **4a**. Parity with today's lab is still PR 5 (the library); the spec's row 4 is split in this PR. ## Rulings (plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-14-lab-simple-view.md`) 1. **PR 4 is two pull requests** — 4a (this one: language switch and simple view) and 4b (report, SVG export, solo and `f`). *User's decision.* 2. **A first visit opens on the simple view**, as the old lab does; the whole-app test files set the advanced view in their reset. *User's decision.* 3. **One debounce owner** — `useAutoRun` watches `params.edits` (gated by `auto`) and `recipe.edits` (ungated); a recipe edit leaves a debt only a cancel erases. *User's decision.* 4. **The recipe writes the knobs at once, through the machine path** (`setMany` → `raiseClamped` → `cell`); the simple seed commits on Enter or blur, not per keystroke. 5. **The draw's moves are not shown** — 0/162 recipes move without randomising, 320 of 32 400 draws move `wMid` by hundredths with it; the command already shows the moved value. *User's decision.* 6. **The page owns `lang` in the hash**; a link's language is applied through `setLang`, so it is remembered; `labLang` is written by a choice, a link, or any reload — only a first visit leaves storage empty. 7. **One `Console`, two interiors, and §5.1 is amended** — React reconciles by type and position, so a second console component would remount the run column. 8. **A segmented choice is a radio group** with the visible text as its accessible name (`PL`, `EN`); arrows, Home and End move the choice. 9. **The simple view shows the old lab's preview subset** — `stroke`, `headWidth`, `headHeight`, `rounded`, `colored`, `hilite`; `cell`, `voids`, `top`, `auto`, `help` and the preset strip are hidden. 10. **The simple panel spans the first two tracks, and `.fw-lab.simple` drops the preset row**, so the stage does not collapse into the `auto` row. 11. **A page "opened from a link" is one whose hash decoded**, whether or not it named a knob; the recipe is then not applied. 12. **The skeleton radios run on arrow keys as well as on clicks**; arrowing across two options starts two runs, the second terminating the first. 13. **On the top bar's Signal plane the segment inverts, and so does the focus ring** — unselected `--void` on `--signal`, selected `--ink` on `--void`, ring `--void`. 14. **Preferences are read and written through one guarded helper**; an unreadable preference is the default, never an exception. ## Parity deltas a reviewer must judge rather than skim - **`labLang` is written by a choice, a link, or any reload — not by a first visit** (Ruling 6): `useUrlHash.ts` applies any decoded `lang` through `setLang`, which writes storage, and the page writes its own hash at mount, so every reload after the first visit rewrites `labLang`; a link that says `en` writes `labLang: en` the same way, as the old lab's `applyLanguage` does (measured: `{}` after a first load, `labLang: pl` after a click, `labLang: en` after opening a link naming it). - **The skeleton radios run on arrow keys** (Ruling 12): the old lab's buttons ran on click only. - **The simple view's seed commits on Enter or blur** (Ruling 4): the old field wrote on every keystroke, so the command and the hash follow a typed seed at its commit. ## What this changes for test authors - **A first visit opens the simple view** (Ruling 2), where PR #66's lab opened only on the advanced view. `LabRoute.browser.test.tsx`, `triggers.browser.test.tsx` and `RunColumn.browser.test.tsx` — which mount the whole app or the column — now set `ui.setMode('advanced')` in their reset. ## Shared with the old lab Both labs read and write `labLang`, `labView` and `labSimple` on purpose — a preference and a recipe are meant to travel between them — so a reviewer switching between the two should expect a choice made in one to open the other the same way. ## The §5.1 correction (Ruling 7) §5.1 said the run column stays one instance because the route builds it and hands it to "whichever console is on screen". React keeps a node by its type and its position among its siblings, not by the identity of the element object: `{col}` replaced by `{col}` is a new parent, and the column remounts — losing a focus a keyboard user left on Generate and the column's `wasRunning` ref. `Console` therefore swaps only its first two tracks and keeps `children` in the third position in both views. The test is `LabRoute.browser.test.tsx` — "the simple view replaces the rail and the presets, and keeps the very same run column" — which looks the column up before the swap and compares by node identity after it. **The mutation that turns it red:** in `Console.tsx`, return `
{children}
` for the simple mode, so `children` moves from the third position to the second (Task 10, Step 9). The spec's §5.1, §5.2, §2.2 and §10 are amended in the last commit. ## Two harness facts Task 1 pins - **Browser test files share `localStorage`** — one origin for every file, so a key written by one file was read back by the next (measured 2026-09-14). `vitest.setup.ts` clears storage, and it runs before a file's own imports, which is when the store reads its three preferences (measured the same day: the next file read the key back as `null` at import). `harness/storage-a` and `storage-b` are the two-file probe. - **Vitest's Chromium takes the machine's locale** — measured `pl-PL` on the maintainer's machine, where the lab opens in Polish and every English-name lookup fails. `vitest.config.ts` pins `contextOptions.locale: 'en-US'`; `storage-b` asserts `navigator.language === 'en-US'`. ## Browser pass (Task 12, Chrome via chrome-devtools MCP, `localStorage` cleared, 1400×900 and 860×900) 1. **First visit** — opens on the simple view, in Polish (`navigator.language` `pl-PL`), and draws the board without a click at both widths; storage stays empty after the load. 2. **Tracks** — at 1400 the simple panel is `grid-column: 1 / 3` over the `168px 1014px 216px` console (1183px wide), the run column the 216px third track; at 860 the console is the 900px query's `150px 709px`, the panel spans both (860px) and the run column is `1 / -1`, a full-width row beneath (y 710, 190px tall). 3. **Stage height** — simple view 385px at both widths; advanced view 366px at both widths (38px preset strip above it). All above 180px. 4. **Contrast**, read back from a 1×1 canvas: unselected `--void` (14,15,18) on `--signal` (94,106,210) = **4.08:1**; selected `--ink` (237,238,242) on `--void` = **16.53:1**. The 4.08:1 is under AA for the 12px text — the pairing `.name` and `.dims` already ship with and the open §7.1 item. 5. **Focus ring** — Tab from the page lands on the checked View radio; `:focus-visible` matches and the ring is `2px solid rgb(14,15,18)` (`--void`) with a 2px offset on the `--signal` plane, at both widths. 6. **Slider and Generate** — four `input` events on a recipe slider moved the CLI command each time; exactly one worker `generate` post followed, 350ms after the last edit (344ms and 350ms in the two runs). Generate with randomising on gave three different boards on `--seed=7` (one worker post each). 7. **Polish** — switching renames all 40 visible page strings and all 7 strings of the board element's control bar ("Drag to pan" → "Przeciągnij, aby przesunąć", the zoom titles); `document.documentElement.lang` and the board's `lang` follow. A reload keeps Polish, the simple view and the recipe (lengths 80, randomising on). 8. **Link** — the address bar's link opened in a new tab reproduces the knobs (the randomised command byte for byte) and the language (English from the link although storage said `pl`), and does not apply the recipe. 9. **Console** — no errors. Vite's two debug lines, React DevTools' info line, "Lit is in dev mode" and a Canvas2D `willReadFrequently` warning from the board element's colour parsing (`gl-color.ts:45`, older than this branch). No `favicon.ico` 404 appeared in Chrome's console list. Seen and not fixed here: at 860 the run column's row is 190px tall and the CLI box (`.fw-cmdfig`, `flex: 0 1 auto`) shrinks to 8px while its `
` keeps `min-height: 58px` and paints behind Generate — in both views. `run.css` and the 900px query are untouched on this branch (`run.css` last changed at `89d1f21` on `lab/run-triggers`), so it predates 4a and is listed for a follow-up.

## Follow-ups

- The ≤900px layout where the CLI box paints behind Generate — predates this branch: `run.css` is unchanged since `lab/run-triggers`.
- The 4.08:1 contrast of the top bar's unselected radio (Ruling 13, the open §7.1 item), so later chips do not inherit it.
- `SimplePanel` and `ViewPanel` both mount `ViewNumberField` with `view-*` ids — fine while only one interior shows at a time, but PR 5's library detail will need an id prefix.

## Not here

- The report with both delta baselines, the SVG export, the solo view and `f` — **PR 4b**.
- The library — **PR 5**, where parity with today's lab is reached.
- The docs route — **PR 6**.
- The filmstrip, the diff strip and ⌘K — **PR 7**.

title: The generator lab as a React application: what starts a run
description:
## What this adds

Everything that starts a run in the advanced lab, and the state the run is
started from. Spec §10's row 3 lists the console in two halves; PR 3a shipped
the first (group rail, knob grid, sliders, view panel, violations panel), and
this PR closes the **second**: the lifted run column with Generate, New seed,
Defaults and Abort, the `auto` and `help` switches, the live command string
with its copy button, the preset strip, the clamp notice, the run status bar's
refusal and big-board warnings, and the URL hash codec with `hashchange` → run.
The lab also now opens on a board instead of on an empty stage, which is §2.2's
last row.

Spec §2.2's trigger table is stated as a test of its own —
`apps/lab/src/run/triggers.browser.test.tsx`, one case per row this PR owns —
and each case asserts both halves of the row: when the run starts, and whether
the knobs were rewritten before it did.

**Parity with today's lab is still PR 5**, not this one and not PR 4. Units 11
and 12 of the monorepo spec are the library, and that is where parity lands.

## The fourteen rulings

1. **SVG export is not here.** Spec §10 puts it in row 4 beside the report it
   shares a worker idiom with; the previous plan promised it in the run column
   and the spec wins. The mock's *Download board file* exists in no version of
   the lab and is a mock invention.
2. **`RunColumn` is a child of `Console`, not a sibling.** `LabRoute` renders
   `<Console>{<RunColumn … />}</Console>`, so PR 4's simple console places the
   very same element and cannot fork it.
3. **The human path and the machine path are different slice methods.** `set`
   and `setStart` increment `params.edits`; `setMany` and `reset` do not, and
   `auto` watches `edits` alone. Without the split a preset, Defaults, a link
   and New seed would each run immediately *and* schedule a second run 350 ms
   later that terminates the first mid-carve. The consequence a reader trips
   over: New seed writes its seed with `setMany({ seed })`.
4. **Every trigger funnels through one `start()`**, and that is where the
   refusal and the debounce cancellation live — the port of `lab-page.ts:869`.
   A disabled button is right for a button and useless for `auto` and for a
   link arriving from another window.
5. **The hash is written with `replaceState`, debounced, and guarded against
   its own writes.** See the parity deltas below.
6. **The hash mirrors the console, not the last run**, and survives a route
   change. See the parity deltas below.
7. **The wire format does not change.** `#` + `encodeURIComponent(JSON.
   stringify({ ...params, __view: { … } }))`, so links pass between the
   deployed Deno lab and this one in both directions. `lang` and `tab` belong
   to PR 4 and PR 5 and are carried through verbatim in an opaque `carried`
   field; `voids` is absent in the old lab and stays absent.
8. **The preset strip lists modes under level labels**, and the accessible name
   carries what the visible label drops: 26 chips reading `25×50 · square`
   would be unreadable, so each chip shows its mode and is named
   `<Level> <W>×<H> <mode>`. The level label is a flat `aria-hidden` sibling
   span, as `GroupRail.tsx` already does — not a `::before`, which would hide
   the text from find-in-page, selection and translation.
9. **`help` hides descriptions from the eye and keeps them for a screen
   reader.** See the parity deltas below.
10. **A preset writes every knob, seed included**, and the *edited* marker
    follows `findPreset`, which compares only the preset's own override keys.
    See the parity deltas below.
11. **Neither the debounce nor the hash writer subscribes in render.** Both
    watch state that moves about sixty times a second during a slider drag, so
    both hold `useStore.subscribe` inside an effect with a stable dependency
    list. A selector in `Shell` would repaint the whole shell on every tick.
12. **Hook tests use `renderHook`**, not a probe component: a `let held: T |
    null = null` captured in a callback narrows to `never` after the null
    check and cannot pass `check`.
13. **The refusal gets a voice, and a big board gets its warning back.**
    `useRun` refuses silently, which is right for the funnel and wrong for the
    person, so `RunStatusBar` prints `generateBlocked` while the knobs are
    refused and the slice is idle, and `generatingBig` above 200 000 cells.
14. **The `f` hotkey and the solo view are PR 4's**, stated in writing. §10
    restored them in prose and assigned them to no row; this PR amends §10's
    row 4 to name them. The preset name in the top bar *is* this PR's, because
    this PR is what makes a preset knowable.

## Four parity deltas to judge rather than skim

These are deliberate departures from today's lab. Each is defensible and none
is accidental; if one of them is wrong, it is wrong here and not in a later PR.

1. **The hash mirrors the console, not the last run** (Ruling 6). The old lab
   writes the hash inside `run()` and `redraw()`, so with `auto` off a copied
   link carries the knobs of the *last board* rather than the ones on screen.
   This PR writes it from a store subscription, for the reason the old lab
   already states for the command string (`lab-page.ts:741`): a URL that
   disagrees with the command box beside it is the worse inconsistency. The
   cost, named: after editing knobs without generating, the link reproduces
   what is configured, not what is drawn.
2. **`replaceState` instead of a pushed entry** (Ruling 5). Back is no longer
   an undo for a knob edit. Three routes share this history, and an entry per
   edit would stop Back from returning to `/boards`; the undo belongs with
   PR 7's run filmstrip, where a run's history is the thing being navigated.
3. **`help` hides descriptions from the eye and keeps them for a screen
   reader** (Ruling 9). The old lab's `body.nohelp .help { display: none }`
   took them from both, and kept the violation visible only because it was a
   `::before` on the hidden element — an accident of CSS a React port cannot
   reproduce. Three things follow: the reason is a separate span that is never
   hidden, `aria-describedby` becomes unconditional, and a link carrying
   `help:false` no longer strips every knob's description from the recipient's
   screen reader. The switch says *show*, which is a visual verb, and that is
   now what it means.
4. **Choosing a preset resets the seed** (Ruling 10), so two presets cannot be
   compared on one seed. `lab-presets.ts` defines an option as "engine defaults
   + these overrides, so choosing one never inherits knobs left over from the
   previous experiment", and the old lab implements exactly that; spec §7.3's
   line about wholesale replacement is about the mock's own
   `resetAll`/`presetId` inconsistency, not the engine's contract.

## The load run, and the four assertions it moved

`Shell` gains one effect after `useUrlHash`, so a pasted link is in the store
before the run starts. It is **deliberately unguarded**, against the plan's own
text: `useGenerator` registers `useEffect(() => kill, [kill])`, and `kill()`
terminates the worker without touching the store, so after StrictMode's
simulated cleanup the slice sits at `phase: 'running'` with a dead worker and a
surviving ref would leave it there forever — on the real dev page, since
`main.tsx` wraps `<App/>` in StrictMode. Measured: with the guard in place the
StrictMode case fails at 30 244 ms. The rule that came out of it: guard an
effect whose side effect is durable and non-idempotent (`useUrlHash`'s read
writes into zustand, which survives the unmount); do not guard one whose side
effect a sibling cleanup undoes.

Four assertions in `LabRoute.browser.test.tsx` assumed an idle page and had to
move. None was weakened:

1. *Generate carves a board, draws it, and says so* opened on
   `toHaveTextContent('Press "Generate".')` — an assertion that the page had
   **not** run. It now polls to `done` and matches `/^Board closed 100%\./`,
   which claims that a run started unasked, finished, and reported. A later
   review found the same case would then pass with `onClick` deleted from
   Generate, because the phase is already `done` when the click lands, so it
   now captures `run.file` before the press and polls for a different one.
2. and 3. *a finished run is offered to the store once per run* keeps its POST
   counts at 1 and 2. What moved is the `fetch` spy: the mount is hoisted above
   it and the load run's own save is awaited first, so the spy observes a quiet
   page. Raising the counts to 2 and 3 would have made them depend on whether
   an asynchronous POST landed inside the window.
4. *the saved board carries the view on screen* keeps `expect(posts).
   toHaveLength(1)` for the same reason, and is stronger in practice: the
   length assertion now also excludes the one POST guaranteed to be in flight,
   so every body assertion reads the press the case made.

Measured, not assumed: the load board is the default 25×50 and finishes in
roughly 40 ms, inside a click's own actionability wait. The whole file costs
about 1.3 s more than before, spread over eleven mounts. Four cases gained a
poll on `run.phase`; one of those is a correctness fix rather than a timing one
(`RunColumn` disables Generate for `running || blocked`, so *Generate is refused
while a rule is broken* would otherwise have passed on the load run rather than
on the violation).

## Deliberately not here

- **PR 4:** the simple view, the language switch, the report with both delta
  baselines, the SVG export — and, as of this PR's spec amendment, the `f`
  hotkey and the solo view.
- **PR 5:** the library (list, size chips, refresh, detail, its own view
  fields, copy, load into lab, two-click delete). Parity lands here.
- **PR 6:** the docs route.
- **PR 7:** the run filmstrip, the parameter diff strip and the ⌘K palette.

## Three hand-offs PR 4 will want

1. **§2.2's page-load row needs "unless the hash carried knobs".** The old lab
   applies the simple recipe before running only when the link carried none
   (`lab-page.ts:1480`). `useUrlHash` currently exposes nothing a caller can
   read for that — it consumes the payload internally — so PR 4 will need it to
   report whether a link was applied.
2. **§5.2 hides `auto` and `help` in simple mode, and both switches live in the
   shared `RunColumn`.** By Ruling 2 the simple console places the same
   element, so the hiding has to happen inside the column rather than by
   forking it.
3. **Spec §8 asks for the trigger table as node unit tests; Task 14 writes
   browser tests.** Six of the eight triggers are buttons, and three of the
   rows assert the knobs at the moment a click starts a run. The three
   simple-view rows PR 4 adds will belong in the same file for the same
   reason.

## Gates

`pnpm nx run lab:test` — 36 files, 231 tests, all passing. `check`, `lint` and
`fmt` clean for `apps/lab`.

## What the final whole-branch review changed

A critical review of the finished branch found one production bug, two false
statements in the repository, and one mechanism a later task had quietly made
unreachable. All four are fixed in the last six commits.

- **`useUrlHash` swallowed the first traversal onto any fragment it wrote.**
  The `written` ref came from the old Deno lab, which writes the fragment with
  `location.hash = …` — an assignment that echoes a `hashchange` and so spends
  the ref. This hook writes with `replaceState`, which never fires one, so the
  ref was never spent: a knob edit armed it, a pasted link was applied and run,
  the following `flush()` early-returned without clearing it, and the next Back
  onto that fragment was swallowed — address bar saying one board, page showing
  another. The ref is gone. The listener now compares the fragment against what
  the **store** holds, which cannot go stale and additionally stops a traversal
  onto an already-current fragment from terminating a carve in flight (§8).
- **The refusal line was unreachable on a loaded page.** `generateBlocked`
  printed only while the run slice was idle, and the load run of §2.2's last row
  makes `done` the resting state of every session. With `auto` on, a knob
  dragged into a violation refused silently while the bar reported a closed
  board. The refusal now outranks every phase except a run actually in flight.
- **Spec §5.1 and §5.2 described the opposite of what shipped** — a two-track
  `Console` with the run column lifted above it. Ruling 2's structure is right;
  the spec text was not amended with it. Both are now amended, with the reason.
- **The command box clipped about two thirds of the command**, in a box whose
  stated job is to show exactly what would be run. It scrolls.

Two smaller corrections of the same kind: a test comment cited a precedent that
did not match the file it named, and a CSS comment stated the wrong mechanism
for an out-of-flow box.

## Known and deliberately shipped

- The selected preset chip is `--void` on `--signal` at 12px, which measures
  4.08:1 where AA wants 4.5:1, and `.fw-top .preset` at `opacity: .8` measures
  3.35:1. The pairing is §7.1's own and `.fw-go` already ships it at ~4.03:1;
  no value on that dial reaches AA below 18.66px bold, so a chip-only patch
  would only make the strip and Generate disagree. This wants a token or a
  pairing decided once in §7.1 and applied to all of them.
- The 26 chips are 26 tab stops ahead of the stage and the console. A
  `role="toolbar"` with a roving `tabindex` is the standard answer and is a
  follow-up, not a blocker.

title: The generator lab as a React application: the parameter console
description:
The lab's advanced console, ported to `apps/lab`: twenty-eight generator knobs in six groups, the nine preview fields beside them, every rule violation and every inactive reason on screen, and a Generate that refuses exactly what the engine would refuse.

This is the first half of spec §10 row 3. The second half — the run column, the live command, `auto`, presets and the URL hash — gets its own plan. Parity with today's lab still arrives at PR 5, exactly as §10 says.

Third on the stack: base is `lab/app-skeleton`. When #63 and #64 merge, rebase and re-target at `main`.

## What it adds

Three store slices carry what the old lab kept in the DOM:

- **`params`** owns the twenty-eight knobs, runs `clampParam` on commit, and recomputes three per-key indexes — violations, inactive reasons, rule floors — once per change. They are sparse on purpose: a knob with nothing to say has no entry, so its selector reads `undefined` twice running and does not render again. A slider drag redraws one knob, not twenty-eight.
- **`view`** gives the nine preview fields typed values, read through `viewNumberOf` exactly once, on commit. §2.3 calls this the main trap of the port: today those controls have no variable at all.
- **`ui`** holds which rail entry is open, and nothing else.

The console itself is the mock's two-track layout: a 168px group rail carrying per-group violation counts, and a panel showing one group at a time (or the preview fields, which the mock calls the *element* section).

## The rulings a reviewer should attack

1. **`KnobSlider` is a styled native `<input type="range">`**, not a `div` with `role="slider"`. A native range input *is* `role="slider"`, and brings arrow keys, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, touch and the platform's value announcement with it. The mock's bar is a `div` with a pointer handler and no keyboard at all.
2. **The mock's pointer scrub on the number is dropped.** A mouse-only gesture with no keyboard equivalent. Its two jobs are covered by the slider and by the inline entry. The cost is paid explicitly: swapping a button for an input and back moves focus twice, so the knob restores focus to the number on commit, and tests it.
3. **The rail is a vertical `role="tablist"`**, not the mock's `<nav>` with `aria-current`. Picking an entry replaces the panel beside it and leaves exactly one visible — that is the tab pattern. It copies all of `TabRow.tsx`'s behaviour, focus management included.
4. **The violations list lives under the console**, not inside the knob panel: one group is on screen at a time, so a violation in `lengths` must stay readable while `shape` is open. The rail's count says *where*, the list says *what*.
5. **A violation is `--error`; a rule bound is `--warn`.** The mock has no error state for a knob at all. Using warn for both would make "your board will not generate" and "here is a bound" the same colour.
6. **An inactive knob is dimmed and explained but not `aria-disabled`**, though spec §7.2's table asks for it. The knob still works, still stores its value, and still matters the moment the knob that disabled it moves; announcing it as disabled would announce something false. The half of §7.2 that *is* kept — the reason via `aria-describedby` — now reaches the slider, the number and the inline entry.
7. **`Shell`'s `params` prop is deleted rather than kept as an override.** Two sources for one value is the bug §2.3 describes in the old lab.

## Found by opening the page, not by the suite

The branch's CSS had never been rendered — the browser tests import no stylesheet. Opening it caught one real defect:
