title: CLI: store boards that do not close, abort on a time budget, trace once a second
description:
## Why

The measurement tooling of the archived branch `archive/worktree-jam-preview` (Node era, never merged) ported to Deno. Three things main lacked, found while auditing the `archive/*` tags: a jammed board left no picture behind (the CLI exited 1 and wrote nothing), a long run could only be killed from outside, and in a thrash the progress trace went silent for minutes because it was tied to multiples of 500 pieces.

## What

- **Engine**: `GenerateAbort` thrown from the `trace` callback ends the attempt; `generate()` returns the partial board with `aborted: true`, no restart, and the leftover measured at the abort. The trace fires at least once a second as well as at every 500th piece. Closed boards are untouched: every recorded fingerprint still matches.
- **CLI**: a board that does not close is stored like a closed one, free cells drawn as holes (the lab's "show jammed cells" rendering); exit code stays 1. `CARVE_TIMEOUT_S=N` aborts after N seconds and stores what was carved; `--dry-run` reports `aborted`, `stuck`, `restarts`, `backtracks`. A budget that is not a number is refused with exit 2. Documented in `--help`.
- **Store**: meta gains the closing report (`restarts`, `backtracks`, `aborted`, `stuck`); a legacy JSON reads back with empty values. The lab sends the same report when it saves.
- **Docs**: both READMEs.

## Tests

134 (`deno task verify` clean). New: `abort.test.ts` (abort semantics, non-abort errors propagate, the once-a-second trace on a 100×100 thrash that used to give 0 traces in 2.7 s), store closing report and legacy fill, CLI abort in `--svg`, simple and `--dry-run` modes, help text. No setting inside the envelope jams cheaply, so the CLI fixture is a 400×400 board under a zero budget.

title: Docs: what a board looks like at 200x200, 500x500 and a million squares
description:
Every example in the README was 40 squares a side or smaller, so the stated
ceiling of 1000×1000 meant nothing to a reader. New section under Size.

## Three boards, one width

Three full boards side by side, all rendered to the same width on the page, so
the real story shows: past roughly two hundred squares a side the arrows stop
being individually visible and the board reads as fabric. That is worth seeing
rather than being told.

Measured with `--dry-run`, seed 7, default settings:

| Size | Arrows | Average length | Longest | Generation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200×200 | 3,619 | 11.1 | 213 | 0.2 s |
| 500×500 | 21,771 | 11.5 | 278 | 1.4 s |
| 1000×1000 | 85,809 | 11.7 | 354 | 9.6 s |

## A window into the fabric

Under them, a thirty-by-thirty window cut out of the million-square board,
rendered at the same zoom as the 30×30 comparison boards further down, so the
fabric resolves back into the same puzzle. It is a real crop of that board
(`rsvg-convert --zoom=9` with a 540×540 viewport), not a separate small board
standing in for one.

## What the numbers say and the pictures cannot

The average arrow barely grows with the board — 11.1 squares at 200×200
against 11.7 at 1000×1000 — so a bigger board buys you more arrows rather than
longer ones. The longest single arrow does grow: 213, 278, 354.

## On file sizes

These three ship as pictures only, unlike every other example, which also has
a downloadable drawing. Their drawings are 0.9 MB, 7 MB and 22 MB, which is
more than belongs in a repository, so the text says so and gives the one
command that produces them. `docs/images/` goes from 2.3 MB to 3.3 MB.

Both languages. No source changed.

title: Docs: dial reference as a list, plus examples at 200x200, 500x500 and 1000x1000
description:
Two follow-ups after looking at the merged README on GitHub.

## 1. Flag names were breaking in half

In the four-column dial tables, the longest flag of each group rendered split
across two lines: `--wshort` showed as an em-dash-looking `--` on one line and
`wshort` on the next.

Not a window-width problem — it reproduces at 1525px with room to spare. CSS
treats the hyphen as a line-break opportunity, and the table layout sizes the
`Option` column from the widest fragment *after* that break (`wshort`, six
characters). So the column is six characters wide, `--wmid` fits and
`--wshort` does not. One row per group is affected: the longest flag. In the
backbone group that would be `--giantspacepenalty`.

There is no clean way to forbid the break inside a Markdown table on GitHub:
`style` attributes are stripped by the sanitiser, and a non-breaking hyphen
would render correctly while silently breaking copy-paste — paste the flag
into a terminal, get an unknown-option error, no visible cause.

So each of the thirty-one dials is now a heading line with the flag, its range
and its default, followed by the description as its own paragraph:

```
**`--wshort`** — range 0–1, default 0.2

Share of short arrows. Higher means more arrows and more tips, but the board
turns into a mess of little hooks.
```

The flag starts a full-width line, so nothing pressures it to break. The six
groups stay collapsed and their counts still match the entries inside:
3, 3, 6, 4, 10, 5 = 31, verified in both files.

## 2. Nothing showed what a big board looks like

Every example was 40 squares a side or smaller, so the stated ceiling of
1000×1000 meant nothing to a reader. New section under Size:

- Three full boards side by side, all rendered to the same width. The honest
  result is that past roughly two hundred squares a side the arrows stop being
  individually visible and the board reads as fabric.
- Under them, a thirty-by-thirty window cut from the million-square board at
  the same zoom as the 30×30 comparison boards, so the fabric resolves back
  into the same puzzle.

Measured with `--dry-run`, seed 7:

| Size | Arrows | Average | Longest | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200×200 | 3,619 | 11.1 | 213 | 0.2 s |
| 500×500 | 21,771 | 11.5 | 278 | 1.4 s |
| 1000×1000 | 85,809 | 11.7 | 354 | 9.6 s |

The average arrow barely grows with the board, so size buys more arrows rather
than longer ones — a point the pictures cannot make on their own.

These three ship as pictures only; their drawings are 0.9 MB, 7 MB and 22 MB,
which is more than belongs in a repository, so the text gives the one command
that produces them. `docs/images/` goes from 2.3 MB to 3.3 MB.

Both languages throughout. No source changed.

title: Docs: a plain-language README for newcomers, in English and Polish
description:
The repository has no landing page. `prototype/README.md` is an engineering
log — 64 kB of measurements, dead ends and in-house vocabulary — and it is
unreadable to anyone meeting the project for the first time. This adds a
README aimed squarely at that person.

`README.md` is English and the default; `README.pl.md` is the Polish
translation, with a language switch at the top of each. The engineering log
stays exactly where it is.

## What is in it

**The puzzle before the tool.** What a board is, the single movement rule,
and what the generator guarantees. Three hand-drawn diagrams carry the rule,
including the case that trips everyone up: an arrow curled around another one
is still free to leave, because only the strip in front of its tip counts.

**Every parameter.** The eleven everyday flags with before-and-after
pictures, and all thirty-one advanced dials in tables grouped the way the
engine groups them — each with the visible effect of raising or lowering it,
and a warning where it can jam the generator. The tables are collapsed by
group so the section does not wall off the page.

**Building and running.** Installing Deno, cloning, the first board, the
standalone binary, every mode of the CLI with real output pasted in, exit
codes, the board store, the lab, environment variables, and a troubleshooting
list keyed by the actual error messages.

## Pictures

Twenty-seven examples under `docs/images/`, generated by the CLI itself and
shipped as PNG for viewing plus SVG for downloading. Comparison pairs are
colourised, because one colour per piece is precisely what the sliders
change. The three rule diagrams carry no text, so they serve both languages.

## Numbers

Everything quoted is measured, not estimated. Piece counts, averages and
timings come from `--dry-run` at 30x30 and 60x60 with seed 7; the dangerous
ranges come from the envelope table in `prototype/README.md`.

Five claims were wrong on the first pass and are fixed here: the count of
simple-mode flags (eleven, not ten), `--giantspan` being measured in the
longer side rather than the width (`engine.ts:815`), `--headtries` being
equivalent to the default from 8 rather than above it, the description of
which cross-knob rules span more than one dial, and a board file name copied
from the wrong size.

## Notes

- No source changed. `deno task verify` passes (124 tests); Markdown is
  excluded from `deno fmt` in `deno.json`.
- One gotcha worth knowing, found while writing this: the binary from
  `deno task compile` cannot save a board without `ARROWZ_BOARDS_DIR`,
  because the default store is derived from `import.meta.url`, which points
  into a virtual filesystem inside the binary. The README says so.

title: Rewrite the prototype in TypeScript on Deno
description:
Every prototype module is strict TypeScript on Deno 2.9; Node is gone. Boards are unchanged: nine fingerprints recorded on Node before the first edit are reproduced by the Deno CLI and frozen in fingerprints.test.ts.

- deno.json with tasks (test, verify, carve, bundle, lab, compile), strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess, lint forbidding any and non-null assertions
- types.ts: Params, Board, Piece, View, SimpleChoice, BoardMeta, worker messages
- engine.ts: types added, algorithm untouched; InvalidParamsError instead of a RangeError with a property
- store/lab-server/carve on Deno APIs; the canonical command is `deno task carve …`
- lab page script extracted to lab-page.ts and bundled with the worker into dist/
- docs updated; spec in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-deno-typescript-rewrite-design.md

title: Add JetBrains Context (jbcontext) integration for Claude Code
description:
## Summary

Adds the JetBrains Context (`jbcontext`) integration for Claude Code, installed with `jbcontext setup-agent --agent claude --auto --scope project` (CLI 0.9.11).

- `CLAUDE.md`: instruction block that makes the `context-explorer` subagent the first step of code discovery, with a single-shot semantic search policy.
- `.claude/agents/context-explorer.md`: Haiku subagent that runs up to three semantic searches and returns `file:line` references.
- `.claude/skills/context-search/SKILL.md`: semantic search skill.
- `.claude/settings.json`: SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks that refresh the index in the background.
- `.mcp.json`: registers `jbcontext mcp` as a stdio MCP server.

The index is remote (repository id `github.com/fronthub-pl/arrowz`); nothing index-related lives in the repository. Contributors without `jbcontext` installed are unaffected apart from the background hooks failing silently.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test 'prototype/*.test.mjs'` passes (112 tests)
- [x] `jbcontext search "incremental leftover absorption scanning only changed fragments"` returns `prototype/engine.mjs` `absorbLeftover`
- [ ] After merge, restart Claude Code and confirm the `jbcontext` MCP server and `context-explorer` subagent are available

title: Docs: the Chrome worker is not slower than Node; the 27 s was a backgrounded renderer
description:
Measured on main 7aaa86d, Chrome 152, Node 24, seed 7, defaults, fingerprints identical.

| board | Node | Chrome worker, tab in front | Chrome worker, another window in front |
|---|---|---|---|
| 500x500 | 1.5-1.65 s | 1.12 s | |
| 1000x1000 | 10.5 s | 7.6 s and 8.9 s (8.5 s with the progress trace) | 33.4 s and 34.5 s |

While backgrounded the renderer shows `pri 4` in `ps` (macOS background task policy) at 100% CPU; in front it shows `pri 47`. Cross-check: `taskpolicy -b node prototype/carve.mjs --width=500 --height=500 --dry-run` takes 5.47 s instead of 1.65 s. The page still reports `document.visibilityState === 'visible'`, so the app cannot detect the slow mode.

Docs only: README line 47 and the spec's two sentences about Insane timing; the stale "minutes" for layers and skeleton at Insane replaced with the round 12 numbers.

title: Engine: the leftover absorption scans only the fragments that changed
description:
## What

`Carver.absorbLeftover()` walked every cell of the board on every call and allocated a fresh `Uint8Array(W*H)` each time. On the slow corner of the simple view at 1000×1000 (`--length=0 --straight=0`, 173 228 pieces) it is called 6 560 times and was 29% of the generation time.

The scan now walks a bitmap of dirty cells: every cell that changed owner and its neighbours (`touch`), the neighbours of a rewritten piece after a successful absorption, and the fragments a scan discovered but did not get to before a hit. Every bit is set at construction, so the first scan and every restart see the whole board. Fragments are evaluated lazily in the order of their smallest cell index with the memo check kept verbatim, so the sequence of `absorbPath` calls, the memo writes and the boards are identical to the full walk.

## Bit-exactness

- `prototype/absorb.test.mjs`: the old method verbatim as the oracle; the same boards through both scans must give the same fingerprint, absorptions, backtracks and the same sequence of `absorbPath` calls (2 122 absorptions, 24 249 calls, 104 backtracks). A second test asserts the scan visits far fewer cells.
- Independent corpus of 574 boards (39 families, 20×20 to 500×500, knobs inside and outside the envelope, voids, restarts): every field identical between main and this branch; 1 500-seed sweep over 325 000 calls identical.
- 112 tests, 0 failures, ~19 s.

## Measured (seed 7, one process at a time)

| board | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| corner 1000×1000 | 34.6 s | 21.4 s (1.62×), fingerprint `9045118d` unchanged |
| corner 500×500 | 2.6–3.0 s | 2.5–2.7 s |
| defaults, layers, skeleton 1000×1000 | 10 / 20 / 10 s | within noise |

README round 13 has the full table, the mechanism and the remaining profile of the corner.

title: CLI: simple mode by default, the knobs behind --advanced
description:
## Summary
- The default `carve.mjs` call takes the simple lab view's inputs: `--width`, `--height` (required), `--length` and `--straight` in 0..1 (`--straight=1` = straightest), `--skeleton`, `--seed`, `--randomized`, `--colorized`, `--lineweight`, `--arrowwidth`, `--arrowheight`. Always one board into the store; `--svg=path` and `--dry-run` work as before. Any other flag is refused with exit 2 and a hint.
- `--advanced` keeps every engine knob, the report and the benchmark exactly as they were; `buildCommand` now emits it, so the lab's command and every saved board's `command` field run unchanged.
- The choice goes through `simpleParams` from `lab-simple.mjs`, the same function the lab uses; `exportCell` moved there so both render the same SVG. `--randomized` draws with `Math.random` like the lab.
- Board meta and the `--dry-run` line keep the full `--advanced` command in `command` (reproduces the board even after randomising) and the simple command as typed in `simpleCommand`.
- `--help` prints the simple flags; `--advanced --help` the knob table.
- README: simple-mode examples first, every advanced example prefixed with `--advanced`.

## Test plan
- [x] `node --test 'prototype/*.test.mjs'`: 110 pass (95 on main + 15 new: simple parser round trips, error lists, help variants, CLI simple mode byte for byte against `simpleParams`, `--randomized` inside the slider ranges, refusal of advanced flags, store `simpleCommand`, report/bench run to the end)
- [x] `node prototype/carve.mjs --advanced --only=easy --square --runs=1` and `--bench=1` by hand

title: Docs: closing measured at the slider ends
description: Random draws at the eight extreme slider combinations through `carve.mjs --dry-run --restarts=0`: 24/24 at 200×200, 400×400 and 500×500, 16/16 at 1000×1000, 0 backtracks, 0 timeouts. Slow corner: very short + most winding at 1000×1000, 24–51 s for 120–136 k pieces. README paragraph on the simple view records it. No code change.

title: Simple view: piece length and line shape as sliders
description:
Two sliders — piece length from very short to very long, line shape from the straightest lines to the most winding — replace the button rows in the simple view; the skeleton switch stays.

`lab-simple.mjs`: a slider has anchors at 0, ¼, ½, ¾ and 1, each giving every knob it controls a range with a canonical value; positions in between interpolate the ranges and snap them to the knob step. A position is a wish, not one configuration: randomising draws inside the ranges at that position, so the same sliders and the same seed give a different board each time. The default position reproduces the engine defaults exactly. `normalizeChoice` maps recipes saved by the button version (category names) onto the matching positions and repairs junk. Big boards keep the raised straightness floor on the winding half.

Tests: 94 pass (91 on main): validation at nine positions per slider and every size, random draws inside range / on step / envelope, monotone pull of the sliders, distinct draws at one position, legacy names, dictionary ends. Checked in Chrome. README updated.

title: Saved boards: command and view rows in the panel
description: The board's command moves to the left panel in the place of the lab command, and the stroke, arrowhead and colour rows of a stored board sit where the lab's rows are in the Preview section (`.libonly`, shown only in the saved-boards tab; `.labonly` hides the lab's). The list, Load into lab and Delete stay on the right. Element ids are unchanged, so the rebuild-and-save flow is untouched. Checked in Chrome: rows and command hidden in the lab tab, shown with a chosen board, recolouring still saves. 91 tests pass. README updated.

title: Arrowheads: arrow under 0.5, sharpened stick from 0.5, flat line ends, size knobs
description:
Redraws the arrowhead after the stroke sweep (0.2..0.9 on a 25×25 board) and the review of the screenshots.

- Under a stroke of 0.5: an arrow 0.4 of a cell + 0.9 of the line width wide, always 0.9 of a cell tall.
- From 0.5 up: a sharpened stick, exactly as wide as the line, 1.4 strokes tall (a wider head no longer fits between neighbours).
- Tip 0.48 past the head centre, so it stays inside the head cell; a bigger head grows backwards.
- Lines end flat (stroke-linecap butt); the tail is rounded by a circle of the line's radius; line and head overlap by 0.2 of the line width (line into the head, or a collar under the line when the head is as wide as the line), so no anti-aliasing seam shows at the base. Default ink set once per group.
- New view knobs, in cells: arrowhead width and height (0 = automatic) in the lab (lab tab and stored boards), in the CLI (`--headwidth=R`, `--headheight=R`), in the stored view and the URL. A head narrower than the line is widened to it.
- A 400×400 SVG grows from 3.2 to 3.8 MB for the tail circles.

Tests: 91 pass (89 on main). The arrowhead test covers every stroke from 0.2 to 0.9 (width and height rules, tip reach, overlap or collar, tail circle, flat ends); a second test covers the knobs; the command round trip includes the new flags. README drawing parameters updated.

title: Arrowhead scales with the stroke; the line ends under the head
description: A fixed head was swallowed by the round line cap from a stroke of 0.5 up (checked at 0.2..0.9 in 0.05 steps on a 25×25 board: legible to 0.45, gone from 0.55). The head is now 0.24 of a cell wider than its line, at most 0.05 short of a line in the next cell, at least 0.9 times as tall as wide, tip still 0.48 past the head centre (a bigger head grows backwards). The line stops half its width short of the base, so its round cap ends exactly under the head. Highlighted pieces get a head sized for their thicker line. The test covers every stroke from 0.2 to 0.9; 89 tests pass. README drawing parameters updated.

title: Arrowhead tip stays inside the head cell
description: The tip reached 0.62 of a cell past the head centre, into the next cell: the arrow looked like it overshot its point, and two heads facing each other in neighbouring cells overlapped. Now tip 0.48, base 0.1 behind the centre and 0.56 wide (height 0.58). Test pins the reach at 0.5 of a cell at most. 89 tests pass. README drawing parameters updated.

title: Ignore .claude/worktrees/
description: Session worktrees are created under .claude/worktrees/ inside the checkout, so the main checkout showed the directory as untracked. Ignore it.

title: Lab: simple view with safe random settings, narrow arrowheads, saved-boards fixes
description:
## What

Four lab changes, one store fix, one engine drawing fix.

1. **Simple / advanced view.** The panel gets a switch (remembered in `localStorage`, simple is the default). The simple view offers a board size (the preset sizes), piece length (long / medium / short), line shape (straight / slightly winding / winding), skeleton (with / without), the seed and a **randomise on every generate** checkbox. `lab-simple.mjs` maps a choice to a full parameter set: canonical values by default, or knobs drawn inside ranges narrower than the engine envelope when randomising. The default choice reproduces the engine defaults exactly. Drawn values go through the knobs, so the command, the URL and the advanced view show what was generated. The advanced view is unchanged.
2. **Arrowheads** are narrow isosceles triangles now (base 0.54 of a cell at height 0.62, was 0.84): heads of two pieces meeting at a right angle in neighbouring cells no longer touch.
3. **Saved boards:** entering the tab or picking a size shows the first board of that size right away.
4. **Recolouring or changing the stroke of a saved board keeps its place in the list.** The store keeps the original `createdAt` on an overwrite (same id) and records `updatedAt`.

## Random ranges

From the analysis notes: straightness ≥ 0.65 (≥ 0.7 above 600 cells a side), coiling penalty ≤ 6 with low straightness, no dense skeleton (`wGiant` ≤ 0.1, step ≥ 6, span ≤ 40), no layers mode at 1000×1000, closing knobs at their defaults. Measured with the canonical CLI (`carve.mjs --dry-run --restarts=0`), every one of the 18 choice combinations twice per size:

| size | draws | closed | backtracks | median | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200×200 | 36 | 36 | 0 | 0.31 s | 0.43 s |
| 400×400 | 36 | 36 | 0 | 1.41 s | 2.73 s |

## Tests

`node --test 'prototype/*.test.mjs'`: 89 pass (81 on main). New: `lab-simple.test.mjs` (7: sizes, defaults, validation of every choice at every size, 25 random draws per combination and size inside range / on step / inside the envelope with untouched closing knobs, category direction, big-board floors, both dictionaries), the arrowhead shape test in `engine.test.mjs`, the overwrite test in `store.test.mjs` now asserts the opposite of before (the board stays in place).

Checked in Chrome: simple view in PL and EN, randomising gives different commands per click, drawn values visible in the advanced view, first board opens on tab entry and on size click, a recoloured board stays at its position.

title: Docs: the probe knob and the leftover test described as they really behave
description:
## What

- **`probe` and `probeLen` help texts (EN in `PARAM_SPEC`, PL in `lab-i18n.mjs`).** The old text said "little visible effect"; the round 12 measurements showed `probe` 1 with length 12 gives an all-short board (maxLen 19–26, 33 k pieces instead of 21.8 k at 500×500) and `probeLen` 2 triples the piece count. A probe is a piece whose target length is drawn around `probeLen` (give or take half) instead of the length mix; the texts say that now. The label no longer calls the probes "inward". Both texts are under the 170-character limit.
- **Spec §7, item 2 (leftover-fragment test).** Replaced the early approximation ("no cell without a free neighbour, no plus-shaped fragment up to 5 cells") with what the prototype does: the local-defect test in radius 2, capped flood fills with the exact bitmask test up to `strandLimit`, the failed-fragment rule, the shared visited marks that make later fills test walled-off pockets (preserved bit for bit by the round 12 fix), and the shortening in jumps with an incremental creep.

No behaviour change; 81 tests.

title: Engine: exact incremental creep in the shortening loop, envelope measured at 500 and 600
description:
## What

The path-shortening loop of the leftover test cost Θ(L²/32) per trimmed path: after the jump phase found a passing prefix, the creep re-ran the whole `wouldStrand` on every longer prefix. With a dense late skeleton (`wGiant` ≥ 0.13, `giantStep` ≤ 7, `giantSpan` ≥ 100) a 600×600 board spent 96 % of its CPU there and took 50–350 s instead of 5–25 s.

- **Engine:** the block becomes `Carver.shortenPath`; the jump phase is unchanged, the creep (`creepUp`) re-examines only what taking one more cell can change: the local-defect predicate on the vertices the full check would visit near the new cell, and a lazy ordered replay of the flood-fill probes (the oversize-fragment rule inspects order-dependent DFS windows, so "adjacent fragments only" is not exact). If the replay ever disagreed with `wouldStrand` it falls back to the plain creep.
- **Tests:** `shortening.test.mjs` keeps a verbatim reference of the original loop and checks every call against it on 64 boards (1716 trims, 2605 refusals, pinned totals), plus twelve boards with trimming pinned from `main`. 81 tests.
- **Docs:** README round 12 with the 500×500 / 600×600 envelope measurement and the loop fix; spec and slice 2 updated.

## Boards are bit-identical

| check | boards | identical |
|---|---|---|
| engine's own differential (calls compared) | 642 boards, 140 111 calls | 642 / 0 mismatches |
| independent review corpus (old vs new engine) | 575 | 575 |
| before/after measurement 500–800 | 44 | 44 |

## Before / after (quiet machine, one process)

| board | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| random set 29 at 600×600 seed 29 (reference) | 106.3 s | 4.8 s |
| set 29, seeds 1029 / 2029 | 39.3 / 11.4 s | 4.6 / 5.2 s |
| set 10 at 600×600 | 24.5 s | 3.0 s |
| `wGiant` 0.2, `giantStep` 2, `giantSpan` 150 grid at 600 | 16.0 s | 6.7 s |
| `giants` 4, `giantStep` 2, `giantSpan` 198, `probe` 0.93 at 800 | 12.4 s | 7.9 s |
| defaults at 600×600 | 2.17 s | 2.15 s |

Profile of the reference board: `wouldStrand` and friends from 102 s to 3.6 s; the remaining time is the unchanged jump phase, the incremental creep is 6 % of `shortenPath`.

## Envelope at 500×500 and 600×600 (measured, documented, not changed here)

About 1 300 boards without restarts: the envelope holds for closing everywhere except `pStraight` 0.6 at 600×600 (alone 11/15; with `warns` 2 0/5 at both sizes; with `anticoil` 10 5/10 at 500 and 0/5 at 600). A coupling rule is a separate decision.

title: Tests: head-scan jam tests bypass the safe envelope
description: PR #2 and PR #4 merged independently and their combination leaves three engine tests red on main: the head-scan tests starve the search with `headTries 1`, `pStraight 0.2` and `absorbLimit 0`, which `generate()` now refuses. They pass `{ unchecked: true }` like the other engine-internal jam tests. 79 tests pass.

title: Generator and lab: refuse settings outside the measured safe envelope
description:
## Why

Five parallel measurements (about 8 100 runs without restarts, boards up to 400x400) plus a code-level analysis showed that boards fail to close only outside a bounded region of knob values, and that the failure is a set of free islands that all have legal heads but nothing carvable from them, waiting on each other in a cycle. Details in README round 11.

## What

- **Engine**: PARAM_SPEC narrowed to the envelope (pStraight >= 0.6, warns >= 2, anticoil <= 10, absorbLimit >= 12, strandLimit >= 10, headTries 2..16, maxBack <= 1000, restarts <= 5, wGiant <= 0.2, giantStraight >= 0.3, giantSpacing <= 3); three cross rules (short + medium <= 0.9, Lmax 0 or >= 6, mix -1 or 0.3..0.7); `validateParams()`, `formatViolation()`; `generate()` throws a RangeError with the violations before carving. `giantStraight`/`giantWarns` are no longer marked inactive at serpentine step > 0 (they act on every skeleton). Help texts rewritten to say where a knob breaks.
- **CLI**: validation in every mode, exit code 2 (JSON line for `--dry-run`, stderr otherwise), new `--help` with the full knob table and rules.
- **Lab**: loaded values pulled into range with a notice, violations listed in red, Generate blocked, stored boards outside the envelope can be viewed but not rebuilt. Polish and English texts.
- **Docs and tests**: README round 11, spec and plan slices carry the envelope; `envelope.test.mjs` pins the contract values and a board fingerprint from main.

Recorded board fingerprints are unchanged: the algorithm is untouched. 76 tests pass.

## Not covered

The envelope was not re-validated at 1000x1000. Boards in a local store made before this change may fall outside it.

title: Engine: strict leftover test as the rescue after a jam
description:
## Why

The eight 1000×1000 boards of the random sweep that jam with hundreds of legal heads are geometric jams, not starved searches. Diagnosed island by island at the first jam (no undo):

| board | free cells | islands | islands with no legal head | with heads, none carvable | largest island |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 (early shred) | 363 404 | 4 512 | **4 300** (all 60 above 1 000 cells) | 212 | 5 457, no head |
| 62 (end game) | 10 417 | 1 545 | 1 042 | 503 (400 of them 1–3 cells) | 168 |

A headless island (every ray crosses another island) is born at a cut and cannot be repaired by undoing: assigning cells only clears rays, so an island loses its last head only through a cut into it — exactly a `wouldStrand` call. An island with heads but nothing carvable is the L-tromino with the head in the corner: decomposable, not carvable.

## What

`wouldStrand` gets a **strict mode** with two more tests:

- **own head** — every fragment next to the path must keep a cell that is a legal head, whatever its size (walk towards the exit edge first, budget 256 cells, then assumed fine);
- **solvable** instead of decomposable for fragments of up to 30 cells — search over subsets: legal head of what is left, piece inside the fragment, repeat; memo of losing subsets, budget 4 000 nodes.

`generate()` runs the first attempt lenient and the restarts strict. New knob `strict` (0 never, 1 on restarts = default, 2 always), bilingual in the lab.

## Measured (copies of the engine, one attempt, no restarts, undo budget 200)

| leftover test | 200×200 `headTries` 1 seeds 1/3 | board 62 | board 30 | pieces on boards that close today | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | jam / jam | jam at 126 s | jam at 54 s | — | — |
| line front (some line through the fragment has a head at its front) | closes / closes | jam, worse | jam | ±5% | ±10% |
| own head | closes / closes | closes, 297 s | jam | +19–25% | 1.5–3.5× |
| **own head + solvable** | closes / closes | **closes, 92 s, 0 undos** | **closes, 429 s, 0 undos** | +17–35% | 4–7× |

The line-front test is refuted (not kept up by cuts elsewhere). The cost of the strict test is intrinsic — pockets shaded by a neighbour that has a head are refused although that neighbour would be carved first — so it is the rescue, not the default: **every board that closed before is bit-identical** (recorded layers fingerprints and the default 1000×1000 `32c62121` unchanged).

All eight jammed boards of the sweep close in one strict attempt, 0 undos: 19 (230 s), 27 (183 s), 30 (429 s), 44 (813 s), 62 (92 s), 79 (235 s), 92 (72 s), 94 (653 s). End to end through the CLI with the default knobs (`--dry-run --maxback=0 --restarts=1`): board 62 closes after the lenient attempt jams and the strict restart carves it, 319 s in all; board 92 in 262 s. Details in `prototype/README.md`, round 10.

## Tests

47 tests (`node --test 'prototype/*.test.mjs'`): the L-corner fragment is decomposable and not solvable; a shaded domino is stranded only in strict mode; the two starved 200×200 seeds close in one strict attempt; the first attempt is lenient and a restart is strict, with the 100×100 seed 3 fingerprint unchanged.

Independent of PR #2 (head scan): both touch `run()`/`wouldStrand`, expect a small conflict when the second one merges.

title: Engine: scan every legal head before the first backtrack
description:
## What

`run()` now scans every legal head of every pool once (`carveOne(true)`) after `absorbLeftover` fails and before the first `undoToFrontier`. Boards that never needed an undo are untouched: the layers fingerprints still match cell for cell.

Two bounds keep the scan from paying for jams it cannot fix:

- three misses in a row switch it off until it hits again;
- one attempt gets at most as many scans as undos (`maxBack`, default 200).

`stats.headScans` / `stats.headScanHits` count the scans for measurements.

## Why

The random 1000×1000 sweep left eight boards jammed with 208–688 legal heads on the board, which read like a starved search: `carveOne` draws only `headTries` heads per pool, and a backtrack undoes the newest neighbour of the leftover, so it never puts the missed heads back in play.

## What it fixes

Genuine starvation. 200×200 with `headTries 1` and `pStraight 0.2` (restarts 0, maxBack 50) jammed on seeds 3, 4 and 6 with 39–133 legal heads left; all six seeds close with `headTries 32`. With the scan those three close with zero undos (regression test).

## What it does not fix, measured

The eight jammed 1000×1000 boards (19, 27, 30, 44, 62, 79, 92, 94, default budget) still jam in the same state (board 44: 336 889 cells / 285 heads vs 336 472 / 286 before). Stopping board 30 at its first jam and classifying the heads: 253 legal heads, all 253 fail the leftover test on the minimal two-cell piece, 0 carvable; board 62: 667 / 667 / 0. About a quarter of the free islands have 1–3 cells and no legal head at all, because their rays cross other free islands. `stuck.heads > 0` is therefore not evidence of starvation; these boards are shredded, and the next candidate is a reachability check in `wouldStrand` (reject a cut that leaves a small fragment with no cell that can ever become a legal head).

## Cost

One attempt of board 94 (restarts 0, maxBack 200):

| engine | time | scans / hits |
|---|---|---|
| main | 25.1 s | 0 |
| scan, no bounds | 62.0 s | 1 268 / 1 067 |
| scan with both bounds | 31.7 s | 200 / 166 |

Full verdicts (4 attempts) with the scan unbounded took 1.3–3.7× longer than before; the bounds bring one attempt back to +26 % on a shredded board and to zero on boards that close without an undo.

## Tests

`node --test 'prototype/*.test.mjs'`: 46 passing. Three new tests: starved 200×200 seeds close with zero undos; a void board with no carvable heads gets at most three scans; a void board with the odd carvable head gets at most `maxBack` scans.

title: Engine: report the legal heads left at the best moment of a jam
description:
## Summary

- `generate()` returns `stuck.heads` next to `remaining` and `sizes`: the number of legal heads the carver had when the leftover was smallest (already measured as `Carver.stuckHeads`, so far only printed by the report mode).
- Zero means the geometry closed the board; more means the search gave up on heads that existed. The dry-run JSON line and the lab worker pass the object through; the CLI failure message names the count as well.

## Why

Re-running the 27 thrashing boards of the random 1000×1000 sweep with the default closing budget showed that every real jam still had 208–688 legal heads out of 4 000 possible, i.e. the jams are search starvation, not geometry. This field is what makes that classification possible from a dry run.

## Test

A 12×12 board with half its cells voided jams at once and the field matches the carver's count. Suite: 43/43 (`node --test 'prototype/*.test.mjs'`).
